title: Water Resources Engineering Intern
description:
Job Description

Dewberry is currently seeking Water Resources Engineering Interns for Summer 2027 to join our Atlanta, GA office. This is an excellent career opportunity for an enthusiastic and talented individual to join a team of outstanding professionals. This position offers tremendous potential for professional growth in a great working environment and the opportunity to apply the latest technology to help our clients solve their most challenging problems.

Dewberry is a leading, market-facing professional services firm with more than 60 locations and 2,500 professionals nationwide. What sets us apart from our competitors is our people. At Dewberry, we seek out exceptional talent and strive to deliver the highest quality of services to our clients. Whether you’re an experienced professional or a new graduate, you’ll have the chance to collaborate with the best and brightest and work on innovative and complex projects at the forefront of the industry. Our commitment to excellence stems from our personal integrity and from other defining attributes, which we call “Dewberry at Work,” that have inspired our employees to be successful for more than a half-century.

Responsibilities

Typical projects involve hydrology, hydraulics, stormwater master plans, mitigation planning, surface water assessment, stormwater quality, and asset management in order to assist federal, state and local clients in Georgia.

Required Skills & Required Experience

  • Currently pursuing B.S. Degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related engineering field required (emphasis in water resources preferred)

  • Experience using ArcGIS and AutoCAD a plus
  • Knowledge of hydrology and open channel hydraulics preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in basic MS Office software

Don’t meet every single requirement? At Dewberry we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace for our employees. So, if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the position description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or other opportunities.

*At this time, Dewberry will not sponsor a new applicant for work authorization.

*Dewberry is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or sexual orientation.

*Only recipients of an offer of employment from Dewberry, will be required to submit to a background screening which may include, but is not limited to, employment verification, educational and other credential verification, driving record check, criminal background check, and an investigative consumer report. These screenings will be conducted by Dewberry’s background vendor of choice and will be conducted in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local law.

Program Information

Summer Intern Program

During the summer intern program, interns gain hands-on project experience, develop technical skills, and put their classroom knowledge into action. Our interns are assigned meaningful work and are given the opportunity to work on projects similar to what they would be engaging with as a full-time employee.

Our interns get the opportunity to participate in a series of workshops and events, including:

  • Networking opportunities to meet other interns, staff, and senior leaders across the business.
  • Learning about our services, projects, and clients.
  • Professional development workshops, including a career planning workshop and a DiSC assessment to learn more about themselves and how to work effectively with others.
  • Summer-long group project where interns work alongside firm leaders to address issues that will impact our future strategy.

title: Correctional LMHP - On-Site - F/T or P/T
description:
Correctional LMHP - On-Site


MindCare Solutions is a leader in delivering comprehensive mental health services across a variety of settings. As a clinician-owned and operated organization, we are committed to high-quality care and strong provider support. We are seeking Licensed Mental Health Providers (LCSW, LPC, LMHP) who are interested in partnering with a growing organization that values collaboration and a strong team-oriented culture, working within a correctional setting.


Schedule: Part-Time or Full-Time, dayshift

Locaation: Hudson, CO

Compensation: negotiable


Position Summary:

  • Conduct comprehensive mental health assessments, including intake screenings, risk evaluations, and diagnostic evaluations for incarcerated individuals.
  • Develop, implement, and regularly update individualized treatment plans in collaboration with the interdisciplinary care team.
  • Provide individual and group therapy services, utilizing evidence-based therapeutic interventions.
  • Monitor patient progress and response to treatment, adjusting interventions as clinically appropriate.
  • Perform crisis intervention, including suicide risk assessments, safety planning, and emergency response.
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and compliant clinical documentation in accordance with facility, state, and federal guidelines.
  • Collaborate with medical staff, correctional officers, and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated and safe patient care.

  • Provide psychoeducation to patients regarding mental health conditions, coping strategies, and medication adherence (as applicable).
  • Support continuity of care by coordinating with community providers upon release.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and adhere to safety protocols within the correctional environment.

Qualifications:

  • Active, unrestricted license as a Licensed Mental Health Provider (LCSW, LPC, LMHP) in the CO.
  • Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Psychology, or a related behavioral health field.
  • Minimum of [1–2] years of clinical experience (correctional, forensic, or inpatient experience preferred).
  • Experience conducting assessments, diagnoses, and treatment planning.
  • Knowledge of crisis intervention and risk assessment, including suicide prevention.
  • Strong documentation skills and familiarity with electronic health records (EHR).
  • Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team in a secure environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to pass required background checks and meet all facility credentialing requirements.

Benefits:

  • Clinician-first mentality
  • Mileage Reimbursement
  • Competitive Salary
  • Malpractice Coverage
  • Full Health & Wellness Benefits
  • HSA/FSA
  • 401k with 4% match
  • Disability
  • Life/ Ad&D
  • Positive/Motivated Culture
  • Company-Paid Holidays
  • Flextime
  • PTO

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Stow, Ohio.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Stow area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Stow requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: C4ISR Analyst
description:
Summary: Bridge Defense seeks highly qualified C4ISR Analyst role at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling producing all-source intelligence on foreign military command, control, communications, computers (C4), and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to ICD 203 standards. Requires TS/SCI with CI Poly and experience authoring DoD product lines for senior policymakers.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Conduct all-source intelligence research to assess foreign C4ISR capabilities, limitations, and vulnerabilities.
  • Analyze foreign military exercises and operations to identify tactics, techniques, procedures (TTPs), doctrine, readiness, integration, and compatibility issues.
  • Evaluate military C4ISR assets (sensors, networks, nodes, targeting, survivability, denial/deception tactics).
  • Support technical targeting, network link analysis, and functional requirements for defense stakeholders.
  • Produce complex written products and briefings tailored to senior policymakers or defense leaders
  • Experience authoring DoD product lines and utilizing ICD 203 tradecraft standards.
  • 3+ years of experience in technical targeting, network link analysis, and functional requirements.
  • HS diploma/GED with 7+ years in intelligence or cybersecurity, or Bachelor’s degree with 3+ years in intelligence or cybersecurity.

Additional Qualifications / Nice to have:

  • Experience working in a Joint Staff environment
  • Experience briefing senior defense clients
  • Experience in computer engineering or network development.
  • Knowledge of cyberspace strategy, policy, and concepts.
  • Familiarity with the Intelligence Community (IC) and Combatant Command environment.
  • Knowledge of the INDOPACOM AOR.

General Factors:

  • Depending on project requirements, may be required to work within a compressed schedule; more than 40-hour work weeks should be expected when schedules demand it.
  • Willing to travel, if needed.
  • No Relocation.
  • Must be able to sit/stand at a desk for long-periods and must be able to lift 20 pounds occasionally.
  • Must be able to multi-task and rapidly change priorities with limited notice.


Clearance: TS/SCI with current CI Poly (adjudicated within the past 5 years)

Location: Joint Base Anacosia Bolling; On-site

Salary Range: 82K - 89K


Online applications, please.

When we review candidates' information, we are looking for the best matches for the position based on the qualifications listed in the job posting. If your skills and experience appear to match an open position, a recruitment services professional or a hiring manager may contact you.


Bridge Defense is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of the company to provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity or expression, national origin or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. If you are a qualified disabled veteran or individual with a disability and need reasonable accommodation to use or access our online system, please contact us at 202-436-9222.

title: Activities Assistant
description:
-

A US News & World Report Best!

Belair Nursing & Rehabilitation is a proud affiliate of National Health Care Associates. As a Certified Great Place to Work and US News & World Report Best for Short-Term Rehab and Long-Term Care, we think that you are going to love it here. Your work will be meaningful to you. You will make a genuine difference in the lives of our aging guests and the families that love them. You will enjoy lasting bonds with the families you meet and with the teams you work on. And if you desire, you will experience real career growth where your expertise and dedication is valued and appreciated. We invite you to join our team!

-

* Part-time; 3 days per week

  • Engage residents in arts and crafts, games, music, and other recreational programs
  • Collaborate with the Activities Director to develop and implement a monthly activities calendar
  • Provide one-on-one support for residents who may need additional assistance
  • Foster a sense of community and social interaction among residents
  • Document and maintain records of residents' participation in activities

If you are passionate about creating positive and engaging experiences for seniors and have the creativity to organize a variety of activities, we invite you to join our team. Make a real difference in people's lives in an environment where compassion, care and expertise come together!

-

What We Offer

As an affiliate of National Health Care, our Belair team enjoys:

  • Competitive compensation and benefits package
  • Comprehensive training and mentorship
  • Opportunities for professional growth and development
  • Supportive and collaborative work environment
  • The chance to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents

Rate of Pay

Starting from USD $24.65/Hr.

-

title: Director, Engineering Operations
description:
The Role

As Director, Engineering Operations, you will build and run the operating system that helps

Product and Engineering translate strategy into measurable business and customer impact. You

will create clarity across outcomes, priorities, capacity, delivery health, risks, and decisions, then

turn that clarity into concise executive communication and disciplined organizational action. This

high-leverage leadership role partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Operations,

Finance, Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Security, and other business functions. You will play

a critical role in ensuring all functions are aligned and understand the expected outcomes.


Responsibilities

Executive Communication Impact

● Create a clear, executive-ready narrative connecting Product, Engineering, and Data

investments, delivery, and operational performance to customer and business outcomes

● Own recurring executive updates, company communications, and board-level inputs,

supported by a reliable source of truth for commitments, outcomes, and delivery health

● Surface material changes, trade-offs, risks, and decisions early, with concise context and

clear recommendations


Outcome & KPI Definition

● Translate company and product strategy into measurable outcomes, objectives, key

results, and operating KPIs with clear owners, baselines, targets, data sources, and

review cadences

● Develop a balanced view of customer and business impact, delivery effectiveness,

quality, reliability, security, efficiency, and organizational health

● Partner with Data, Finance, Product, and Engineering to improve instrumentation and

use KPI trends to guide decisions and evaluate results


Portfolio & Planning Cadence

● Design and operate annual, quarterly, and ongoing portfolio-planning cadences across

Product and Engineering

● Maintain a current portfolio view connecting strategic outcomes, initiatives, ownership,

dependencies, milestones, capacity, and risk

● Facilitate prioritization and sequencing decisions so assumptions, trade-offs, decision

rights, and changes are explicit


SDLC Process & Operating Reviews

● Define and continuously improve a lightweight, consistent software delivery lifecycle

from discovery through release, adoption, measurement, and learning

● Establish operating reviews focused on outcomes, delivery confidence, quality, reliability,

customer impact, constraints, risks, and decisions

● Use operating data, retrospectives, automation, and appropriately governed AI-enabled

practices to remove friction and improve delivery without adding unnecessary process


Resource & Capacity Planning

● Build a practical capacity model connecting portfolio demand with available teams,

critical skills, hiring plans, external partners, and operational obligations

● Partner with Finance, Product, and Engineering leaders on headcount planning,

allocation trade-offs, capability gaps, and investment choices

● Model alternative portfolio and staffing scenarios and compare planned versus actual

capacity to improve future decisions without creating false precision


Cross-Functional Risk & Decision Tracking

● Establish a clear system for identifying, owning, escalating, and resolving cross-

functional risks, dependencies, and decisions

● Facilitate difficult discussions where business goals, customer needs, technical

constraints, security, compliance, cost, or timing compete

● Close the loop by documenting decisions, updating plans, confirming accountable

owners, and addressing recurring root causes


Organizational Leadership & Collaboration

● Serve as a trusted operating partner to the CTO, Engineering leadership, Product

leadership, and the Engineering Leadership Team

● Strengthen cross-functional relationships, ownership, and accountability through

structured thinking, sound judgment, influence, and consistent follow-through


Qualifications & Experience

● Leadership experience in Engineering Operations, Product Operations, Technical

Program Management, Business Operations, a technical Chief of Staff role, or a

comparable function within a SaaS or product-led technology company

● Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated success connecting

Product and Engineering work to customer and business impact

● Experience defining outcomes, OKRs, KPIs, scorecards, portfolio-planning processes,

and operating-review cadences across multiple teams

● Working knowledge of modern product development and software delivery lifecycles,

including platform, reliability, security, and technical investment trade-offs

● Experience with resource, headcount, budget, and capacity planning in partnership with

Finance and functional leaders

● Strong analytical judgment and the ability to build trustworthy reporting from product,

engineering, financial, and customer data

● Proven ability to facilitate difficult cross-functional decisions, manage material risks and

dependencies, and bring structure to ambiguity

● Pragmatic experience using AI-assisted tools to improve synthesis, planning, and

analysis while verifying outputs and protecting sensitive information


What Great Looks Like

A Director, Engineering Operations who is thriving in this role demonstrates:

● Executive clarity - Product and Engineering impact, trade-offs, risks, and decisions are

understood without leaders reconstructing the story themselves

● Outcome accountability - initiatives begin with clear intended outcomes and are

evaluated using credible evidence after delivery

● A predictable, adaptable portfolio - commitments are realistic, priorities are explicit,

and changes are deliberate and well communicated

● A stronger operating system - coordination costs decline, risks surface earlier, data

becomes more trustworthy, and accountability becomes clearer over time


"Someone who makes Product and Engineering easier to understand, easier to lead, and more

effective at turning strategy into measurable results."


Interview Process

The process includes a conversation with the hiring manager; role-specific rounds covering

executive communication, outcome and KPI definition, portfolio and operating-system design,

capacity planning, and cross-functional leadership judgment - including how you use and verify

AI-assisted tools - and a company values conversation with People Ops. Your recruiter will

share the exact sequence when you advance.

What You'll Receive:

  • A competitive compensation package
  • Employer-sponsored 401(k) with match
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible time off and hybrid / remote work environment
  • The anticipated annual salary range for this role is $200,000 - $230,000. Actual compensation and title will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skills.

description:

  • Flexible can-do attitude, willing to help out with all types of tasks in an ever-changing environment

  • Express ideas and otherwise communicate with the spoken word

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in West Palm Beach, Florida.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the West Palm Beach area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near West Palm Beach requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Director of Development and Alumni Relations
description:
Overview of Woodland School

Located just west of Stanford University, Woodland School is an independent day school that offers a joyful approach to learning in a diverse, respectful, and inclusive environment for approximately 300 students in early childhood through eighth grade. Woodland is a small school with a big heart.

Woodland School specializes in education that inspires students by nurturing each individual’s voice, intellect, and character. With an emphasis on inquiry-based and student-centered learning, children are empowered and encouraged to be active and engaged learners. Our students’ innate sense of wonder is the foundation of learning at Woodland School.

Woodland School’s faculty create a school environment that is as supportive and nurturing as it is challenging, and they embody the core values of the school—integrity, curiosity, resilience, equity, respect, and stewardship. The teachers are themselves learners, constantly searching for ways to improve their practice. A robust professional development program supports the faculty by connecting them to the best practices in pedagogy, curriculum development, educational technology, and student assessment.

Woodland School is seeking a highly motivated Director of Development and Alumni Relations. The Director will join the school as Woodland begins a new chapter in its 45 year history and will have an opportunity to create and implement various strategic initiatives for the school.

Position Overview

The Director of Development and Alumni Relations reports to the Head of School and collaborates with the entire leadership team including the Director of Finance, Director of Communications, and the Director of Admissions. The Director of Development and Alumni Relations is responsible for recurring fundraising campaigns including the Annual Fund, gala, major gifts, special events, grants, and communication. The Director works in close collaboration with the Campaign Director, a fixed-term role overseeing a four-year campaign to form an inaugural endowment for Woodland. In addition, the Director plans and executes the vision and strategy of Woodland School related to alumni engagement to enhance loyalty, dedication, and support for the School. The job is accomplished through the individual’s own direct efforts as well as effectively leveraging the skills and volunteer contributions of Woodland parents and alumni, Board of Trustees, and staff.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reports directly to the Head of School, is a member of the Leadership Team, and participates on the Board of Trustees’ Advancement Committee
  • Collaboratively designs, implements, and oversees a comprehensive fundraising program designed to secure significant financial resources from trustees, parents, alumni, foundations and others to support Woodland School’s mission and strategic priorities
  • Oversees all recurring fundraising efforts and programs, including Annual Fund, special fundraising events, major donor programs, grants, capital campaigns, planned giving, donor prospecting and research, and office administration to meet or exceed annual development plan income goals
  • Leads and coordinates the efforts in the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donors
  • Guides and supports the Head of School in fundraising activities
  • Presents to the Board of Trustees and Head of School an annual development plan for achieving specific goals
  • Oversees all aspects of the grant-writing program
  • Attends and participates in a variety of fundraising, stewardship, community-building, and other campus events throughout the year in order to stay informed and updated on school activities
  • Collaborates with the Board of Trustees to reach fundraising goals, to engage the Board in fundraising activities, and to identify new individual and corporate funding prospects.
  • Supervises the Advancement Associate, a shared resource who works to support the Director of Development and Alumni Relations, the Director of Communications, and the Director of Admissions.

Leadership and Management Experience

  • A charismatic leader whose approach to development creates enthusiasm for Woodland School from all constituents
  • Strong management experience, including the ability to foster an environment of creativity, collaboration, and professional growth in a convivial work atmosphere
  • Ability to manage and lead professional and volunteer staff, including recruiting, training and professional development. Establishes clear directions and sets goals, objectives, and benchmarks.
  • Ability to communicate a compelling and inspired vision and sense of core purpose
  • Proven ability to think strategically, creating plans that reflect best practice but also create fresh approaches. Comfortable making strategic decisions based on analysis, wisdom, experiences, and judgment
  • Ability to design, implement, and direct multiple projects

Fundraising Experience

  • Proven success in asking for, closing, and coaching others on fundraising for annual needs and strategic campaigns, as well as building and maintaining long-term relationships with major individual donors, foundations, and corporations in an independent school environment
  • Knowledge of current and evolving trends in advancement and effective independent school fundraising practices
  • Ability to identify, develop, and maintain relationships with current and prospective major donors, foundations, organizations, alumni and corporate funders
  • Broad financial responsibility includes setting fundraising objectives, evaluating results, and developing corrective strategies as needed

Communication and Interpersonal Skills

  • High emotional intelligence, with the ability to create excitement about Woodland School’s goals, developing constructive and long-lasting relationships with all constituents
  • Strong interpersonal, organizational, networking, facilitation and management skills; works both independently and within a team-oriented structure
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking, negotiations and effective communication with diverse audiences
  • Ability to convey Woodland’s mission to diverse groups, including major donors, board members, and others critical to Woodland’s advancement
  • Strong computer skills, including experience using Google Suite, and relationship database programs (eTapestry)
  • Engages alumni in the life of the School through consistent and positive communication using electronic, print, and social media
  • Innovative and entrepreneurial approach, including solutions to complex issues. Exercises good judgment and decision making. Has the ability to work well under pressure and the ability to reason, think creatively, and solve problems
  • Appreciation for and desire to participate fully in the dynamic life of an elementary school community

Professional Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required (Master’s degree preferred)
  • Proven track record of raising funds from individuals and foundations, with impressive results
  • Minimum of 3 years of Development experience, preferably in an independent educational institution
  • Prior experience with major gifts as well as foundation and corporate grant writing is preferred
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented and able to manage multiple projects simultaneously and adapt to changing environments and priorities
  • A self-starter with the ability to work productively and meet benchmarks and goals timely and without day-to-day supervision
  • Excellent understanding of principles and techniques of Development activities, including annual giving, major giving, planned giving, event planning, capital campaigns, marketing and communications, grant procurement, and alumni relations
  • Excellent planning skills - organized, communicates, follows through, and evaluates
  • Requires some work in evenings and weekends as well as travel. Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Position requires absolute confidentiality and professionalism in appearance, attitude and presentation

Compensations and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $160,000-$180,000, depending on qualifications and experience. The compensation package will be competitive and commensurate with experience, degree attainment and the local independent school market.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The position can be physically demanding. Reasonable accommodations may be made if requested in advance.

How to Apply

Candidates for this position should submit a cover letter, resume, and contact information for three to five references. Please combine all documents into a single PDF to submit.

Note

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) incumbent in this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. All duties and responsibilities are essential functions and requirements are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. To perform this job successfully, the incumbents will possess the skills, aptitudes, and abilities to perform each duty proficiently. Some requirements may exclude individuals who pose a direct threat or significant risk to the health or safety of themselves or others. The requirements listed in this document are the minimum levels of knowledge, skills, or abilities. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an “at will” relationship.

Woodland School does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin in the administration of its educational or admission policies, financial aid distribution, or other school programs. Woodland School is dedicated to the goal of building a culturally diverse and pluralistic faculty committed to teaching and working in a multicultural environment and strongly encourages applications from candidates who reflect such diversity.

title: Environmental Health and Safety Specialist
description:
Job Description:

Safety at Chewy is Paramount!

Our Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) mission focuses on providing tools, resources, and environments that support safe, efficient, healthy behaviors and proactively encourages employees to lead their health and well-being.

To assist with delivering upon our mission, Chewy is seeking a full-time Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist to serve as a designated shift representative for our Mount Juliet, TN Fulfillment Center (FC), coordinating and implementing all areas of the Chewy EHS Program as encouraged by leadership.

The EHS Specialist promotes a positive environment while following Chewy standards and maintaining a safe work environment.

What you'll do but not limited to:

  • Demonstrate passion for EHS.

  • Serve as the designated EHS shift representative, coordinating and implementing all areas of the Chewy EHS Program as coached by the Site EHSM.

  • Influence behavior and encourage dedication on the part of all Team Members in following Chewy EHS standards and maintaining a safe work environment.

  • Training and mentoring Team Members on observed at-risk behaviors.

  • Support leadership efforts to ensure compliance with corporate EHS Program expectations and applicable federal and state laws.

  • Identify and communicate leadership of compliance issues, EHS risks, and improvement opportunities by performing daily, weekly, and monthly audits.

  • Conduct risk assessments related to jobs performed and new equipment introductions.

  • Recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures to leadership, including ergonomic considerations.

  • Facilitate the incident investigation process.

  • Maintain accurate daily, weekly, and monthly metrics applying corporate-based reporting systems to provide onsite leadership with data to mitigate injuries and incidents.

  • Maintain required paperwork to follow EHS standards.

  • Perform required standard of work observations and audits.

  • Train and assist Team Members in completing their EHS responsibilities.

  • Perform specific EHS training as required by the EHS Manager.

  • Demonstrate strong communication, collaboration, analysis, and customer-centric skills.

  • Demonstrate the ability to analyze accident data, new processes, and equipment for potential EHS concerns and conduct job hazard and job safety analyses.

What you'll need:

  • High school or equivalent diploma.

  • A minimum of 1 year in an EHS related field OR a bachelor’s degree in EHS-relevant field OR 6 months experience performing in a safety-related role within Chewy.

  • Knowledge of OSHA regulations specifically 29 CFR 1910.

  • Experience using Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint in a professional capacity.

  • Able to maintain confidentiality in matters involving personnel issues.

  • Ability to develop and implement department objectives and strategies.

  • Available to work flexible shifts, including days, nights, and/or weekends.

Bonus:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher, preferably in an EHS-relevant field.

  • Experience leading and mentoring a team.

  • Experience in emergency response with active First Aid and CPR certificates.

  • Experience with Intelex, Avetta, Asana, Smartsheet, Safety Management Systems, Microsoft Office, or other similar workspace software.

Why Chewy:

  • Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision.

  • Team member discounts and perks.

  • Collective and dynamic work environment.

  • Opportunities for professional growth and development.

We offer the following benefits for Team Members:

title: APP - NJ
description:
We are seeking Board Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNP) who are dual licensed for both New York and New Jersey to expand access to behavioral health care in your area. If you're passionate about making a difference in mental health and committed to providing exceptional care, we would love to discuss this opportunity with you!


Our Commitment to You:

  • We extend a warm invitation to new PMHNP graduates. Our team is dedicated to delivering exceptional mental health care while fostering the professional development of our providers. During the first 8 weeks, we provide a more robust training and experiential learning environment, where there is additional support.
  • We are committed to providing competitive compensation for our clinicians, including a competitive base salary and a quarterly productivity-based bonus. We offer a comprehensive benefits package tailored specifically for clinicians, with a portion of healthcare premiums covered.
  • At Mindful Care, we strive to minimize administrative tasks and offer schedule flexibility, allowing clinicians to focus on providing excellent care while maintaining control over their schedule. We handle patient scheduling, prior authorizations, case management, billing, and other support functions.
  • Our efficiency enables us to offer better reimbursement rates and lower practice expenses, allowing us to pass on economic benefits to our clinicians. Additionally, we streamline the intake process by having clinical specialists gather patient information and conduct assessments, allowing clinicians to spend more quality time with their patients.
  • We welcome new graduates and provide a collaborator at no expense to supervise clinical work and sign off on accrued clinical hours. Our model emphasizes supportive therapy and non-stimulant or non-narcotic medication management for our patients.


Your Qualifications:

  • Completion of a Master's degree in nursing from an accredited program
  • Active RN license within the employed state
  • Board certification by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) or the American Association of Nurse Practitioners (AANP) as a PMHNP-BC is necessary-new graduates may apply, but cannot start until licensed.
  • APN authorization to practice family health within the employed state, as approved by the Board of Nurse Examiners
  • Possess an active DEA or have an application underway. We can assist you in obtaining licensure.
  • Authorization for prescription practice
  • Solid knowledge of related federal and state regulations, including HIPAA and OSHA compliance
  • Exceptional communication and patient/care delivery, along with strong leadership skills
  • Excellent ability to organize, with a team player mindset
  • Eagerness to engage with diverse groups
  • Supporter of LGBTQ+ initiatives
  • Bilingual abilities are advantageous


Why Choose Mindful Care:

  • Attractive salary package, including a base salary of $120,000 alongside quarterly performance incentives and per diem opportunities.
  • Employer contributions toward Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Enjoy a flexible working arrangement, with 50% remote telehealth work paired with 50% in-office consultations (work four days a week, 10 hours per day); all essential equipment supplied
  • Mindful Care provides a collaborator at no expense to you. The collaborator will be responsible for supervising your clinical work and signing off on all clinical hours accrued during your employment with us
  • Minimized administrative load with full-time in-house billing and appointment handling services
  • Licensing support if you are asked to obtain additional state licenses. Our credentialing department will be happy to assist in managing this process for you, and we cover the costs up front or will reimburse you if necessary.
  • Inclusive benefits package featuring 100% Employer-paid malpractice coverage, matched 401k plan, generous FTO, plus 8 holidays, paid parental leave, and more
  • Prospects for growth and professional improvement as the organization expands
  • Commitment to employee well-being as an organization centered on mental health care
  • Participate in globally sponsored company events, such as exciting Mindful Care summer activities and our annual Holiday Gala and Awards events


Position & Schedule Type

  • Type: Regular Full Time 4 day, 10 hour shift
  • Hours Scheduled Between: Monday-Friday, 8am-8pm
  • Location: Hoboken, NJ
  • Type: Hybrid - (2 days remote, 2 days in office)


Compensation

In addition to a highly competitive benefits package, Mindful Care's Full-Time Advanced Practice Provider (APP) compensation plan ranges from approximately $120K to $200K+ annually, consisting of a base salary and a monthly productivity incentive.


The standard base salary begins at $120K, with the opportunity to earn up to $80K annually in productivity incentives (*monthly bonuses, based on utilization metrics).

Most clinicians reach a total compensation of $155K-$160K once they achieve 55% utilization. Monthly productivity incentives are guaranteed during the onboarding ramp-up period to ensure financial stability as providers build their caseload.


All offers to candidates will ultimately be based on that candidate's individual experience, years of prescriptive authority for psychiatric medication, and skillset.

title: Collections Associate
description:
Job Title: Collections Associate
Hybrid/Remote: Remote
Schedule: Mon to Fri, 8:30a to 5:30p Mountain
Pay Rate: $22/hr to $26.62/hr, DOE

Job Overview:
As a Collections Associate on the Collections team, you'll serve as flexible, floating support across our full suite of 8 products spanning all entities. No two days look the same in this role -- you'll move between products and queues based on where the team needs you most, supporting case influxes, providing backup coverage, and stepping in wherever collection efforts need reinforcement. You'll be equipped with comprehensive training essentials to build fluency across our products, then given the autonomy to float where the work is. The Collections team owns the end-to-end collections process -- reviewing each account to determine the best approach, then executing that plan to bring in the maximum amount of revenue. The ideal candidate brings collections knowledge and experience, possesses a customer-centric mindset, and is able to contribute strongly individually and as part of a small but high-performing team to optimize collection efforts and deliver on critical financial targets.

Required Qualifications:
  • 1-2+ years of direct collections experience, preferably in e-commerce, payments, financial services, or a similar industry
  • Proven ability to learn, adapt, and train on new processes and procedures -- this role touches 8 products, so adaptability is essential
  • Comfort with a highly variable day-to-day, shifting between products and case types based on team needs
  • Logical and rational thinker with demonstrated data analysis and investigative skills
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills -- must have the ability to prioritize and balance multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Strong interpersonal and decision-making skills with the ability to resolve conflicts and build relationships within a dynamic organization

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Knowledge of payment processing methods, including ACH, check, digital wallet, international payments, virtual and credit cards

title: Public Area Attendant
description:
Hotel Name: M Social Sunnyvale
Location: Onsite – Sunnyvale, CA
Salary Range: $25.00 Hourly

Join the Team at M Social Sunnyvale

At M Social Sunnyvale, we don’t just welcome guests—we create moments, spark connections, and bring energy to every interaction. Designed for the young at heart, M Social delivers a bold and vibrant hospitality experience.

About M Social Sunnyvale

As the first ground-up M Social in the U.S., this innovative property features 263 rooms, a dynamic courtyard, and the signature Beast & Butterflies social hub. Located in Silicon Valley, the hotel blends technology, design, and social connectivity to create a unique guest experience.

As part of Millennium Hotels & Resorts, a global hospitality leader with over 145 hotels across key destinations worldwide, our hotel is backed by a legacy of quality, consistency, and service excellence—driven by a passion for hospitality, an entrepreneurial spirit, innovation, and a progressive, solutions-oriented approach."

At Millennium, we are guided by our core values:

  • Passion for Hospitality – Delivering meaningful and memorable guest experiences
  • Entrepreneurial – Taking ownership and acting with agility
  • Innovation & Progressive – Continuously improving how we operate and serve
  • Solutions & Results Oriented – Staying adaptable and focused on results

These values shape how we work, how we lead, and how we create exceptional experiences for our guests and our teams.

About the Role:

As our Public Area Attendant, you will be responsible for maintaining the cleanliness, appearance, and overall presentation of the hotel's public spaces. Your work ensures that every guest experiences a clean, inviting, and well-maintained environment from the moment they arrive until the time they depart.

This role is ideal for someone who takes pride in creating beautiful spaces, enjoys staying active, and is committed to delivering exceptional hospitality through attention to detail and outstanding service.

Your Impact – Public Space Excellence

You will play a vital role in creating a positive first impression for our guests by maintaining immaculate public areas throughout the hotel. Your dedication to cleanliness, organization, and service helps reinforce the vibrant M Social guest experience while supporting the overall success of hotel operations.

What You'll Be Doing

Public Area Cleaning

  • Clean and maintain hotel lobbies, corridors, elevators, restrooms, meeting spaces, fitness center, offices, and other public areas
  • Vacuum, sweep, mop, dust, polish, and sanitize all assigned areas
  • Clean windows, mirrors, glass doors, furniture, fixtures, and decorative surfaces
  • Empty trash and recycling receptacles and replace liners as needed
  • Maintain exterior entrances and other designated outdoor areas to hotel standards

Appearance & Quality

  • Conduct routine inspections of public areas to ensure cleanliness and presentation standards are maintained
  • Replenish guest supplies in public restrooms and common areas
  • Report maintenance issues, damaged furnishings, or safety hazards promptly
  • Ensure all areas remain clean and guest-ready throughout the day

Guest Service

  • Greet guests with a friendly and professional demeanor
  • Respond promptly to guest requests or direct guests to the appropriate department
  • Maintain a courteous, helpful attitude while working in guest-facing areas
  • Assist in creating a welcoming and comfortable environment for all visitors

Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all OSHA guidelines, hotel safety procedures, and chemical handling protocols
  • Safely operate cleaning equipment and machinery
  • Properly store cleaning supplies and equipment after each shift
  • Report unsafe conditions or incidents immediately
  • Follow lost-and-found procedures and maintain guest confidentiality

Team Collaboration

  • Work closely with Housekeeping, Engineering, Front Office, Food & Beverage, and Banquets to maintain hotel appearance
  • Assist Room Attendants and Housepersons when operational needs require
  • Communicate effectively regarding cleaning priorities and maintenance concerns
  • Support special events, meetings, and high-traffic periods by maintaining cleanliness throughout the property

Inventory & Equipment

  • Maintain cleaning carts and equipment in clean, organized, and safe working condition
  • Monitor supply levels and notify supervisors when replenishment is needed
  • Properly use floor care equipment, vacuums, extractors, and other housekeeping tools
  • Assist with deep cleaning projects and seasonal cleaning schedules

Requirements

    • Passion for hospitality and delivering exceptional guest service
    • Strong attention to detail and commitment to cleanliness
    • Ability to work independently while maintaining productivity
    • Excellent time management and organizational skills
    • Positive attitude and dependable work ethic
    • Flexibility to work mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, and varying shifts

Technical / Role-Specific Requirements

    • Previous housekeeping, janitorial, or custodial experience preferred but not required
    • Knowledge of commercial cleaning techniques, chemicals, and equipment is a plus
    • Ability to safely operate floor care equipment and cleaning machinery
    • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions
    • Basic English communication skills; bilingual abilities are a plus

Preferred Qualifications

    • Previous experience in a hotel, resort, or commercial facility preferred
    • Experience maintaining high-traffic public spaces is highly desirable
    • Familiarity with hospitality cleanliness standards is a plus

Physical Requirements

    • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the shift
    • Frequently bend, kneel, reach, push, pull, and lift up to 50 pounds
    • Ability to push cleaning carts and operate floor care equipment
    • Comfortable performing repetitive physical tasks in both indoor and outdoor environments

Education

    • High school diploma or equivalent preferred
    • Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered

Benefits

At Millennium Hotels & Resorts, we support our employees with a competitive benefits package designed to promote wellbeing and long-term success:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • Company-paid Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Coverage
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Company Match (where applicable)
  • Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays
  • Hotel Room Discounts across our global portfolio
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to plan terms and company policy.

Why Join Us

At Millennium Hotels & Resorts, you’re not just taking on a role—you’re joining a global organization committed to people, performance, and growth.

Whether you’re supporting operations behind the scenes or delivering service on the front line, your work contributes to a culture focused on hospitality, collaboration, and results.
If you’re looking for an opportunity to grow, contribute, and make an impact, we invite you to join our team.

title: Tissue Distribution Specialist-Entry Level (Eye Bank)
description:
Make a difference in the lives of others by helping give the gift of sight!


VisionGift (VG) is a non-profit organization founded in 1975 by Lions Clubs of Oregon, which recognized the need for an eye bank to provide ocular tissue for transplants, research and medical education. Since its inception, over 65,000 people have received the gift of sight from tissue procured and screened by VisionGift, which works closely with transplant surgeons. Additionally, ocular tissues have been utilized for valuable research projects and surgical training.


Please visit www.visiongift.org for more information on our organization.


VG has an opening for a challenging and rewarding full-time Tissue Distribution Specialist I (TDS) position in our Portland location. The TDS, under the supervision of the Transplant Distribution Manager, will work as part of a team to: ensure timely evaluation, suitability determination, and distribution of donor tissue for transplant utilization. TDS is the primary contact during normal business hours for surgeons, schedulers, and other affiliated organizations. The position is a day shift position, and upon training completion includes being part of an on-call rotation to potentially cover evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays needs.


This is a great opportunity for individuals who support donation, possess strong problem-solving skills, and have an excellent attention to detail. While we encourage those who meet the requirements to apply, we have had successful candidates from a variety of working and educational backgrounds. This is a fast-paced role where mastery and ownership of important processes is gained quickly.


A successful TDS will have the opportunity to carry out the following functions for VG :

  • Learn how to evaluate transplant-potential corneas to determine surgical suitability through various methods, including specular microscopy and slit lamp microscopy
  • Develop skills in matching transplant corneas with patients and surgeons, taking into account surgery type, surgical suitability, surgeon preferences and VG processing schedule
  • Build and manage the VG surgery calendar by processing tissue requests
  • Network with other eye banks and partner entities to facilitate fulfillment of transplant needs domestically and internationally
  • Prepare for and arrange tissue shipments, both outbound and inbound, including international shipments
  • Learn to navigate and maintain a highly developed database to carry out daily functions
  • Assist with face-to-face interactions with surgeons and surgery center staff as needed
  • Maintain a professional demeanor and interact well with others
  • Other duties as assigned

Starting Pay: $21.20/hour plus shift differentials for weekends.


In addition to the hourly wage, VisionGift offers a generous benefit package including, but not limited to:

  • Medical and vision with an employer paid plan option
  • Dental benefits
  • $20,000 employer-paid life insurance policy
  • Employer-paid short-term disability
  • 401K match
  • 7 paid holidays, 1 DEI holiday and 1 floating holiday
  • Sabbatical leave
  • Shift differentials for nights & weekends
  • Paid Leave
  • Voluntary benefits such as Dependent Care and FSA and more

title: Director of Information Technology
description:
Overview

The IT Director provides enterprise-level leadership for BerryDunn’s technology strategy, operations, and modernization efforts in support of a geographically distributed workforce, multiple office locations, and the firm’s continued growth. This role shapes the vision and direction for IT infrastructure, enterprise systems, business applications, architecture, data platforms, and digital transformation, ensuring technology capabilities enable strategic priorities, operational effectiveness, service reliability, and future growth. Leading the IT Leadership Team, the IT Director serves as a strategic business leader, leveraging technology, data, automation, and artificial intelligence to strengthen client service, improve operational scalability and employee experience, and support the firm’s long-term growth.

Travel Expectations: This role requires minimal travel, less than 10% per year.

You Will

  • Lead the development and execution of a multi-year IT strategic and operational plan that positions IT as a proactive partner in firm growth, transformation, service excellence, and operational effectiveness.
  • Establish IT goals, governance practices, service expectations, and performance measures that strengthen accountability, reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Develop and manage annual operating and capital budgets, technology forecasts, business cases, sourcing strategies, vendor investments, and multi-year investment roadmaps that optimize firm value, cost effectiveness, resource capacity, and service quality.
  • Establish enterprise architecture practices, including technology standards, solution design governance, integration patterns, platform roadmaps, and technical debt management.
  • Oversee internal systems, enterprise applications, data platforms, integrations, and databases to ensure solutions are secure, scalable, reliable, maintainable, and aligned with firm architecture standards.
  • Lead evaluation, governance, and adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, automation, and productivity platforms, to improve business outcomes while aligning with risk, cybersecurity, data protection, and compliance requirements.
  • Advance observability and performance insight across IT systems, including service health, application performance, incident trends, availability, reliability, and KPI reporting.
  • Partner with firm leaders and transformation stakeholders to prioritize and deliver technology initiatives that improve client service, operational efficiency, automation, digital enablement, and business outcomes.
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity, risk, compliance, and business continuity stakeholders to align technology decisions with security requirements, data protection expectations, and firm risk priorities.
  • Partner with business leaders to govern technology demand, prioritize the IT portfolio, and balance resource capacity, business value, risk, and strategic objectives.
  • Lead technology-enabled change by building stakeholder alignment and readiness and coordinating communication, training, adoption, and sustained use of new systems and tools.
  • Promote continuous learning and innovation across IT through knowledge sharing, technical development, communities of practice, and ongoing capability building.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Lead and develop the IT Leadership Team, fostering a culture of empowerment, collaboration, innovation, and accountability.
  • Oversee recruitment, development, retention, and succession planning for IT staff.
  • Define, communicate, and engage others in strategic plans, policies, and technology standards across all levels of the firm.
  • Build and maintain strategic relationships with external partners, vendors, and industry associations to enhance IT strategy and capabilities.

You Have

  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
  • 10-15 years of progressive IT leadership experience in a professional services or complex office environment, including experience leading managers, technical teams, vendors, contractors, and/or managed service providers.
  • Proven experience developing IT strategy, governance practices, technology roadmaps, and operational plans that align with business objectives.
  • Experience managing IT budgets, sourcing strategies, vendor relationships, contracts, statements of work, and service delivery expectations.
  • Experience leading enterprise applications, internal systems development, architecture, integration, database, data platform, or cloud-based technology teams.
  • Working knowledge of modern IT practices, including SDLC, project management, service management, data governance, cybersecurity, cloud platforms, and secure configuration practices.
  • Experience with observability, monitoring, IT service analytics, operational dashboards, and KPI-based performance management.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional transformation initiatives with measurable business outcomes.
  • Relevant technical, ITIL, project management, cloud, or security-related certifications valued.

Compensation Details

The base salary range targeted for this role is $185,000 - $210,000. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based on factors such as company and personal performance. This salary range represents BerryDunn’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. If an applicant possesses experience, education, or other qualifications more than the minimum requirements for this posting, that applicant is encouraged to apply, and a final salary range may then be based on those additional qualifications; compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to years of experience, depth of experience, seniority, merit, education, training, amount of travel, and other relevant business considerations.

BerryDunn Benefits & Culture

Our people are what make BerryDunn special, and in return we strive to support our employees and help them thrive. Eligible employees have access to benefits that go beyond what’s expected to support their physical, mental, career, social, and financial well-being. Visit our website for a complete list of benefits and a look into our culture: Experience BerryDunn.

We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process or perform essential job functions. Please contact careers@berrydunn.com to request an accommodation.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

About BerryDunn

BerryDunn is the brand name under which Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC and BDMP Assurance, LLP, independently owned entities, provide services. Since 1974, BerryDunn has helped businesses, nonprofits, and government agencies throughout the US and its territories solve their greatest challenges. The firm’s tax, advisory, and consulting services are provided by Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC, and its attest services are provided by BDMP Assurance, LLP, a licensed CPA firm.

BerryDunn is a client-centered, people-first professional services firm with a mission to empower the meaningful growth of our people, clients, and communities. The firm has been recognized for its efforts in creating a diverse and inclusive workplace culture, and for its focus on learning, development, and well-being. Learn more at berrydunn.com.

title: Machine Helper 2nd Shift

title: Cybersecurity Engineer
description:
Position Summary

As a company, MAG is dedicated to providing real-time situational awareness to help our customers make the world safer. At MAG, we believe that our success is due to the exceptional employees we recruit, hire, and retain. If you are interested in joining a team that is laser-focused on serving our customers with technical expertise, operational excellence, and flawless execution, then we encourage you to apply today!

MAG Aerospace is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Cybersecurity Engineer to join the team in Tobyhanna, PA. The role involves handling a range of cybersecurity tasks for a diverse network system encompassing servers, laptops, switches, and HAIPEs. The ideal candidate will be conducting cybersecurity verifications to support the Wideband Satellite Communication Operational Management System (WSOMS) subsystems. Join us in ensuring robust cybersecurity for critical operations!

*This role is 100% on-site at the Tobyhanna Army Depot***You must have an active DoD Secret Clearance or be eligible to obtain one**

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Reviews all WSOMS subsystem Information Assurance-related documentation
  • Perform vulnerability assessments using approved Department of Defense scan and analysis tools
  • Provide Risk Management Framework Assessment and Authorization (RMF A&A) support
  • Maintain policy updates for Assured Compliance Assessment Solution Content Automation Protocol (ACAS), Nessus, and Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) scanning tools

title: Plant Chief Engineer
description:
Overview

Gibbon Packing, LLC, an American Foods Group Company has an opportunity for a Plant Chief Engineer at our Gibbon, NE plant.

As our Plant Chief Engineer, you will:

  • Provide assistance and direction to other plant maintenance and operations employees in proper plant procedures and manufacturing methods.
  • Provide guidance for preventative and repair maintenance to ensure that plant operations are able to meet output quotas and deadlines.
  • Design all preventative maintenance programs in coordination with the maintenance and engineering staff.

  • Ensure compliance to all state and federal regulations.
  • Collaborate with various departments to maintain the mechanical integrity of all plant programs.
  • Prepare an effective schedule for all maintenance operations.
  • Prepare annual and monthly maintenance budget proposals and ensure the achievement of all objectives with the required budget.
  • Assist in the installation and maintenance of all machines and tools.
  • NOTE: this description is not intended to be all-inclusive. An employee may perform other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization; these duties are considered marginal.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Required):

  • Must be able to work in the United States without sponsorship.
  • Must be able to effectively communicate in English (speaking, reading, and writing).
  • 5-7 years supervising, planning, and scheduling hourly maintenance personnel.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior supervisory experience in a USDA inspected beef, pork or poultry facility.
  • Valid Certified Plant Engineer (CPE) certification.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Working knowledge of refrigeration systems, steam, and hot water generation systems.
  • Experience in utilizing computerized maintenance management systems to deploy maintenance strategies.
  • Knowledge of rendering and wastewater system management.
  • Strong knowledge and troubleshooting of overhead conveying systems, conveyors, HVAC, hydraulics, compressed air systems, electrical systems, and equipment utilized in food processing.
  • Ability to communicate well (verbal and written) with all levels of employees from hourly to upper management.
  • Ability to identify and address safety hazards; promote safety on a daily basis.
  • Ability to lead by example, encourage teamwork and learning, and motivate the hourly workforce.
  • Must have a high math aptitude; be assertive; and be able to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to perform consistent, accurate work with minimal direction and work successfully as part of a team.

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as laptop computers, desk phones, and smartphones. The position will also be required to regularly visit production facility work environments.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk or sit; use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move objects. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, and color vision.

Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. Applicants with a disability who require a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process can contact Human Resources at the location(s) where you are applying. We participate in the E-Verify program in certain locations as required by law.

Summary

Gibbon Packing, LLC an American Foods Group Company is a privately held beef processing company located in Gibbon, Nebraska. We appreciate our employees and reward them for a job well done. As a member of the team, you will find yourself challenged and contributing in a significant way to the success of the business, and you will be rewarded for that success. If you want to feel appreciated for a job well done and be part of something bigger, then consider joining American Foods Group, a “hire to retire” type of company.

What we offer:

  • Competitive pay
  • Excellent benefit plan. Benefits include: Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flex Spending Accounts, Voluntary Benefits, PTO, 401k, Short Term Disability, Discount Meat Purchase Program, and more!
  • Training, growth and advancement opportunities that will make this the best and last company you work for.

Check Out the Gibbon, NE Area!

Improve your quality of life by residing in Gibbon, Nebraska, a rural city located in the center of Nebraska. Gibbon is located close to many recreational areas and is a short drive from Kearney, NE.

The area also offers:

  • The Great Platte River Road Archway – a museum and monument commemorating the valley’s role in westward expansion. The campus surrounding the museum includes hiking/biking trails, artwork and sculptures, and picnic shelters.
  • Windmill State Recreational Area which includes a swimming beach, 6 lakes for fishing, hiking trails, and more!
  • Year-round community events that the whole family will love.

Try to convince us that there is a better place to live and work other than Gibbon Packing, LLC in Gibbon, NE!
