title: Social Content Producer
description:
As our Social Content Producer, you will join a team that leads with kindness, dreams big and takes action together. You will run our social shoots end to end — planning them, styling them and making them happen every two weeks — so there is always a supply of art-directed, social-first creative to put behind our paid social spend.


💰 Salary: £38,000 – £45,000

👩 Reporting to: Creative Production Lead (interim: Paid-Social Creative Strategist)

📍 Location: Potters Bar

🏙 Hybrid: 2-3 days per week in Potters Bar (and/or wherever needed for shoots)

📝 Employment type: Full Time


Why this role matters ✨


Paid & Organic Social is where most people meet Elizabeth Scarlett for the first time, and creative - not targeting - decides whether that experience goes anywhere. This year we want to triple the number of ad concepts we put into the market, without sliding into the flat, disposable content the category is full of. That means shoots running every fortnight, planned properly and styled to a standard we are proud of. Today they happen when someone can find the time between campaigns.

This is your chance to:

  • Unblock our biggest growth constraint — not budget, not ideas, but the number of finished concepts we can get in front of people each month.
  • Prove that volume and craft are not a trade-off. Most brands tripling their output let the quality slip; this role exists so that we do not.
  • Build a shoot operation from a standing start — the rhythm, the kit, the locations, the props, the freelance hands — and own it as it grows.


What you will be doing 🚀


1. Run a Fortnightly Shoot Rhythm

  • Own a rolling shoot calendar that puts a social shoot in the diary every two weeks
  • Take the concepts written by the Paid-Social Creative Strategist and turn them into a schedule, a shot list and a plan that can genuinely be delivered in a day.
  • Work backwards from the paid-social testing calendar so shoots land ahead of the campaigns that need them
  • Turn the shoot process into something repeatable — templates, checklists and timings the team can run to, rather than something rebuilt from scratch each fortnight.


2. Own Pre-Production End to End

  • Turn each brief into a detailed shot list covering every concept, product, angle and format the team needs from the day.
  • Handle the logistics — samples, props, locations, permissions, creator and talent bookings, kit, call sheets and timings — so everyone arrives knowing exactly what is being made.
  • Pull and prepare product yourself, checking every piece is shoot-ready: right colourway, steamed, unmarked and matched to the concept it belongs to.
  • Manage the shoot budget sensibly, finding the props, locations and freelance hands that give us a premium result without a campaign-sized spend.


3. Style the Shoot Day

  • Style set, surfaces, props and product to the ES look: natural light, minimal props, the product as hero, and space around everything to breathe.
  • Art direct on the day alongside the Video Creators, holding each frame to the brief while keeping the pace needed to get through the full list.
  • Keep the day moving — you are the one watching the clock, the light and the list, so the last set-up is shot as well as the first.
  • Solve problems on the spot: the sample that has not arrived, the location running late, the concept that is not working in front of the camera.


4. Multiply Concepts From Every Shoot Day

  • Plan each day to produce multiple distinct concepts rather than one, with variants in framing, styling, product and setting built into the shot list from the start.
  • Capture the extra assets that make a concept stretch further — alternate openings, verticals, stills, cutaways and detail shots.
  • Find the cheap wins between shoots: quick self-shot captures, in-office set-ups, and content grabbed alongside brand and campaign shoots.
  • Track what has been shot against what has been briefed, so the team always knows what is in hand and what is still missing.


Who we are looking for 🧳


Mindset:

  • A producer's diary and a stylist's eye. This role needs both: you can run a call sheet to the minute and still care whether the linen is folded correctly in shot.
  • Every two weeks means every two weeks. You treat the cadence as a commitment rather than an ambition, and you plan far enough ahead that a missing sample never becomes a cancelled day.
  • You style for the crop, not the room. You think in vertical, sound-off and thumbnail, and you know a set-up that looks beautiful in person can be unreadable at 9:16 on a phone.
  • Volume is a planning problem, not a quality one. You get twelve usable concepts out of a day most people would get four from — because you built the day that way, not because you rushed it.
  • Calm when the day goes sideways. Shoots go wrong. You are the one who reorders the schedule, finds the substitute prop, and keeps everyone relaxed enough to do good work.

Must-have skills:

  • Proven experience producing content shoots end to end — pre-production, scheduling, logistics and running the day itself.
  • Hands-on styling experience with product, props and set, ideally for a brand where how the thing looks is the whole point.
  • The ability to turn a creative brief into a workable shot list, including the timings and set-up order that make the day possible.
  • Confidence working with creators, talent, photographers and videographers on set, directing them warmly and clearly.
  • A strong understanding of social-first formats — vertical video, sound-off viewing, and what a scroll-stopping frame actually needs.

Nice to have:

  • Experience shooting paid social or performance creative, with a sense of what a hook needs from the camera.
  • The ability to self-shoot and cut a rough edit on a phone or camera when a full set-up is not warranted.
  • A background in homeware, accessories, fashion, beauty or gifting.
  • An existing network of freelance crew, stylists, locations and prop sources in and around London.

Experience:

  • Likely 3–5 years in content production, styling, studio or shoot management for a brand, agency or studio.
  • Experience owning shoots yourself rather than assisting on someone else's.
  • Backgrounds we value: content production, social-first video production, art department and styling, studio management, in-house brand shoot teams, creative production at a DTC brand.
  • A portfolio of shoots you have produced and styled — we care far more about this than your CV.

Culture fit:

  • Kind, collaborative and uplifting.
  • Entrepreneurial and action-oriented.
  • Appreciates the value of brand as a growth lever.
  • Cares about the quality of the work and the people creating it.
  • Excited to join a purpose-led brand blending creativity, commerciality and conservation.
  • Comfortable with the unglamorous half of a shoot day — the carrying, the steaming, the resetting — because that is what makes the other half possible.


What success looks like

In your first six months, a social shoot happens every two weeks without anyone having to chase it, and the number of finished ad concepts reaching the account each month has roughly tripled. By month twelve, the rhythm runs on templates and a library the whole team pulls from, freelancers and creators know the process before they arrive, and the work still looks art directed — nobody looking at our ads would guess we had tripled the output.


You're probably not the right fit if...

  • You are an editorial or campaign stylist at heart. Here the budgets are modest, the pace is fortnightly, and a shoot is judged by how many concepts it produced rather than how it looks in a lookbook.
  • You are a producer who hands styling to someone else. This seat holds both, and on most shoot days you will be the one dressing the set.
  • You want to own the concepts. The Paid-Social Creative Strategist writes the briefs; your craft is turning them into real, beautifully made footage. If that would frustrate you, this is not the right seat.


What we offer 💡


Salary, bonus & benefits

  • £38,000 – £45,000 DOE
  • 10% performance bonus
  • Health Insurance, plus Health & Wellbeing financial support
  • Life assurance & enhanced Pension contributions

Flexibility and time

  • Hybrid working (minimum 2 days in-office) with regular time in Potters Bar
  • 24 days holiday plus bank holidays
  • Up to 1 month “work anywhere" in the UK

Personal development

  • Annual L&D budget (3% of salary)
  • Annual summer retreat (e.g. 42 Acres in Somerset)

Team perks

  • £500 ES products per year at 60% team discount
  • 25% friends and family discount code

Impact and ownership

  • Own the shoot operation behind our fastest-growing channel — you are building it, not staffing someone else's.
  • Direct contribution to our wildlife conservation mission.


Our hiring process 👟

  1. Intro call with our People Team
  2. Interview with our Paid-Social Creative Strategist
  3. Interview with our Senior Creative
  4. Portfolio Share
  5. Final round: interview with the Growth Director


🌿 We have the products, the audience and the spend. What we need is someone who can make sure there is always something beautiful to put behind it.


Apply now and bring your talent to Elizabeth Scarlett.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Lake Stevens, Washington.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Lake Stevens area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Lake Stevens requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Henkilökohtainen avustaja Myyrmäen alueelle Vantaalle
description:
Tule mukaan luomaan elämäsi tarinaa Avustajasi Validia Oy:lle! Haemme nyt henkilökohtaisia avustajia Myyrmäen alueelle.

Miltä kuulostaisi merkityksellinen ja arvokas työ sinulle sopivilla työajoilla? Haluaisitko saada työkokemusta hoitoalasta näköalapaikalta, tai kaipaatko tekemistä eläkepäivien ratoksi rauhallisissa olosuhteissa yksi asiakas kerrallaan? Tule mukaan! Henkilökohtaisena avustajana meillä pääset osaksi asiakkaidemme arvokkaita tarinoita.

Validialla henkilökohtaisen avun asiakkaat ovat vammaispalvelujen piiriin kuuluvia henkilöitä. Henkilökohtainen apu on kotona tai kodin ulkopuolella tapahtuvaa avustamista niissä asioissa, joihin henkilö ei itse kykene sairauden tai vamman vuoksi. Avustaminen voi olla harrastuksissa tai opiskelussa tukemista, kodinhoidollisia askareita tai vapaa-ajan tapahtumien mahdollistamista. Toisinaan avustajan tärkeimpänä tehtävänä on olla juttukaverina ja seurana: olla se kiireetön ihminen ihmiselle. Henkilökohtaisen avustajan rooli asiakkaan arjessa on merkittävä, sillä pyrkimyksenä on tukea ja mahdollistaa kotona asuminen mahdollisimman pitkään, sekä tarjota mahdollisuus aktiiviseen ja mielekkääseen arkeen toteuttaen asiakkaan itsemääräämisoikeutta.

Työ sopii sinulle, joka kaipaat vaihtelevuutta ja satunnaisuutta työhösi – työtä tehdään asiakkaan tarpeiden ja toiveiden mukaisesti. Sinulla on myös mahdollisuus vaikuttaa vuorojesi ajankohtiin yhdessä asiakkaan kanssa sopien. Työskentelet itsenäisesti ja sitoudut sovittuihin käytäntöihin. Avoimella asenteella ja omalla persoonalla pääsee pitkälle! Joustavuuden ansiosta työmme sopii niin opiskelijalle kuin eläkeläisellekin lisäansioksi. Emme edellytä sinulta alan koulutusta tai työkokemusta, mutta nämä luetaan eduksi.

Tarjoamme sinulle

  • Työehtosopimuksen mukaisen palkkauksen: Yksityisen sosiaalipalvelualan TES, palkkaluokka G16A

  • Kohtaamisia erilaisten ihmisten kanssa

  • Joustavan työajan

  • Mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa oman työsi sisältöön

  • Mahdollisuuden tutustua vammaistyöhön ja hoitoalaan

  • Perehdytyksen osaamisesi mukaan

  • Ammattitaitoisen huumorilla höystetyn työyhteisön tuen

  • Mahdollisuuden lisäopintojen kautta työllistyä myös muihin sosiaali- ja terveysalan työtehtäviin

Toivomme sinulta

  • Aitoa kiinnostusta avustamistyötä kohtaan

  • Positiivista ja iloista asennetta

  • Halua oppia uutta ja kehittyä työssäsi

  • Riittävää suomen kielen taitoa, muu kielitaito katsotaan eduksi

Edellytämme sinulta

  • Tartuntatautilain 48 §:n mukaista rokotussuojaa sekä 55 §:n mukaista tuberkuloosiselvitystä

  • Rikosrekisteriotteen esittämistä sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon valvonnasta annetun lain mukaisesti

Jätäthän tietosi hakulomakkeen kautta. Henkilökohtaisen avun tehtäviin tarvitaan uusia työntekijöitä sitä mukaa, kun asiakaskuntamme kasvaa. Olemme hakijoihin yhteydessä, kun hakijan ja asiakkaan tarpeet ja toiveet kohtaavat. Täytäthän hakemuksesi siis huolellisesti! Lisätietoja tehtävästä kaivatessasi voit olla yhteydessä meihin sähköpostitse hkapuhr@validia.fi.

title: Data Analyst Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
Position Title: Data Analyst Intern

Reports to: Manager, Automation Architect

Location: Greensboro, N.C.


POSITION SUMMARY

We are seeking a detail-oriented and technically minded Data Analyst Intern to join our team. In this role, you will work within our on-premise data environment, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the data that powers our business decisions. A significant portion of this internship focuses on data quality assurance (QA). You will ensure that our data is accurate, consistent, and reliable by performing rigorous testing and validation.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


Data Quality Assurance (QA) & Testing

  • Source-to-Target Validation: Perform comparative analysis between source systems and our Data Warehouse to ensure data was extracted and transformed correctly.
  • Regression Testing: Validate data outputs after system updates or pipeline changes to ensure existing reports and dashboards remain accurate.
  • Data Integrity Checks: Write SQL scripts to proactively identify nulls, duplicates, or schema mismatches before they impact the business.
  • Bug Reporting: Document data anomalies clearly and track them to resolution, working closely with engineers to identify the root cause.

Analysis & Technical Operations

  • Data Analysis: Write complex SQL queries to extract and manipulate data for ad-hoc business requests.
  • Infrastructure Interaction: Use the Linux command line to navigate servers, execute validation scripts, and grep logs for errors.
  • Kubernetes Support: Assist in monitoring data applications running on Kubernetes; check pod status and retrieve logs (kubectl logs) to aid in debugging QA failures.
  • Documentation: Maintain the Data Catalog and Business Glossary, ensuring that metric definitions match the technical reality of the data.
  • Supplier N-Tier Mapping: Research and identify data sources to build supplier n-tier maps, discovering relationships between Tier 1 suppliers and their upstream sub-suppliers (Tier 2, Tier 3, etc.).


POSITION REQUIREMENTS:


Education

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field.

Technical Skills & Knowledge

  • SQL (Essential): Strong proficiency in writing SQL queries. You must be able to write queries to test data (e.g., finding set differences, counting variances).
  • Linux / Command Line: Comfort working in a Linux environment. You should know basic shell commands (bash) for file management and log inspection.
  • Kubernetes: Basic conceptual understanding of containerization. Familiarity with kubectl is a plus.
  • Data Concepts: Understanding of Data Warehousing (Star Schema) and ETL processes.
  • Programming: Basic proficiency in Python (Pandas) for scripting or data automation.
  • QA Mindset: A natural skepticism of data. You should have the habit of asking, "Does this number actually make sense?"

Soft Skills & Attributes

  • Attention to Detail: The ability to spot small discrepancies in large datasets.
  • Technical Curiosity: A desire to understand the infrastructure (servers/containers) that supports the data.
  • Communication: Ability to clearly report bugs and explain "why" a data point looks wrong to stakeholders.



Over the years, we’ve discovered that the most effective and successful associates at apexanalytix are people who have a specific combination of values, skills, and behaviors that we call “The apex Way”. Read more about The apex Way -

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Park, Florida.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Park area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Park requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Repair Technician
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We have an exciting opportunity for a Repairs Technician to join us in our St Agnes store! As a key ambassador for our Lived & Loved program, you will be responsible for repairing Finisterre clothing and hardware, contributing to our circularity initiatives. This role requires a self-motivated individual who thrives in fast paced workshop and possesses a passion and the skills for craftsmanship.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Technical

  • The capability to assess an item for repair and stabilize the issues.
  • An expertise in darning, zip replacements and patching insulated and woven garments. The ability to deconstruct and reconstruct items.
  • Skilful use of industrial flatbed sewing machine, knowledge of relevant sewing attachments and when to use in accordance with fabrics and hardware.
  • Competent knowledge of hardware fixings, toggles, zip sliders, snaps, etc
  • An understanding of colour, which tones are well suited and the visual story of colour.
  • Ensuring repairs are an exceptional standard. Attention to detail is imperative.

Customer Experience

  • Ensuring excellent customer service communication with each customer interaction.
  • Meeting and greeting our repair customers in store. To be enthusiastic and knowledgeable about why we repair, how we repair, the history of Finisterre repair and communicating this with our customers, in line with Lived & Lived standards.
  • Understanding customer needs and responding in a timely and efficient manner by phone, email or in person.

Workshop Coordination

  • To look after the workshop in line with Lived and Loved department standards.
  • Liaising with Head of Repair responding to urgent needs for smooth running of London Repair Workshop.
  • Ensuring all machinery is kept in good working order. To inform Head of Repair of any issues.
  • Liaising with HQ Repairs to ensure fabric library is kept seasonally stocked. Supplemented by ordering any hard to acquire fabrics from list of approved online fabric stores.
  • Ordering of all hardware and liaising with Repairs HQ to ensure stock is replenished.
  • Liaising with HQ Repairs weekly to relay any issues, improvements, moments.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FINISTERRE

  • A passion and a competence of garment repair
  • Ability to work independently and to deadlines.
  • Trained and experienced in the use of industry level sewing machinery.
  • Proven experience visible and invisible repair techniques
  • Proven experience in hand sewing, machine sewing, repairing, deconstruction and reconstruction of garments in woven and technical fabrics.
  • Experience and competence of all types of zip replacements.
  • Competent in using stock systems, previous experience of Shopify desirable.
  • Excellent customer service, both written and verbal. Experience communicating with customers in retail setting an advantage.
  • A strong commitment to learning about the key skills, deliverables and challenges of Lived & Loved Repairs, and to delivering continuous improvement.
  • A willingness to own and drive your personal development plan and open to asking for and accepting feedback on performance. Thrives on positive change.
  • Commitment to inclusivity, equality and social and environmental sustainability.
  • Passion, energy and aspiration in line with Finisterre values, products, brand and customers.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work in a team.
  • This role will require a level of flexible availability and will be required to work some weekends.

Important: The successful candidate must, by the start of their employment, have permission to work in the UK. Please note that Finisterre are not licensed to sponsor overseas workers.


WHAT YOU’LL RECEIVE FROM FINISTERRE

We are offering a part time 22.5 hours/3 days, fixed term contract, based at our Headquarters at Wheal Kitty, St Agnes, Cornwall. We’ll invest in you with a salary of £16,200 (calculated on pro rata basis to a full time equivalent of £27,000)

But it’s not just a job. At Finisterre, we provide an opportunity to grow and develop yourself within at a fast-paced, growing B Corp certified brand with a great culture and an exciting purpose. You’ll get the chance to collaborate with a diverse community of people with a shared mission. In return, we take good care of you through a range of initiatives and rewards, including:

  • 25 days holiday per year, plus up to 8 UK bank holidays (pro rata for pat time employees)
  • Additional holidays for length of service
  • Your birthday day off
  • Up to 3 days of paid volunteering – we will support you in giving back to communities and causes
  • A discretionary bonus scheme, based on company performance
  • An enhanced pension scheme with Scottish Widows
  • 60% product discount for personal and gift use
  • 30% Friends and Family product discount
  • Enhanced Family Leave policies to support you in growing your family
  • Life assurance with access to an online wellbeing platform which includes, an employee assistance program, virtual GP appointments, digital gym, and a range of perks
  • Access to a range of wellbeing resources, including counselling services, cycle to work, eye tests, and wellbeing activities
  • Regular company and team social events
  • Various discounts from our B Corp community
  • Access our online Learning Library and company-wide training sessions delivered by both internal and external trainers to support you in your ongoing development.
  • An hour to spend in or by the sea every Tuesday followed by Sea Tuesday companywide meeting
  • And so much more!

Closing date: We’ll be interviewing as we go along, so we’d encourage you to submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

Finisterre is committed to building diverse and inclusive teams. We celebrate difference and encourage everyone to join us and be themselves at work.

title: Technician, AD Operations
description:
Position Summary:

The Renewable Gas Field Service Technician is responsible for operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting renewable gas systems and associated equipment across multiple facilities. This role requires a high degree of physical mobility and the ability to respond quickly and decisively to equipment malfunctions, safety risks, and hazardous conditions—including those caused by severe weather events. The technician must be prepared to travel between sites at short notice and maintain site safety and operational continuity during critical incidents.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Operate and monitor renewable gas compression and decompression facilities, including rotating equipment, gas monitoring and metering systems, compressors, and gas delivery systems.
  • Troubleshoot equipment failures and malfunctions to determine root cause; perform repairs, maintenance, or replacement of components.
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance on mechanical systems, including pumps and compressors.
  • Maintain, modify, and repair instrumentation and control equipment (e.g., recorders, flowmeters, analyzers, and other monitoring tools).
  • Serve as the lead on-site technician, coordinating operational and maintenance activities.
  • Record and analyze operational data; provide daily, weekly, and monthly reports on trends, availability, and production.
  • Collect samples for quality testing and maintain accurate compliance records.
  • Maintain a clean and organized working environment at all facilities.
  • Assist with process control improvements to enhance operational efficiency.
  • Respond swiftly to urgent operational issues, including gas leaks, mechanical failures, or extreme weather-related disruptions, to ensure safety and system integrity.
  • Other duties and project assignments as directed.

Qualifications:

· 4 years of experience with industrial equipment

· 2 years of experience in industrial maintenance

· Valid U.S. work authorization

· High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)

· Valid Driver’s License

Preferred Skills:

· Strong understanding of mechanical systems and safety protocols

· Basic knowledge of PLC systems, Analog I/O, Digital I/O, RTD Probes

· Basic knowledge of working with Electrical Voltages of 24vDC, 120vAC, 480vAC

· Basic knowledge of troubleshooting 480v Motors, and VFD’s

· Ability to read Electrical Schematics and P&ID Drawings

· Ability to read and follow technical documentation and work instructions

· Experience with wastewater or gas processing systems (preferred)

· Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

· Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and prioritize tasks

· Excellent verbal and written communication

· High degree of self-motivation and initiative

· Must demonstrate physical agility and endurance to navigate industrial sites quickly, including stairs, ladders, confined spaces, and uneven terrain

· Ability to maintain situational awareness and composure in hazardous or time-sensitive environments

Work Environment:

· Standing for extended periods

· Stair and ladder climbing

· Lifting up to 50 lbs

· Working with and around hazardous materials

· Outdoor work in varying weather conditions, including extreme heat, cold, and severe weather events

· Use of required PPE (hard hat, safety glasses, air masks, hearing protection)

· Participation in on-call rotation for rapid response to operational incidents

· Ability to work in high-stress or emergency environments, including immediate response to hazardous gas conditions or mechanical failures

· Must be capable of rapid deployment between sites, often under unpredictable or challenging field conditions

Schedule:

· Monday to Friday, 8-hour shifts

· On-call rotation for after-hours and weekend coverage

· Primary site locations: Enterprise, AL

· Occasional travel to additional facilities (20%)

title: Technical Trainer
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Deliver and support the ongoing development of training programs and curriculum for Chief Operators, Drivers, Analysis personnel, customers, and employees requiring refresher or remedial training in Shelton, in the field, and at international locations. Deliver classroom, practical, digital, and field-based instruction using modern training methods designed to strengthen knowledge retention, technical competency, and on-the-job performance.

Support the continuous improvement and modernization of training programs by evaluating instructional effectiveness, trainee performance, emerging technologies, field feedback, and operational needs. Assist with the development and enhancement of course content, instructional materials, assessments, and training delivery methods.

Administer the Certification Hub and maintain compliance with required inspection certifications, railroad credentials, and training records. Monitor trainee progress, assess development needs, and partner with field management to address training gaps and support progression through established qualification and certification pathways. Provide new hire training coverage as required.


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Training Delivery and Instruction

·Deliver classroom, virtual, practical, and field-based instruction on rail flaw detection techniques, principles, methodologies, equipment, safety requirements, and related operational practices.

·Apply effective instructional practices using a variety of training methods, including presentations, demonstrations, interactive exercises, scenario-based learning, simulations, videos, digital content, and hands-on practice.

·Conduct practical demonstrations and exercises involving the operation of rail flaw detection equipment and the identification, interpretation, and assessment of track flaws.

·Incorporate real-world operational scenarios, case studies, and problem-solving exercises to strengthen technical judgment and decision-making skills.

·Reinforce learning through short-form training, refresher modules, knowledge checks, and microlearning techniques where appropriate.

· Administer qualification, technical, and safety examinations and practical assessments.

·Evaluate trainee competency through written assessments, practical demonstrations, observations, and established performance standards.

·Maintain standards of academic performance, conduct, and participation, providing coaching and counseling to trainees as required.

· Report trainee progress, training concerns, and program recommendations to the Global Training Manager.

· Promote Sperry’s culture, safety expectations, trainee success, technical excellence, and quality standards.

· Maintain training facilities, instructional technology, equipment, and training materials in good working order.

·Remain current on developments in rail flaw detection technologies, non-destructive testing practices, instructional methods, learning technologies, and applicable regulatory requirements.

Curriculum Development and Continuous Improvement

· Support the design, development, and ongoing modernization of the Sperry School of Rail Testing curriculum.

·Develop and update instructor-led materials, practical exercises, job aids, videos, digital learning content, assessments, and other instructional resources.

·Identify opportunities to incorporate digital, self-paced, video-based, microlearning, simulation, and blended-learning approaches into the curriculum.

·Incorporate lessons learned from field operations, quality findings, safety observations, technical changes, customer feedback, and trainee performance into training content.

· Evaluate training effectiveness using trainee performance, assessment results, field feedback, operational outcomes, and other available training metrics.

· Recommend improvements to curriculum content, delivery methods, training duration, sequencing, and instructional tools to improve knowledge retention, technical competency, and trainee readiness.

·Support structured learning pathways that integrate classroom instruction, digital learning, hands-on practice, field experience, certification, and ongoing proficiency validation.

·Support the development of refresher and remedial training programs to address identified performance, competency, safety, or technical knowledge gaps.

International and Customer Training

· Travel to domestic and international locations to deliver classroom, practical, field-based, and blended technical training.

·Deliver customer training on applicable Sperry technologies, equipment, testing methodologies, and related technical topics as required.

·Adapt training delivery, as appropriate, to accommodate regional operating requirements, customer requirements, regulations, equipment, and participant experience levels.

· Conduct Canadian Operator training when classes require qualification to operate in Canada.

· Support consistent global training standards while recognizing applicable regional and customer requirements.

Certification Hub and Compliance

·Administer the training and certification hub and coordinate with field personnel to maintain compliance with required railroad credentials, inspection certifications, safety qualifications, and other required training.

· Maintain accurate and timely training and certification records in Rippling and other applicable systems.

· Regularly review certification status and identify upcoming expirations, missing requirements, and compliance gaps.

· Coordinate with field management and employees to ensure required certifications and credentials remain current.

· Support the development and maintenance of defined certification and qualification pathways for operational positions.

title: LRDR Systems Analyst
description:
Overview

Job Title: LRDR Systems Analyst

Contract: SSPARS

Location: Beale AFB, CA

FLSA Status: Exempt

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Must possess good written and verbal communication skills to include the ability to explain results of analysis to both technical and non-technical personnel.
  • Experience with command and control (c2) systems and/or phased array radars is desired.
  • Sensor Manager Qualification Course (SMQC) is highly desired

LICENSES OR CERTIFICATION:

  • Required to maintain a certification as a Missile Defense Radar Operator.

BASIC FUNCTIONS OF THE JOB:

  • The LRDR Systems Analyst utilizes their experience, knowledge, and analytic tools to determine system performance in both the operational environment and the testing environment. The systems analyst supports the operations manager by performing the duties of an assistant manager.

PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • The systems analyst will interface with a number of external agencies to assess radar performance, deficiencies, and anomalous behavior.
  • Support the system via on call when outside of normal working hours.
  • Analyze critical system files such as the mission plan file, satellite catalog, and satellite task list for abnormal data or overflow.
  • Analyze computer/radar O&M logs for system or operator errors. Analyze daily uncorrelated target (UCT) rates to identify abnormal performance.
  • Review the one-year library of computer system logs, ensuring the logs are properly archived and maintained.
  • Review and analyze system calibration, operability assessment test results, ESPs and other indicators which give an indication of system performance utilizing the system calibration metrics on the Space C2 Agency website.
  • Analyze occurrences of system outages or operational degradation such as the following:
    • False Launch and Impact Message or False Impacting Object Reports
    • Indications of radar system degradation
    • Uncommon computer halts or hangs
    • CAT 1 satellite misses;
    • EMI
    • Failure to track a real missile launch or significant portions of a real missile launch in coverage
    • Other abnormal data, performance, and occurrences that may lead to a system failure.
  • Provide analyses to support site operations investigations to the Director of Operations (DO), Operations Support, or SOC-B CMDR/CCH.
  • Provide Problem Reports (PRs) to support site operations investigations by the DO, Operations Support, CMDR/CCH, or Installation/Site Commander. Submit a Deficiency Report (DR) for unusual and unique anomalies, or outages.
  • Generate an AF Form 1067 or Standard Change Form (SCF) prior to installing new software constants for the subarray test and element test installations.
  • Generate an SCF for system or software modifications for corrective or preventive action as a result of analyses or any other proposed system/software modifications.
  • Evaluate and provide written technical analysis on any system modification/upgrade proposal or recommendation.
  • Maintain references to any associated PR, DR and SCF and supporting data.
  • Draft ICE plans and ICE reports as requested and provide data, supporting documentation and recommendations for all testing activities.
  • Interface with Space Training and Readiness Delta Detachment 4 (Det 4) and other military personnel, as well as other contractor personnel, to support testing activities. Activities shall include, but not be limited to:
    • Development
    • Test and Evaluation (DT&E)
    • Operational Test and Evaluation (OT&E), and Installation
    • Checkout and Evaluation (ICE) testing
  • Develop and maintain checklists to be used by site MDRO personnel.
  • Performs other analysis duties as directed by management.

SUPERVISION:

  • Works under the supervision of the Operations Manager
  • Will act as a supervisor at times as the Assistant Manager

SECURITY CLEARANCE

  • Currently hold or be able to obtain and maintain the proper US DoD issued security clearance, which requires US Citizenship. Security clearance eligibility may be discussed during the interview phase.
  • Employment and start date are contingent upon the candidate receiving the required US DoD issued interim security clearance

WORKING ENVIRONMENT:

  • Exerts limited physical energy. May have to handle 20-30 pound loads on occasion.
  • Working Conditions: Normal office environment. May work extended hours or weekends. May travel overnight or on weekends.

Pay Range

Starting from USD $110,000.00/Yr.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Dickerson, Maryland.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Dickerson area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Dickerson requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: IT Systems Administration
description:

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Pleasanton, California.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Pleasanton area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Pleasanton requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

The Field Decommission Technician supports the safe and efficient decommissioning of power distribution equipment at customer sites and Emerald Transformer facilities. The position is responsible for dismantling retired units, recovering salvageable metals and usable parts, and handling oils, solvents, and other liquid compounds in accordance with company safety and environmental expectations. This role requires regular travel throughout Emerald Transformer’s service territory, including overnight and extended stays, and the flexibility to work overtime, call-in hours, evenings, and weekends to meet customer needs. When field work is not scheduled, the technician is assigned work at the home facility and may also support other field crews or Emerald Transformer entities as needed.

Key Responsibilities
  • Decommission power distribution equipment in commercial and industrial environments.
  • Disassemble decommissioned power distribution units safely and efficiently.
  • Salvage metals and recover usable parts from decommissioned equipment.
  • Handle, contain, and dispose of oils, solvents, and other liquid compounds in accordance with company environmental and safety requirements.
  • Use hand tools, pneumatic tools, and cutting torches to complete assigned work.
  • Operate forklifts, overhead cranes, and other material handling equipment as needed.
  • Maintain accountability for shop tools and equipment at the assigned worksite.
  • Travel throughout Emerald Transformer’s service territory, including overnight and extended stays near customer locations.
  • Work overtime and respond to call-in needs, including evening and weekend emergency work, to support customer requirements.
  • Collaborate closely with coworkers and contribute effectively in a team-oriented environment.
  • Perform assigned work at the home facility when field decommission work is not scheduled, based on direction from facility leadership.
  • Support other field crews and, when needed, perform assignments for any Emerald Transformer entity.
  • Maintain a safe, orderly, and productive worksite at all times.
  • Package and bale materials for shipment and load trailers as assigned.
Education/Certifications
  • A high school diploma or GED is preferred.
  • A valid driver’s license is preferred.
Experience
  • One to three years of experience in industrial labor, field service, demolition, mechanical disassembly, rigging, scrap/salvage operations, transformer or electrical equipment support, or a related hands-on environment preferred.
  • Experience using hand tools and pneumatic tools in a production, shop, or field environment required.
  • Experience working around heavy equipment, metal components, or material handling operations preferred.
Knowledge Skills & Abilities
  • Ability to safely decommission and disassemble power distribution equipment.
  • Ability to identify and recover salvageable metals and usable components.
  • Ability to safely handle oils, solvents, and other liquid compounds.
  • Ability to use hand tools and pneumatic tools effectively.
  • Ability to operate a cutting torch to cut metal parts.
  • Ability to operate forklifts, overhead cranes, and other material handling equipment as needed.
  • Ability to work independently, stay self-directed, and complete tasks in a timely and efficient manner with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to work closely with others in a team-oriented environment.
  • Willingness and ability to travel throughout Emerald Transformer’s service territory, including overnight and extended stays.
  • Willingness and ability to work overtime, call-in hours, and evening or weekend emergency assignments as needed.
  • Ability to perform heavy physical work, including exerting up to 100 pounds occasionally and more than 50 pounds frequently.
  • Ability to climb, push, stand, hear, walk, reach, feel, balance, pull, stoop, lift, finger, crawl, crouch, kneel, grasp, and perform repetitive motion as required by the job.
  • Ability to work indoors and outdoors and tolerate extreme cold, extreme heat, vibration, atmospheric conditions, exposure to oils, and other hazardous conditions including moving mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, scaffolding, heights, heat, and chemicals.
  • Ability to work in narrow aisles or passageways and to consistently use required personal protective equipment, including eye protection, gloves, and hearing protection.
  • Commitment to following company environmental and safety programs, company policies, and standard operating procedures.

title: Correspondence Writer - FS ACES Program
description:
CWI Works is recruiting for a Correspondence Writer position through the Forest Service Experienced Services (FS-ACES) Program. This grant-administered program provides experienced professionals with an opportunity to support the mission and operations of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, U.S. Forest Service.

Role and Responsibilities

A Correspondence Writer is responsible for receiving, organizing, processing, and responding to all forms of written correspondence, including electronic letters and correspondence received through the mail. The skills required pertain to the systematic management of all official communications to ensure they are received, acted upon, and stored effectively, supporting both internal operations and external relationships. The Secretary has required a timely response to controlled correspondence, and the agency needs to prioritize these responses to ensure they are handled in a timely manner.

Duties include:

  • Drafting and writing correspondence in order to process, receive, organize, and respond to all forms of written correspondence, including electronic letters and correspondence received through the mail.
  • Responding promptly and accurately to written correspondence, ensuring clarity, professionalism, and timeliness using internal controlled correspondence systems and clear guidance/text language.
  • Maintaining records of correspondence for legal, compliance, and operational purposes.
  • Routing correspondence to the appropriate individual or department for review and signature.
  • Ensuring confidentiality and data protection when managing and tracking correspondence.
  • Using the systematic management of all official communications to ensure they are received, acted upon, and stored effectively, supporting both internal operations and external relationships.

Qualifications

Successful candidates must be 55 years of age or older and eligible to work in the United States. Candidates must have a High School Diploma or GED and a minimum of 20 years of relevant experience in a related field. Candidates should have demonstrated experience drafting and managing professional correspondence, organizing and tracking official communications, maintaining accurate records, and routing correspondence for appropriate review and signature. Strong written communication skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to handle confidential information are essential. Experience working with correspondence tracking systems and government or administrative applications is highly desirable. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite is also required.


Hours & Compensation:

Part-Time position working up to 30 hours per week @ $80.00.

title: Mental Health Professional
description:
Position type: Full time, exempt, 10 Month

Reporting & Collaboration​

  • Key Collaborators:

    • Special Education Case Managers

    • Behavior Climate Specialists

    • Teachers and Instructional Staff

    • Families and External Mental Health Partners

Autonomy & Decision Making​

The Mental Health Professional exercises professional judgment in:

  • Designing and delivering therapeutic interventions aligned to student needs

  • Monitoring progress toward IEP counseling goals

  • Conducting risk and safety assessments

  • Determining appropriate clinical supports and referrals

  • Recommending Tier 3 interventions for students experiencing significant behavioral or emotional challenges

IEP Mental Health Service Delivery

  • Maintain timely and accurate documentation of services in SpedTrack and SCUTA.

  • Provide individual and small group counseling aligned to IEP goals.

  • Participate in IEP meetings and collaborate with special education teams on student support strategies.

Tier 3 Behavioral & Mental Health Intervention

  • Provide clinical support for students experiencing significant behavioral or emotional challenges.

  • Implement evidence-based therapeutic approaches such as cognitive behavioral strategies, trauma-informed interventions, and solution-focused counseling.

  • Support the development and monitoring of Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) for students with intensive behavioral needs.

CARE Team / MTSS Coordination

  • Coordinate or support CARE/MTSS processes for students requiring intensive interventions.

  • Facilitate structured problem-solving meetings to identify barriers to student success.

  • Monitor progress of Tier 3 interventions and adjust supports as needed.

Section 504 Coordination

  • Support the development and monitoring of Section 504 plans

  • Collaborate with teachers and families to ensure accommodations are implemented with fidelity.

  • Maintain documentation and compliance with federal guidelines.

McKinney-Vento Homeless Liaison Responsibilities

  • Serve as the school’s McKinney-Vento liaison, ensuring students experiencing homelessness are identified and supported in accordance with federal law.

  • Ensure students experiencing homelessness receive immediate enrollment protections and equitable access to school services.

  • Coordinate supports such as transportation, academic access, and participation in school programs.

  • Maintain required documentation and ensure compliance with McKinney-Vento federal requirements.

  • Partner with families and community organizations to connect students with housing, social service, and community resources.

  • Collaborate with external agencies to ensure coordinated support for students

Service Delivery

  • IEP counseling minutes delivered with fidelity and compliance.

Student Impact

  • Improved behavioral and social-emotional outcomes for students receiving Tier 3 supports.

Compliance

  • Accurate and timely documentation of counseling services and intervention progress.

Systems Coordination

  • Effective CARE/MTSS coordination for students with intensive needs.

  • Effective implementation and monitoring of 504 accommodations

Student Access & Equity

  • Students experiencing homelessness are identified and supported in compliance with McKinney-Vento requirements.

  • Barriers to enrollment, attendance, and participation are minimized through coordinated school and community supports.

  • Expertise in evidence-based mental health and behavioral interventions

  • Strong knowledge of special education counseling services and compliance requirements

  • Ability to conduct risk assessments and crisis intervention

  • Experience supporting students with trauma, behavioral challenges, and emotional regulation needs

  • Knowledge of McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act requirements

  • Excellent documentation, organization, and time management skills

  • Ability to build strong relationships with students, families, and school staff

Required

  • Valid state licensure or certification in a mental health discipline

  • Experience providing counseling or behavioral intervention services to children or adolescents

  • Strong understanding of student mental health and behavioral support practices

Preferred

title: Area Safety and Quality Officer
description:
Job Title: Area Safety and Quality Officer

Location: Modesto, CA, US (100% Onsite for rounding across two hospitals)

Position Type: Regular, Full-Time | Travel: Up to 20%

Job Level: Director / Senior Director

Salary Range: USD $216,700 – $255,000 / year

Travel Requirements: Up to 20% of the time (local service area rounding).

Visa Sponsorship: Not available for this position

Relocation: Evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

Position Overview

The Area Safety and Quality Officer provides strategic leadership, executive oversight, and clinical expertise across small- to medium-sized service areas (facilities with under 300 licensed beds). Responsible for two hospitals within the Modesto service area, this role drives the development and execution of comprehensive clinical quality, patient safety, infection prevention, risk management, and continuous survey readiness initiatives.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned Registered Nurse with executive-level experience leading a health system Quality Department, adept at aligning clinical operations with regulatory standards, evidence-based practices, and organizational strategy.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Operational Management

  • Build organizational capacity and prepare high potentials for growth opportunities and advancement; build collaborative networks inside and outside the organization.
  • Provide a framework for soliciting and acting on performance feedback; drive collaboration to set goals and provide open feedback and coaching to foster performance improvement.
  • Model and drive continuous learning, overseeing the recruitment, selection, and development of talent; stay current with industry trends, benchmarks, and best practices.
  • Act as a thought leader on industry trends, benchmarks, and best practices; share insights within and across teams to drive continuous improvement.
  • Motivate and empower teams; maintain a highly skilled and engaged workforce by aligning cross-functional resource plans with business objectives.
  • Provide guidance on complex decisions and create opportunities for expanded decision-making scope and impact across teams.
  • Oversee the operation of multiple units and/or departments by identifying member and operational needs; translate business strategy into actionable requirements.
  • Engage strategic, cross-functional business units to champion and drive support for business plans and priorities; set standards, measure progress, and ensure resolution of escalated issues.
  • Set and communicate goals and objectives; analyze resources, costs, and forecasts to incorporate into business plans; obtain and distribute necessary resources.
  • Anticipate and remove performance obstacles; address performance gaps and implement contingency plans to ensure business objectives are accomplished.
  • Serve as a subject-matter expert and trusted source to executive leadership, offering influence and consultation in the development of broader organizational strategy.

Clinical Quality, Safety & Program Development

  • Serve as the subject matter expert on clinical quality improvement processes and regulations for internal/external executive stakeholders, sponsors, business owners, and external quality organizations.
  • Provide consultation on the interpretation and implementation of policies, regulations, and legislation, advising on long-term strategies to address changing regulatory environments.
  • Proactively engage internal and external committees and projects to determine necessary infrastructure changes to advance quality assurance initiatives and ensure long-term compliance.
  • Foster collaborative, results-oriented partnerships across clinical and administrative roles to influence organizational policy and maintain an adaptive compliance framework.
  • Forecast and direct future educational programs to raise awareness of changing regulation requirements, internal concerns, and database usage.
  • Identify and remove barriers to process improvement, weighing practical, technical, and organizational capability considerations when advising on policy changes.
  • Oversee the development of new clinical quality improvement programs by maintaining key stakeholder relationships and ensuring program sustainability.
  • Serve as an SME across health concepts, regulatory requirements, and change management principles to prioritize programs that optimize clinical quality, safety, and health outcomes.
  • Advocate for clinical programs and consult with executive management, technology stakeholders, and external vendors to develop the health system as a learning organization.

Grievance, Quality of Care Reviews & Surveillance

  • Direct the quality-of-care complaints and review process, representing the organization in grievance meetings, cases, reviews, referrals, and formal mechanisms.
  • Respond to and direct the preparation of documentation, records, and information requested for specific and highly sensitive patient case reviews.
  • Report trends in investigations and claims for red flags, appeal reasons, and overturns, advising leadership on strategic direction to reduce reoccurrences.
  • Define standards for the surveillance of quality improvement metrics, quality care incidents, and near misses according to established protocols to ensure consistent application of policies.

Infection Prevention & Control

  • Oversee infection prevention and control programs to improve employee and patient safety by presenting information from epidemiological investigations, simulations, and cluster research to executive stakeholders.
  • Serve as the primary contact during significant outbreak containment protocols and response efforts.
  • Consult with Administration on the infection control implications of architectural design, renovation, and facility construction.

Risk Management & Patient Safety

  • Direct risk management efforts by defining and presenting standards for corrective action plans identified through utilization reviews, clinical audits, claim denials, and satisfaction surveys.
  • Utilize information gathered from root cause analysis (RCA), failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA), and adverse event assessments to establish policies that mitigate future risk.
  • Define standards for health outcome analysis to continuously monitor oversight effectiveness.
  • Oversee patient safety programs by serving as the primary contact during significant event management and response to safety hazards, accidents, incidents, and threats.
  • Collaborate with executive management and external personnel to develop patient care and satisfaction programs that improve patient flow, clinical support, and transitions of care.

Data Management & Performance Improvement

  • Oversee systems, procedures, and forms to improve data management programs, using data to monitor and improve worker and patient safety programs.
  • Ensure the organization's quality improvement monitoring agenda integrates data management, pattern analysis, and practice trends into long-term strategic plans.
  • Act as an SME in interpreting and applying data from databases, vital statistics, discharge records, claims, and health sources to guide long-term strategy.
  • Present and advise on the application of formatted reports (e.g., infection control research, utilization reviews, population health needs analysis) to guide executive planning.

Regulatory Audits & Continuous Survey Readiness

  • Direct regulatory audits and survey efforts, serving as the primary liaison between government, regulatory bodies, and management during onsite visits and evaluations.
  • Establish long-term standards for audit documentation, information, tools, and reporting throughout the auditing process.
  • Forecast and establish continuous survey readiness activities to adapt to evolving regulatory requirements.

Care Optimization & Population Health

  • Define the future direction and standards for evaluating the cost-effectiveness, practicality, and appropriateness of medical care provided to patients.
  • Ensure case reviews are completed and followed up on, partnering with stakeholders to empower practitioners to adhere to standard operating procedures for timely care access.
  • Advocate with key stakeholders to resolve systemic concerns and ensure treatment plans meet patient needs promptly.
  • Define standards for population health needs to drive policy direction addressing community health concerns, transportation access, patient rights awareness, and no-show reductions.
  • Utilize patient case review results to advocate for policy and technology changes that improve overall health care utilization.

Qualifications & Requirements

Must-Have Requirements:

  • Active Registered Nurse (RN) License.
  • Executive Quality Leadership: Proven experience leading a Quality Department at the Director level or above.
  • Inpatient Experience: Extensive clinical and operational leadership experience in an inpatient hospital setting.
  • Onsite Availability: 100% onsite presence required for daily rounding across two hospital facilities in the Modesto service area.

Education & Experience:

  • Education: Master’s degree in Business, Health Care Administration, Public Administration, or a directly related field.
  • Total Healthcare Experience: Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in clinical and management roles within a health plan or multi-faceted healthcare system/multi-provider setting.
  • Leadership: Minimum 9 years in a leadership role (with or without direct reports).
  • Clinical & Administrative Background: Minimum 8 years in a clinical setting, healthcare administration, or directly related field.
  • Budgeting & Operations: Minimum 4 years of experience managing operational or project budgets.
  • Data & Systems: Minimum 6 years of experience utilizing databases and spreadsheets for data analysis.
  • Training: Minimum 4 years of experience delivering professional training programs.
  • General Health System Experience: Minimum 7 years in healthcare or a directly related field (combined with Master's degree).

Certifications:

  • Professional Healthcare Quality Certificate (e.g., CPHQ): Must be obtained within 24 months of hire.

title: Mechanical Design Engineering Intern
description:
Mechanical Engineering Internship

This internship will be part of an multi discipline team with collaborative projects and daily tasks to support continuous improvement and expansion of manufacturing production equipment.

  • Assist the facilities engineering team with continuous improvement and machine projects
  • Mechanical design
