title: Project Director, Evaluation and Measurement Strategy
description:
About the Position

The Project Director, Evaluation Strategy and Analytics will lead the development, monitoring, and evaluation of the Powerful Learning team’s data strategies, evaluation frameworks, and performance metrics. A primary focus of this role is demonstrating the overarching efficacy of our work, research, pilots, and services through rigorous data frameworks, automated dashboards, and academic-grade reports. This individual will serve as a liaison to internal teams, external research partners, and funders to ensure alignment between strategy, operations, and outcomes. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in applied research methods, data visualization, and data strategy to elevate our impact on the K-12 community.


Responsibilities

Research Design & Impact Efficacy

  • Design theory of change and logic models that clearly map inputs, activities, and outputs to define KPIs, implementation fidelity, and ROI tracking across various pilots, services, and research initiatives.
  • Lead research design for the team, including the development of longitudinal studies and control groups to demonstrate measurable and sustainable growth and prove the efficacy of our general work and programmatic interventions.
  • Serve as the primary research liaison (e.g., for Verizon Innovative Learning Schools and other partners) to develop strategies informed by programmatic goals and outcomes.
  • Implement internal evaluation systems to assess program fidelity, implementation quality, and internal operational effectiveness for new pilots and ongoing services.

Data Strategy & Automated Dashboards

  • Develop self-serve dashboards (Tableau, Power BI) to monitor the organization’s performance, operational health, and key outcomes across all research and service portfolios.
  • Streamline and automate data collection pipelines utilizing SQL and advanced survey tools (e.g., Qualtrics).
  • Collaborate on data strategies for building extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) pipelines that are scalable, cost-effective, and capable of real-time reporting.
  • Ensure the compliance of all software and tools with Digital Promise's data security and privacy guidelines.

Statistical Analysis & Reporting

  • Conduct complex statistical analysis utilizing R, Python, and/or SPSS to measure the efficacy of pilots and services, and to identify broader educational trends.
  • Produce academic-grade reports and technical writing required for grant compliance and institutional stakeholders, supporting annual proposals and continued funding efforts.
  • Convert complex statistical findings into pitch-ready metrics and engaging visualizations for Business Development and Partnerships to drive organizational growth and showcase the impact of our work.
  • Identify performance gaps and leverage evaluation insights to inform the continuous innovation process across Powerful Learning programming and services.

OKR & Performance Management

  • Facilitate the development, alignment, and tracking of OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) across teams to ensure strategic objectives are achieved.
  • Monitor quantitative and qualitative performance indicators to support external evaluations and internal continuous improvement.

Project Management

  • Effectively manages competing priorities, oversees external contractors and leads projects with a strict focus on quality, timelines, and adapting to changing needs.
  • Proactively keeps stakeholders informed, mitigates risks, and motivates cross-functional teams to achieve project milestones and advance Digital Promise’s equity goals.


Core Competencies

  • Analytical & Problem Solving: Utilizes data and research to adapt to changing project needs, troubleshoot issues, and develop effective solutions.
  • Relationship Management: Highly collaborative and organized, with a proven ability to build strong internal and external partnerships to drive execution.
  • Communication: Demonstrates active listening, clear written and verbal communication, and effective use of workplace tools (e.g., Slack, Asana) to foster strong interpersonal connections.
  • Continuous Learning: Actively pursues professional development, stays current with industry trends, and builds diverse internal and external networks.


Other duties as assigned




Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • A Bachelor's degree in information systems, statistics, data science, mathematics, or a related field is required (Master’s degree preferred).
  • A minimum of 7-10 years of experience in strategic planning, data science, performance measurement, or evaluation frameworks.
  • Experience working with data warehouses, data transformation tools, and writing technical documentation.
  • Exceptional project management skills with knowledge of K-12 school technology systems, applicable data privacy practices/laws, and tools like Asana, Salesforce, and Microsoft/Google suites.

Technical & Analytical Skills

  • Statistical Analysis: Strong proficiency in statistical programming and analysis utilizing R, Python, and/or SPSS.
  • Research Design: Proven background in advanced research methods, including longitudinal studies and control groups.
  • Data Visualization & BI: Extensive experience building self-serve, interactive dashboards using Tableau and Microsoft Power BI (Google Data Studio/Grafana a plus).
  • Database & Collection: Experience streamlining data collection using SQL and survey tools (Qualtrics preferred); understanding of relational databases (MySQL, Google BigQuery) and API integrations.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Deep knowledge of logic models, ROI tracking, implementation fidelity, and OKR methodologies.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Technical Writing: Exceptional ability to produce academic-grade reports and technical writing for grant compliance.
  • Translation & Pitching: Proven ability to translate complex data and statistical findings into pitch-ready insights for Business Development, Partnerships, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Contribute positively to the culture of the functional group, team and organization based on our team values and commitments

Impact Goals

  • Monitor, track, and report progress on relevant goals, for self and direct reports


At Digital Promise, we also seek candidates with:

  • A strong commitment to working toward Digital Promise’s mission and impact goals
  • An interest in redesigning learning systems to better serve those who are historically and systemically excluded
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional team members to ensure information is shared, projects are completed on time, and goals are reached.

Working Conditions

Digital Promise Global is a hybrid organization. Employees are expected to travel at least 4 times a year for in-person meetings and the annual staff retreat. Additional travel may be required based on role and responsibilities.

  • (a) Travel up to 15%
  • (b) Physical/Sensory Demands Fast-paced working environment. Extensive computer usage and online engagement & communication. Must be willing to build inclusive relationships and collaborate with employees at all levels within the organization and external partners.
  • (c) Special Provisions: Occasional work outside of normal business hours, such as weekends and evenings required.


Compensation

We consider candidate experience and location when determining where a candidate may fall within that range. Digital Promise Global offers a competitive total rewards package including coverage of 85% of health insurance premiums for employee coverage and 75% of health insurance premiums for dependent and family coverage, 15 vacation days, 12 sick days, 3% 401k employer contribution, 3% employer 401k match, and a flexible work environment.

The full-time salary range for the position is based on geographical regions, with exact salary depending on relevant experience.

California: $132,821-$144,541

DC Metro Area & NYC: $120,747-$131,401

National: $108,672-$118,261

To Apply

Please apply and submit your resume, cover letter, and salary requirements. Applicants are encouraged to submit their materials as soon as possible. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis until the search is successful.


Digital Promise is an equal opportunity employer and considers all applications without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex/gender, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, marital or veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

title: Firmware Engineer
description:
FIRMWARE ENGINEER

Monaco Enterprises, Inc., a Spokane based manufacturer of fire, mass notification, and security alarm systems, is seeking a professional, result-oriented, enthusiastic candidate to participate in designing, developing, and documenting electronic products, systems and circuits.

Monaco is expanding the Firmware Engineering team to develop the next generation of our proprietary embedded products. Successful candidates must be fluent in C/C++ programming, possess experience in embedded hardware applications, and have an interest in collaborating within a small product development team. Candidates should possess a willingness to utilize Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistance and tooling to support firmware development and problem-solving within the Firmware Engineering lifecycle.


Job Responsibilities:

A successful candidate will join the firmware engineering team with a focus on tasks to solve well-defined problems. The successful candidate will perform the following duties:

  • Analysis and troubleshooting of embedded operations and hardware interfaces

  • Discovery and design of firmware specifications and code modules

  • Development of firmware code for well-defined problems and established designs

  • Firmware documentation and QA activities

  • Utilize modern AI assistance and tooling to accelerate the problem-solving process.


Essential Functions:

  1. Capability to understand the operation of embedded hardware components

  2. Capability to analyze and troubleshoot embedded firmware operations and hardware interfaces

  3. Firmware discovery and design, including research and collaboration on technical specifications and methods

  4. Implementation of embedded firmware applications, hardware interface APIs, and test application suites

  5. Documentation of specifications, source code and product results

  6. Perform first level QA activities: identify test strategies, unit testing, resolve defects and perform root cause analysis

  7. Follow established firmware development processes and best practices

  8. Collaborate with engineering team members on new ideas, processes, and projects


Job Requirements:


  • BS degree in computer science, computer engineering, or related technology field (or equivalent experience)

  • Minimum of 3-4 years of professional experience outside of education

  • Experience working on embedded systems and interfacing with hardware components

  • Experience as an individual contributor throughout the embedded development lifecycle

Additional Knowledge, Skills and Technologies:

  • C/C++ programming languages

  • Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), Compilers, Debuggers, Processors such as:

    • Crossworks IDE, GCC toolchain

    • STM32 processors and hardware application layer

  • Git, GitFlow

  • Oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, meters, spectrum analyzers

  • Ability to read and comprehend electronic schematic diagram

  • Proficiency in leveraging AI assistance and emerging technologies to optimize firmware development workflows


Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Most hours spent standing and sitting. Occasional lifting up to 30 pounds. Constant fine finger manipulation, talking, hearing, and seeing. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, reaching, and repetitive motion. Occasional bending, crouching, grasping, and/or reaching above shoulder level and vibration.

Qualified applicants should apply before September 30, 2026 at to complete a job application for this job opportunity. The salary range for this position is $80,168.40 min. - $101,500 max. annually depending upon experience.

Monaco Enterprises offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and AD&D. We also offer flexible spending accounts and 401(k) Plan.

Applicants must be able to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and background check.

Monaco Enterprises is a Drug Free Workplace and Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants are considered regardless of ethnicity, nationality, veteran or disability status, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation or gender identity, or other protected status.

title: Regulatory Specialist - Wastewater Enterprise - SFPUC (5620)(166336)
description:
Under direction, the Regulatory Specialist assists in assuring that all San Francisco Public Utilities Commission operations, planning and development, property management, maintenance and maritime projects comply with federal, state and local laws and regulations and requirements. Essential functions of the position include: maintaining a working knowledge of the laws and regulations promulgated by various federal, state and local environmental and regulatory agencies; inspecting property, facilities, operations and construction activities to assure compliance with applicable laws and regulations; providing compliance assistance and/or enforcing environmental regulatory requirements; working well with others in multi-tasking situations; coordinating efforts among PUC staff, with other City departments and with regulatory and resources agencies to acquire the necessary authorizations to operate and to undertake new projects and maintenance activities; advising management of pertinent regulations affecting planned or in-progress projects and activities; collecting, reviewing and/or analyzing quantitative environmental data; reviewing and coordinating work of technical consultants; reviewing and/or preparing risk assessment, environmental compliance, environmental monitoring, and/or CEQA/NEPA reports; coordinating with other utilities, regulatory and planning agencies and the public; developing and administering project budgets and establishing and maintaining records and regulatory files. The nature of the job may require performing field investigations on foot in rough terrain and uneven surfaces; confined space entry; climbing and descending ladders and travel and work at distant facilities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The essential duties of this position include, but are not limited to:

1. Research and track all federal, state and local regulations that may affect the department.

2. Advise management of pertinent and timely regulations and make recommendations on the appropriate departmental actions. Provides regulatory expertise and permit processing support to managers and staff.

3. Reviews plans including planning and development plans, capital improvement project plans, property management & maintenance plans, and other related plans.

4. Performs or oversees consultants' performance of an environmental sample collection and analysis program.

5. Assists in making technical presentations to regulatory agencies and related public agencies.

6. Implements and assists in developing permit processing and inspection practices and procedures related to compliance with regulations affecting operations and facilities maintenance projects, property development and management and land-use programs to manage environmental liabilities.

7. Develops and maintains effective working relationships with a diverse staff.

8. Establishes and maintains permit files.

9. Drives city vehicles to various wastewater facilities and sites in the City and adjacent locations.

10. Performs all related duties as assigned.

Education:

A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in natural sciences, engineering, environmental or resource planning or a related field; AND

Experience:

Four years of verifiable work experience in environmental permitting and regulations; environmental investigations; environmental or other regulatory compliance; or environmental project management; or utility regulatory analysis.

License and Certification:

Possession of a valid California driver's license.

Substitution:

  • A Master's degree in natural sciences, engineering, environmental or resource planning, public policy, economics or a related field may substitute for one (1) year of work experience.
  • A law degree may substitute for one (1) year of work experience.
  • A PhD in natural sciences, engineering, environmental or resource planning, public policy, economics, or related field may substitute for two (2) years of work experience.

One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.) Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Desirable Qualifications: The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

  • Experience in municipal wastewater and stormwater systems, infrastructure, design or related projects.
  • Familiarity with and understanding of basic chemistry principles and nomenclature.
  • Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills, including use of pivot tables, lookup functions, conditional formatting, and conditional logic.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Please review our articles on Employment Application and Minimum Qualifications and Verification of Experience and/or Education for considerations taken when reviewing applications.

Verification: Applicants may be required to submit verification of qualifying education and experience at any point during the recruitment and selection process. If education verification is required, information on how to verify education requirements, including verifying foreign education credits or degree equivalency, can be found at How to Verify Education Requirements

Note: Falsifying one’s education, training, or work experience or attempted deception on the application may result in disqualification for this and future job opportunities with the City and County of San Francisco.

Applications completed improperly may be cause for ineligibility, disqualification or may lead to lower scores.

Selection Procedures: After application submission, candidates deemed qualified must complete all subsequent steps to advance in this selection process, which includes the following:

In-Person Written Examination (Weight: 100%): Candidates who meet minimum qualifications will be invited to complete the In-Person Written Examination. The purpose of the In-Person Written Examination is to evaluate the experience, knowledge, skills and abilities that candidates possess in job-related areas, which have been identified as critical for this position and include, but are not limited to:

  • Knowledge of federal, state and local laws, regulations and ordinances.
  • Knowledge of environmental regulatory processes.
  • Knowledge of environmental field and laboratory procedures.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships.
  • Ability to develop and implement strategies.
  • Ability to communicate verbally and in written format.
  • Ability to drive city vehicles while maintaining insurability.

A passing score must be achieved on the In-Person Written Examination in order to continue in the selection process and be placed on the eligible list.

Candidates will be placed on the eligible list in rank order according to their final score. Candidate scores on this examination may also be applied to other announcements involving other job titles, when directed by the Human Resources Director.

What else should I know?

Overview

SummaryORAU seeks an experienced Senior Advisor with deep expertise in healthcare payment design and value‑based care to support the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Innovation Center (CMMI).

The Senior Advisor will advise on the research, development, and refinement of innovative payment models authorized under Section 1115A(a)(3) of the Social Security Act. This role provides high‑level subject matter expertise across multiple models. The Senior Advisor will advise on model design, documentation, clearance materials, and when applicable data analysis to inform decisions across Medicaid and Medicare contexts.

Primary PurposeTo serve as a subject matter expert in payment model design, bringing extensive experience across Medicaid, Medicare, pediatric, and adult populations. The Senior Advisor will advise multiple model teams, support payment policy development, contribute to documentation and clearance, and offer analytical insight when needed.

Responsibilities

Key Duties and Responsibilities(Approx. 20 hours/week, remote work)

  • Payment Model Design & Support – Advise on the design of alternative payment model (APM) features, including upside/downside risk, global budgets, capitation, shared savings/losses, risk corridors, and other payment methodologies.
  • Model Documentation & Clearance – Review and offer insights on model design documents, clearance packages, concept papers, and public‑facing materials ensuring accuracy and alignment with policy intent.
  • Cross‑Model Advisory Support – Provide expertise across multiple model teams; participate in working sessions, advise on policy option development, and ensure alignment across programs.
  • Support for Policy Development & Stakeholder Engagement – Assist model teams in preparing for internal and external engagement, including stakeholder consultations, interviews, RFIs, and policy discussions.
  • Data Analysis & Modeling – Support or review quantitative modeling and financial simulations, benchmarking analyses, and evaluation of payment design parameters as needed.

Qualifications

Payment Design Expertise• Experience designing APMs, including global budgets, capitation, shared savings/losses, risk corridors, and financial risk arrangements.• Strong understanding of attribution methodologies for both total cost of care and episode‑based models.• Working knowledge of benchmark development approaches and risk adjustment methods (clinical, demographic, social risk).

Medicaid & Medicare Knowledge• Direct experience with Medicaid managed care rate development, capitation pricing, and HCBS payment methodologies.• Understanding of Medicare payment systems, CMS innovation model structures, and related rate-setting principles.

Pediatric & Adult Population Expertise• Background in pediatric payment models and Medicaid‑funded pediatric services.• Experience with adult populations across both Medicaid and Medicare.

Documentation & Policy Development

• Experience developing model memos, policy documents, clearance materials, and public‑facing technical materials.

Analytical Skills (Preferred)• Experience conducting financial simulations, benchmarking analyses, data evaluation, and quantitative modeling.

Education & Experience Requirements• Master’s degree in public health, health economics, or closely related field. • 10+ years of relevant experience in healthcare payment model design, value‑based care, and Medicaid/Medicare programs.

title: Mechanical Commissioning
description:

SUMMARY: Mechanical Commissioning within a data center construction environment.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Execution of commissioning activities on mechanical equipment and systems.
  • Systems Supported:
  • Industrial chilled and hot water systems, process cooling water, exhaust systems, and compressed air systems, including boilers, chillers, cooling towers, air handlers, roof top units, air compressors, fans, and motors.

Requirements:

title: Harvest Supervisor
description:
Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable fruits and vegetables under our Fresh and Foods divisions.   • 401(k) with company match

  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

  • 7 Company Paid Holidays

Purpose of Position:


Del Monte Foods is the Foods Division of Fresh Del Monte, a global grower, producer and marketer of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable produce. Del Monte Foods has a powerful portfolio of brands, including the iconic Del Monte®, Contadina® and S&W®. We are currently seeking a Harvest Supervisor or Harvest Operations Boss (HOB).


The Harvest Supervisor or Harvest Operations Boss (HOB) is responsible for maintaining, repairing, and supporting harvesting equipment while coordinating daily field operations during the production season. This position provides technical leadership to seasonal harvest personnel, ensures harvesting equipment is operating safely and efficiently, and supports field operations through preventative maintenance, equipment troubleshooting, work coordination, and inventory management. Performance is measured by equipment reliability, operational efficiency, safety, quality, and the successful coordination of seasonal harvest activities.


Accountabilities:


Harvest Equipment Maintenance & Repair

  • Coordinate daily harvest equipment readiness to support production schedules.
  • Assign daily work activities and coordinate priorities for seasonal harvest and cart operators.
  • Monitor field operations to ensure harvesting activities are completed safely and efficiently.
  • Communicate equipment status, operational concerns, and repair priorities with field leadership.
  • Support coordination between field operations and processing plant personnel.
  • Rebuild harvesters and dumpcarts during offseason to ensure performance is maintained at a high level.


Team Leadership & Employee Support

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, guidance, and technical support to seasonal harvest employees.
  • Train and mentor operators on equipment operation, maintenance awareness, and safe work practices.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, and effective communication throughout harvest operations.
  • Assist leadership with scheduling priorities and workforce coordination during harvest.
  • Support onboarding and training of new seasonal employees.

Equipment, Inventory & Administrative Support

  • Maintain equipment service records, CropTrak documentation, and other maintenance records.
  • Create purchase orders and coordinate parts procurement supporting harvest operations.
  • Monitor parts inventory and recommend replenishment to minimize equipment downtime.
  • Maintain organized field shop work areas, tools, and equipment.
  • Support special projects and additional operational assignments as business needs require.

Safety, Quality & Regulatory Compliance

  • Follow all company safety policies, field safety requirements, and operational procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with Lockout/Tagout procedures during maintenance and repair activities.
  • Identify, communicate, and correct unsafe conditions affecting employees or equipment.
  • Promote safe equipment operation while maintaining product quality and harvest efficiency.
  • Support compliance with company quality standards and field operational requirements.


Minimum Skills Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Agricultural equipment maintenance or heavy equipment mechanical experience.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience performing preventative maintenance and equipment repair.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • Ability to lead and coordinate seasonal employees while maintaining a safe work environment.
  • Basic computer skills for maintenance documentation, purchasing, and reporting.
  • Ability to work flexible schedules, overtime, weekends, and rotating shifts during harvest season.
  • Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience that provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities will be considered.
  • Previous leadership or lead worker experience.
  • CDL preferred.
  • Experience with agricultural harvesting equipment.
  • Experience with maintenance management systems or CropTrak.
  • Knowledge of preventative maintenance programs and inventory control.
  • Welding, torching, and fabrication skills a plus.

***Please note: This position does not qualify for relocation expenses.***

Our diverse product portfolio also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts—available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Venice, Florida.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Venice area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Venice requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

description:
A Recycling Line Picker is responsible for sorting and separating recyclable materials from a moving conveyor belt in a recycling or waste processing facility. The role helps ensure recyclable materials are recovered efficiently while maintaining safety and quality standards.

  • Sort and separate recyclable materials such as paper, cardboard, plastics, metals, and glass from a conveyor belt.
  • Remove non-recyclable, contaminated, or hazardous items from the waste stream.
  • Maintain quality standards by ensuring materials are correctly segregated.
  • Monitor the conveyor line and report equipment faults or operational issues.
  • Keep the work area clean and free from hazards.
  • Follow all health, safety, and environmental procedures.
  • Assist with housekeeping duties and general plant operations as required.
  • Wear and properly use personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Work effectively as part of a team to meet production targets.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced industrial environment.
  • Good attention to detail and ability to identify different recyclable materials.
  • Physically fit and able to stand for extended periods.
  • Ability to follow safety instructions and procedures.
  • Reliable, punctual, and team-oriented.
  • Previous experience in recycling, waste management, manufacturing, or warehouse operations is advantageous but not essential.
Working Conditions
  • Indoor recycling or waste processing facility.
  • Exposure to noise, dust, odors, and varying temperatures.
  • Standing for long periods and performing repetitive tasks.
  • Shift work, including evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays, may be required.
Typical PPE Requirements
  • Safety boots
  • High-visibility clothing
  • Gloves
  • Safety glasses
  • Hearing protection (where required)
  • Dust mask or respiratory protection (where required)

title: Supervisor, Power Control
description:
Overview

Supervisor, Power Control

Lead the team that helps keep our communities connected.

Cobb EMC is seeking an experienced Supervisor, Power Control to oversee the monitoring, operation, control, and integrity of our electrical distribution system. In this critical leadership role, you will guide Power Control operations, support outage restoration, coordinate with field personnel, and help ensure members receive timely, accurate, and courteous service

Schedule:Rotating schedule including nights, evenings, weekends, and holidays

Benefits:

  • Company paid Health Insurance Premiums!
  • Insurance is effective your first day of employment
  • Retirement Security Pension plan!
  • Automatic 7% Company paid contribution to 401k with additional matching!
  • Annual Bonus Program!
  • Tuition and Certification reimbursement!
  • Learn more HERE

To learn more about Cobb EMC visit our website at www.cobbemc.com

Responsibilities

What You’ll Do

Lead Power Control Operations

  • Oversee the safe and effective operation of the electrical distribution system.
  • Originate, review, approve, and issue switching orders.
  • Monitor system conditions, identify and isolate faults, and coordinate power restoration.
  • Analyze SCADA alarms and take appropriate action based on system conditions.
  • Respond to emergencies involving transformers, distribution lines, and other system equipment.
  • Coordinate with engineers, planners, field personnel, and utility workers regarding clearances, switching orders, and system changes.
  • Partner with the SCADA/AMI team to help maintain accurate field-device information.
  • Maintain current knowledge of evolving system-protection schemes.

Maintain Accurate Records and Schedules

  • Monitor and maintain records associated with SCADA, control-room equipment, weather radar, radio communications, and the video wall map board.
  • Maintain required daily operational and security logs.
  • Ensure radio logs comply with FCC regulations.
  • Oversee the proper processing of outage reports.
  • Provide accurate monthly and annual trouble data for senior management.
  • Develop and maintain the department’s 24/7 rotating work schedule.

Support Members and Field Teams

  • Monitor communications and ensure important information reaches the appropriate field locations.
  • Report unusual conditions to the appropriate personnel.
  • Ensure member inquiries are addressed promptly, courteously, and professionally.
  • Route complaints to the appropriate personnel during normal business hours.

Strengthen Operational Readiness

  • Monitor system loads and automated field devices.
  • Help oversee the operation of SCADA equipment.
  • Develop and maintain written Power Control procedures.
  • Create and maintain initial and ongoing training for System Operators.
  • Implement storm procedures when required.
  • Demonstrate Power Control functions to touring groups.
  • Maintain updated company information for public-relations purposes.

Develop and Lead the Team

  • Manage hiring, promotions, training, documentation, and other employment matters for department staff.
  • Coach employees through hands-on guidance, reinforcement, and continued learning.
  • Manage daily workloads and employee schedules.
  • Conduct performance planning and review sessions.
  • Promote fair and consistent treatment across the department.
  • Actively support Equal Employment Opportunity principles

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

High School or equivalent.

Minimum one year experience as System Operator III or equivalent. Excellent working knowledge of line feeds, system locations, interpretation of system maps, work order procedures, corporate policies and procedures.

Good working knowledge of FCC rules and regulations.

Successful completion of required training courses and assessments for advancement to this position.

SKILLS: Proficient with SCADA, OMS and the current Cobb EMC software for historical record keeping and reporting

Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Demonstrated supervisory skills.

Ability to effectively communicate via two-way radio.

Ability to effectively perform under pressure and in emergency situations.

Proficient in operating, testing and troubleshooting the Cobb EMC Electrical Distribution System including substation equipment, generators, and automated field device equipment via the SCADA system.

Proficiency with personal computers (i.e., current Windows operating system, Microsoft Word and Excel).

Proficient in maintaining accurate reports and records.

Proficient in performing outage analysis by feeder, recloser and other devices

Proficient in operating, testing and troubleshooting the Cobb EMC Electrical Distribution System including substation equipment, generators, and automated field device equipment via the SCADA system.

Possess valid Integrated Transmission System (ITS) Operator’s Certification.

PREFERRED:

Associates Degree in Electrical, Electronics or related field

Previous Supervisory Experience

CORE Values:

Put People First

Care, listen and connect. Think team, not self. Respect and value differences.

Stay Safe

No shortcuts. See the big picture, no tunnel vision. Look out for each other

Innovate

Embrace change. Think big and bold. Be part of the solution.

Own It

Own your attitude, actions and words. Find a way. No BCD. Never stop learning.

title: Crewleader Cookroom
description:
Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable fruits and vegetables under our Fresh and Foods divisions. Our diverse product portfolio proudly bears the Del Monte® brand and also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts - available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.


Purpose of Position:


Del Monte Foods is the Foods Division of Fresh Del Monte, a global grower, producer and marketer of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable produce. Del Monte Foods has a powerful portfolio of brands, including the iconic Del Monte®, Contadina® and S&W®. We are currently seeking a Cookroom Crew Leader. The Cookroom Crew Leader is responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and operating cookroom equipment used in root crop and green bean processing operations. This role supports safe, efficient, and compliant production of commercially sterile canned products that meet company quality, food safety, and productivity standards.


The Cookroom Crew Leader works closely with production, maintenance, quality, sanitation, and operations teams to maintain cookroom performance, minimize downtime, and support seasonal employee training. This role functions primarily as a skilled maintenance mechanic within the cookroom area while also providing day-to-day guidance to seasonal employees during processing season. The position does not have direct reports but is expected to support work coordination, training, and maintenance documentation within the department.


Accountabilities:


Equipment Maintenance and Troubleshooting

  • Maintain, troubleshoot, repair, and operate cookroom equipment, conveyors, can tracks, and related systems.
  • Diagnose equipment failures and complete repairs to minimize downtime and support production schedules.
  • Perform preventative maintenance activities, equipment inspections, lubrication, and minor fabrication work.
  • Assist with equipment changeovers, startup activities, shutdowns, and seasonal line preparation.
  • Support installation of replacement parts, equipment upgrades, and process improvements.
  • Work closely with maintenance and production teams to prioritize repairs and maintain operational readiness.
  • Track maintenance work performed and complete required labor hour, repair, and maintenance documentation accurately.

Cookroom Operations and Product Certification

  • Operate cookroom equipment in a manner that maintains compliance with established procedures, product specifications, and sterilization requirements.
  • Complete required documentation accurately and maintain product certification records.
  • Review cookroom logs, temperature records, weight checks, seam integrity records, and other production documentation for accuracy.
  • Support internal audits, inspections, and verification activities related to food safety and product quality.
  • Maintain compliance with Better Processing School requirements and cookroom certification standards.
  • Assist with corrective actions, deviation reviews, and documentation updates as needed.

Employee Support and Training

  • Train and guide seasonal employees on cookroom equipment, procedures, food safety, and work expectations.
  • Provide day-to-day direction to seasonal employees within the cookroom area during production season.
  • Reinforce safety, quality, attendance, productivity, and housekeeping expectations.
  • Support onboarding and training of new employees within the department.
  • Promote teamwork, communication, accountability, and cross-functional support across the facility.

Safety, Food Safety, and Quality

  • Follow all company safety policies, GMPs, food safety requirements, and quality standards.
  • Maintain safe operation of cookroom equipment and work areas.
  • Support lockout/tagout, confined space, hot work, and chemical handling procedures.
  • Report unsafe conditions, equipment issues, injuries, and product quality concerns promptly.
  • Maintain clean and organized work areas within the cookroom department.
  • Support compliance with product certification requirements and commercially sterile food processing standards.


Minimum Skills Required:


  • Mechanical aptitude required.
  • Welding and torch cutting experience required.
  • Basic knowledge of electricity, hydraulics, and steam systems required.
  • Good verbal and written communication skills required.
  • Basic computer skills required.
  • Valid driver’s license required.
  • Ability to lead and train employees effectively.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to use a variety of hand tools and maintenance equipment.
  • Ability to provide personal tools needed to perform assigned duties.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to work all shifts and overtime as needed.
  • Ability to crawl, squat, kneel, bend, twist, reach, climb, and work overhead.
  • Ability to work in hot, humid, and changing plant environments.
  • Ability to maintain strong attendance and follow all company policies
  • Post-high school mechanical maintenance training or technical education.
  • 3–5 years of maintenance, production, or cookroom experience.
  • Experience working in a food manufacturing or canning environment.
  • Experience leading seasonal employees or training new employees.
  • Experience with product certification programs and documentation requirements.
  • Experience with Better Processing School or commercially sterile food production requirements.
  • Experience with continuous improvement, process improvement, or equipment reliability initiatives.
  • Equivalent combinations of education, mechanical experience, maintenance experience, production experience, leadership experience, and food manufacturing experience that provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities will be considered.


***Please note: This position does not qualify for relocation expenses.***


Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh and fresh cut fruits and vegetables. Our diverse product portfolio also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts—available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.


We are committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace and are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Fresh Del Monte and its affiliates do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, gender, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We also participate in E-Verify* where applicable, to ensure employment authorization eligibility. Driven by our core values—Excellence, Care, Passion, Trust, and Creativity—we invite you to explore our career opportunities and join our FRESH team.

title: Scenic Project Manager
description:
Overview

PRG is the world’s leading technology provider within the entertainment and events industry. Our mission is to bring together the power of our people with our production and rental expertise to deliver unforgettable events. PRG has the largest inventory of production equipment for hire and offers a complete 360-degree range of services to clients within the live events industry. These include music touring and festivals, TV & Film, Theatre, Sports and E-sports and Corporate live events. Our clients and partners rely on PRG’s innovation, experience and in-depth expertise in video, lighting, rigging, staging, virtual productions, and set & automation systems to bring their creative visions to life. With 38 offices located in North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia, PRG offers the ability to provide services worldwide by collaborating with our local partners.

Responsibilities

The Project Manager – Scenic is responsible for the planning, coordination, and execution of scenic fabrication and live event projects, including corporate events, trade shows, exhibits, permanent installations, concert touring, residencies, and sporting events.

Working closely with Account Executives, Sales, Technical Design, Engineering, Project Coordinators, and Operations, the Project Manager supports projects from initial scope development through final execution and closeout. This role is responsible for translating project Scope of Work into detailed execution plans while ensuring projects are delivered on time, on budget, and aligned with client expectations.The Project Manager serves as a primary point of contact throughout the project lifecycle and is expected to maintain clear communication with clients, vendors, and internal stakeholders while providing a high level of customer service both internally and externally.

This position plays a key role in coordinating logistics, labor, budgeting, scheduling, change management, and operational execution while maintaining accuracy within internal project management and asset tracking systems.

Project size, complexity, and level of responsibility may vary depending on experience level and business unit requirements.

It is the policy of PRG to provide excellent customer service both internally and externally. Employees are expected to perform all duties and responsibilities in alignment with this standard at all times. Additional related duties may be assigned as required.

  • Develop and maintain detailed project plans in collaboration with Account Executives, Technical Product Managers, Project Coordinators, and Operations teams
  • Manage scenic projects from award through closeout, ensuring delivery aligns with scope, budget, timeline, and client expectations
  • Communicate regularly with clients regarding project status, schedules, deliverables, inclusions, exclusions, and scope changes
  • Collaborate with Sales and Account Executives to identify opportunities for additional services and value-added solutions
  • Coordinate with Technical Design, Engineering, and Fabrication teams to align project execution strategies and technical requirements
  • Participate in project pricing reviews (Deal Desk) and assist with quote revisions and change order management
  • Track and manage project change orders, approvals, and scope modifications, ensuring all impacted stakeholders are informed
  • Maintain integrity and accuracy of project data within Asset Management Systems (AMS) and other internal tracking systems throughout the project lifecycle
  • Monitor project financial performance, labor actuals, vendor costs, and project budgets, including participation in month-end reconciliation processes
  • Ensure equipment schedules, return dates, and project logistics are accurate and updated within internal systems
  • Maintain complete and accurate project documentation, including schedules, budgets, drawings, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, logistics documents, and subcontractor agreements
  • Coordinate project logistics, transportation, vendor activities, and third-party services
  • Determine project labor requirements, develop labor schedules, and track labor actuals throughout project execution
  • Coordinate with labor teams regarding staffing, travel, accommodations, and per diem requirements
  • Ensure timely and accurate submission of project paperwork, labor reports, expenses, and timesheets Participate in client presentations, site visits, and project meetings as required
  • Support or oversee on-site execution and management of show labor as required
  • Promote and reinforce job site safety standards while addressing operational and safety concerns as needed
  • Lead project closeout activities, including reconciliation, post-show reporting, and client follow-up
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives and implementation of updated project management processes and procedures

Qualifications

Qualifications / Knowledge & Skills

  • Strong project management skills with exceptional attention to detail
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
  • Ability to read and interpret contract scope, technical drawings, plans, and project documentation
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize multiple projects under tight deadlines
  • Creative problem-solving mindset with the ability to adapt in fast-paced environments
  • Working knowledge of scenic fabrication, scenic automation, engineering, lighting, audio, video, rigging, labor coordination, and live event production workflows
  • Experience managing budgets, vendor relationships, client communication, and conflict resolution
  • General understanding of labor regulations and job site safety requirements
  • Ability to lead, collaborate, and work effectively across multiple teams and departments
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and project management software
  • Experience using Asset Management Systems (AMS) or similar project tracking systems
  • Some travel, including international travel, may be required

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position approximately 50% of the time
  • Must be able to bend, climb stairs, and continuously stand or walk for extended periods as required
  • Must be able to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
  • Must be able to communicate effectively in both written and verbal forms
  • Hearing and vision within normal ranges are required for communication, reviewing drawings, and inspecting project work

Other Duties

  • Understanding of and compliance with company policies

Travel Required

  • Some travel required depending on project needs • Must have a valid passport • Must have a valid driver’s license

Required Education & Experience

  • Technical education and/or training in scenic fabrication, live event production, or related disciplines preferred
  • 5+ years of experience working in the entertainment or live events industry

EEO and Disclosure

PRG is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

PRG is a drug-free work environment, pre-employment testing will be required.

Production Resource Group LLC participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

PRG cares about the safety of our employees and applicants. PRG does not use chat rooms for job searches or communications. PRG will never request personal information via informal chat platforms or unsecure email. PRG will never ask for money or an exchange of money, banking or other personal information prior to an in-person interview. Be aware of potential scams while job seeking. For information on job scams, visit, https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/JobScams or file a complaint at https://www.ftccomplaintassistant.gov/.

title: Legal Interns Summer 2027

description:
CEO Lawyer Summer 2027 Personal Injury Attorney Internship Program

For Rising 3L Law Students

Only 5 Positions Available!

This is more than an Internship. It's a Direct Path to Becoming a PI Attorney


CEO Lawyer is seeking five exceptional rising 3L law students to join our Summer 2027 Personal Injury Attorney Internship Program.

This program is designed to identify, train, and develop the next generation of elite plaintiff attorneys through meaningful legal work, direct mentorship, and a structured career pathway that extends well beyond the summer.

Successful interns will have the opportunity to:

  • Complete the Summer 2027 internship program
  • Continue working part-time during their 3L year
  • Receive ongoing mentorship and professional development
  • Sit for the Bar Exam following graduation
  • Transition into a full-time attorney position upon successful bar admission

Unlike traditional internships that end with a reference letter, our goal is to develop future members of our legal team.

Why CEO Lawyer?

Real Personal Injury Litigation Experience

From day one, you will work alongside experienced attorneys on real personal injury cases involving:

  • Motor vehicle accidents
  • Catastrophic injuries
  • Wrongful death claims
  • Premises liability matters
  • Complex injury litigation

You will gain exposure to every stage of case development, including legal research, discovery, demand preparation, medical record analysis, damages evaluation, and litigation strategy.

Direct Access to Industry Leaders

Learn directly from attorneys with more than 75 years of combined personal injury litigation experience.

This is not a program where interns observe from the sidelines. You will receive hands-on mentorship, real-world feedback, and meaningful opportunities to develop practical legal skills that prepare you for attorney practice.

A Career Path Before Graduation

Most law students spend their final year hoping to secure employment after graduation.

Our internship program is designed to identify future attorneys early and invest in their long-term success. High-performing interns may have the opportunity to continue working with the firm through law school and transition into a full-time attorney role after bar admission.


What You'll Do

  • Assist attorneys and legal staff with case preparation and litigation support
  • Conduct legal research and draft memoranda, demand letters, and other legal documents under attorney supervision
  • Review and organize medical records, discovery materials, and case documentation
  • Track deadlines and assist with case management workflows
  • Participate in client intake, case evaluation, and strategy discussions as appropriate
  • Prepare exhibits, summaries, and supporting documentation for legal proceedings
  • Communicate professionally with clients, medical providers, experts, opposing counsel, and third parties as directed
  • Observe and support mediations, depositions, hearings, and other aspects of personal injury litigation
  • Utilize Microsoft Office and firm case-management systems to support day-to-day legal operations
  • Collaborate with attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and operations professionals to deliver exceptional client service
  • Demonstrate professionalism, initiative, accountability, and a commitment to continuous learning

Qualifications

Required

  • Current law student who will be a Rising 3L in Summer 2027
  • Enrolled at an ABA-accredited law school
  • Expected to sit for the Uniform Bar Examination (UBE) following graduation
  • Strong academic performance and demonstrated interest in Personal Injury Law
  • Excellent written, verbal, analytical, and organizational skills
  • High level of professionalism, reliability, and attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work collaboratively while also handling assignments independently
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint)
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately
  • Must successfully complete all firm onboarding requirements and background screening
  • Authorized to work in the United States

Preferred

  • Prior experience working in a law firm, legal clinic, judicial internship, or litigation environment
  • Interest in pursuing a long-term career in plaintiff-side personal injury law
  • Bilingual or multilingual communication skills

title: Therapy Aide
description:
With traumatic brain injury, life changes in an instant. For us, the is no greater reward than easing human suffering and helping people put their lives back together. As a Clinic/ Therapy Aide I or II, you will play a critical role in transforming lives and helping individuals regain their independence and quality of life.


At CNS, we are a community of "PATHfinders" who work together to find every path possible for our patients to reach their maximum independence and quality of life. We create a supportive work environment through selflessness, innovation, and hard work. We take work very seriously, but we also enjoy a great atmosphere of fun and professional development, and we are committed to promoting a rich environment for each other to thrive through collaboration and empowerment.

Full time, part time and PRN availability

Responsibilities

The Clinic/Therapy Aide I or II will perform necessary clerical duties and with assist with patient treatments as directed. Ability to manage multiple tasks and to work with other staff and departments within a team to ensure quality patient care. Primary responsibilities are assisting with activities in a variety of departments. Duties may include answering phones, and clerical duties including data entry. May accompany patients to appointments. Work is full time during the weekdays, Monday-Friday 7:00am to 4:00pm. Work is performed at the clinic with occasional work in the community or residential site. Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Assists with the implementation of patient treatment programs in the Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and Speech/Education Departments according to legal guidelines and under the direct supervision of a licensed therapist. Requires lifting, handling, carrying and manipulating patients, equipment and supplies weighing up to 150 pounds.
  • Requires ability to use proper lifting techniques, good balance, and sufficient strength to provide patients with virtually all levels of assistance from standby to maximum assistance. Must have adequate endurance, motor, visual and cognitive skills to demonstrate and/or assist with therapeutic exercises, activities of daily living, social skills, transfers and handling therapeutic equipment.
  • Performs toilet and chair transfers without assistance for patients up to 150 pounds utilizing approved transfer techniques. Transfer techniques include standing, walking, stooping, bending, kneeling, squatting, lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling. Patients requiring moderate to maximum assistance and weighing over 200 pounds are lifted and/or transferred by two persons.
  • Performs documentation such as daily progress notes, treatment modules, and behavior modification documentation. Performs organizational/administrative projects such as filing and light typing. Sets up and dismantles patient charts in a timely manner.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

title: Constr Superintendent III
description:
Overview

Are you looking for a highly rewarding opportunity that provides extensive career growth opportunity? Next150 Construction is seeking a motivated Construction Superintendent III to lead complex trade scopes or multiple crews within a major project, providing direct field leadership to ensure work is executed in accordance with approved scope, safety requirements, quality standards, and schedule commitments. This role supports self-performance operations while collaborating closely with the Lead Superintendent on jobsite logistics, resource planning, and sequencing, mentoring junior field leaders, workforce coordination, and union engagement while assisting with advanced planning and execution activities. This position also supports the implementation of field technology, sustainability practices, and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance safety, quality, and operational efficiency.

Next 150 Construction offers employees multi-dimensional training opportunities through a number of resources for those that are early in their career. While managing your responsibilities to the project, you will be able to enroll in trainings through our award-winning Gilbane University to build leadership and technical skills. In addition, you would work with an experienced team which provides you with the opportunity to learn new industry skills every day.

Responsibilities

  • Leads and coordinates assigned trade contractors, self-performed crews, and field activities to ensure work is executed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with approved scope, schedule, and quality requirements
  • Develops, documents, and communicates detailed work plans for assigned scopes and ensures compliance with approved work plans and field directives
  • Maintains a thorough understanding of contract documents, drawings, specifications, and coordination requirements to support effective trade-level planning; verifies that all required permits, inspections, and compliance documentation are in place for assigned work areas
  • Acts as the primary Next 150 safety representative for assigned scopes, enforces applicable safety policies and procedures, and supports a strong safety-first culture in the field
  • Oversees quality control for assigned trades, conducts inspections, documents findings, and implements corrective actions to maintain compliance with project and company standards
  • Leads contractor meetings related to assigned scopes and coordinates activities with field and project leadership
  • Maintains accurate daily field reports, safety documentation, and production records using Procore and other required systems
  • Creates and manages trade-level schedules and implements contingency plans to maintain commitments and mitigate impacts; communicates schedule status, constraints, and updates to the applicable team
  • Plans and manages jobsite logistics for assigned scopes, including access, material flow, temporary facilities, and sequencing
  • Assists in resolving jurisdictional disputes and field-level conflicts within assigned scopes
  • Tracks production, labor hours, and productivity metrics, and reports variances to field leadership

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Nearby Field, California.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Nearby Field area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Nearby Field requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Mobile Crisis Clinician
description:
Mobile Crisis Clinician

Pay Grade: 8

Under the general supervision of the Mobile Crisis Director, the Mobile Crisis Clinician performs direct clinical services, including crisis intervention and de-escalation for individuals of all ages.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Performs direct clinical services, including crisis intervention and de-escalation for individuals of all ages.
  • Performs indirect clinical services, including, timely and complete case documentation following DWIHN policies and procedures.
  • Documents all crisis intervention activities in the electronic medical record to ensure accuracy of records and regulatory compliance.
  • Provides coordination and follow-up for clients and assists in obtaining necessary additional services, coordinating with the Access Center or the patient’s current outpatient therapy plan.
  • Maintains clinical documentation that is accurate and up to date, including assessments, progress notes, crisis/safety plans, and other required documentation.
  • Participates in agency and system staff meetings.
  • Participates in community meetings.
  • Collaborates with schools, law enforcement and other organizations.
  • Assists individuals/families in developing natural supports to increase success in the community.
  • Provides counseling, guidance, support, resources, and encouragement to individuals served so that they can learn to take responsibility for and actively participate in their own recovery.
  • Provides on call duties as needed which include but are not limited to responding to calls from mobile crisis clinicians and peers.
  • Provides mobile crisis services in the community.
  • Performs related duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSA’S)

  • Knowledge of DWIHN policies, procedures, and practices.
  • Knowledge of the DWIHN provider network and community resources.
  • Knowledge of the Michigan Mental Health Code.
  • Knowledge of MDHHS policies, rules, regulations, and procedures.
  • Knowledge of Federal policies, rules, regulations, and procedures as it relates to DWIHN.
  • Knowledge of Mobile Crisis principles and practices.
  • Knowledge of Crisis Services principles and practices.
  • Knowledge of behavioral health and mental health principles and practices.
  • Knowledge of the Michigan Medicaid Provider Manual.
  • Knowledge of MHWIN.
  • Knowledge of the LOCUS model.
  • Knowledge of the clinical care process (screening, assessment, treatment planning, case management and continuing care).
  • Knowledge of and ability to use screening and assessment tools for behavioral health services.
  • Knowledge of the Adult continuum of care for all disability designations (I/DD, SMI, Co-Occurring Disorder).
  • Knowledge of adult’s services; Outpatient, Co- occurring services, CM, ACT, Supported Employment and Med Drop.
  • Knowledge of Integrated Care services for behavioral health patients.
  • Knowledge of medical and behavioral health practices and terminology.
  • Knowledge of compliance standards.
  • Knowledge of Medical Necessity Criteria for Behavioral Health Services.
  • Knowledge of SUD guidelines and licensing certifications.
  • Knowledge of crisis training and experience in de-escalation, i.e., suicide prevention, development of crisis plans, trauma informed care, etc.
  • Assessment and evaluation skills.
  • Conflict Resolution skills
  • Computer skills.
  • Organizational skills.
  • Report writing skills.
  • Negotiation skills.
  • Problem Solving skills.
  • Decision Making skills.
  • Interpersonal Skills.
  • Communication skills.
  • Collaboration skills.
  • Multitasking skills.
  • Teamwork Skills.
  • Ability to communicate orally.
  • Ability to communicate in writing.
  • Ability to work effectively with others.
  • Ability to work with an ethnically, linguistically, culturally, economically and socially diverse population.
  • Judgement/Reasoning ability


REQUIRED EDUCATION:

A Master’s Degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, Human Services, the Social Services, or a related field.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:

One (1) year of full-time paid professional clinical experience working in crisis services or a closely related area.


REQUIRED LICENSE(S).

A Valid State of Michigan clinical licensure: RN, LMSW, LMHC, LPC, LLP or PhD.

(A limited license will be accepted).

A Valid State of Michigan Driver’s License with a safe and acceptable driving record.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Employees in this classification must travel throughout Wayne County. Candidates will be required to travel to homes, community-based settings, hospitals, schools, courts, etc.

Mobile Crisis Operations is a 24/7 unit. There will be positions offered for the Day Shift (7-3); Afternoon Shift (3-11) and the Midnight Shift (11-7). Candidates must be able to work a flexible schedule.
