title: Seamer Technician
description:
Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable fruits and vegetables under our Fresh and Foods divisions. Our diverse product portfolio proudly bears the Del Monte® brand and also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts - available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.


Benefits We Offer Include:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance
  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • 7 Company Paid Holidays
  • 24/7 Telemedicine & Employee Assistance Program
  • Optional voluntary benefits (legal, accident, identity protection)
  • Eligibility on the first of the month following your hire date


Purpose of Position:


Del Monte Foods is the Foods Division of Fresh Del Monte, a global grower, producer and marketer of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable produce. Del Monte Foods has a powerful portfolio of brands, including the iconic Del Monte®, Contadina® and S&W®. We are currently seeking a Insights & Analytics Manager.


The Seamer Technician is responsible for performing routine inspection, measurement, and evaluation of can seams to verify package integrity and ensure finished product meets established food safety, quality, and manufacturing specifications. This position collects production samples, performs visual seam inspections and destructive seam tear-downs, measures critical seam characteristics, calculates required values, documents results, and promptly communicates deviations to Production and Quality personnel.


The Seamer Technician works closely with Production, Quality Assurance, and other plant personnel to identify seam-related concerns and support timely corrective action. Performance is measured by the accuracy and timeliness of seam evaluations and documentation, adherence to established sampling and testing procedures, and compliance with food safety, quality, and workplace safety requirements.


Accountabilities:


Seam Inspection & Testing

  • Collect representative can samples from assigned production lines at established frequencies.
  • Perform visual inspections of can seams and overall container integrity.
  • Prepare cans for destructive seam evaluation using approved tools and procedures.
  • Perform complete seam tear-downs to evaluate critical seam characteristics.
  • Measure seam length, thickness, countersink, body hook, cover hook, and other required seam dimensions.
  • Calculate seam overlap and other required seam measurements.
  • Compare inspection and measurement results against established product and container specifications.
  • Verify measurements and calculations are complete and accurate before documenting results.
  • Perform additional package integrity or quality checks as trained and assigned.


Quality Monitoring & Response

  • Monitor seam inspection results for conditions that may indicate developing equipment, container, or process issues.
  • Immediately report measurements, calculations, or visual observations outside established specifications to Production and Quality leadership.
  • Clearly communicate seam-related concerns to appropriate personnel to support timely investigation and corrective action.
  • Support additional sampling or seam evaluations following adjustments, deviations, or other quality events as directed.
  • Assist Production and Quality personnel with determining whether subsequent seam checks meet established specifications.
  • Maintain awareness of applicable product quality and food safety requirements while performing seam evaluations.

Documentation & Data Integrity

  • Accurately document all seam inspection measurements, calculations, observations, and results.
  • Enter required seam inspection information into applicable computer systems.
  • Complete required paperwork, logs, and reports accurately and within established timelines.
  • Maintain accurate, neat, legible, and traceable quality records.
  • Verify documentation is complete before submitting or retaining records according to established procedures.
  • Communicate documentation discrepancies or unusual results to appropriate leadership.

Sampling & Quality Support

  • Follow established sampling frequencies, procedures, and testing requirements.
  • Handle production samples appropriately to prevent inaccurate or compromised test results.
  • Support additional quality checks and testing after receiving required training.
  • Assist Quality and Production personnel with product or packaging evaluations as needed.
  • Support investigations involving seam integrity or container-related quality concerns.
  • Assist with training other qualified employees in seam inspection and tear-down procedures when assigned.

Equipment, Tools & Work Area

  • Properly use seam inspection, measuring, and can tear-down equipment.
  • Handle cans, lids, measuring devices, and testing tools safely and according to established procedures.
  • Maintain seam inspection equipment and work areas in clean and orderly condition.
  • Identify damaged, malfunctioning, or inaccurate testing equipment and report concerns promptly.
  • Dispose of product, cans, lids, and testing materials according to established procedures.
  • Support general housekeeping and sanitation activities within assigned work areas.

Operational Support

  • Coordinate sampling activities with production operations to ensure required checks are completed without unnecessary disruption.
  • Communicate effectively with Production, Quality Assurance, and other plant personnel.
  • Assist production personnel with work activities as operational needs require.
  • Maintain flexibility to support changing production schedules, products, and assigned lines.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Safety, Food Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all company safety policies, GMPs, food safety requirements, quality procedures, and regulatory standards.
  • Use appropriate PPE, including required head, hearing, eye, hand, and foot protection.
  • Use appropriate hand protection when handling hot cans or performing destructive seam evaluations.
  • Follow established safe procedures when opening cans and performing seam tear-downs.
  • Maintain awareness of wet or slippery floors, forklift traffic, moving equipment, pinch points, and other manufacturing hazards.
  • Follow Lockout/Tagout requirements when applicable.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and obstruction-free work areas.
  • Report injuries, near misses, unsafe conditions, quality concerns, and equipment issues promptly.


Minimum Skills Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Basic mathematical skills are necessary to perform measurements and calculations.
  • Basic computer and data-entry skills.
  • Ability to accurately perform detailed measurements and calculations.
  • Ability to follow established sampling, testing, food safety, and quality procedures.
  • Ability to maintain accurate, neat, and legible records.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify measurements or conditions outside established specifications.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with Production, Quality, and other plant personnel.
  • Ability to work effectively with minimal supervision after completion of required training.
  • Ability to work day or night schedules and extended production-season hours as required.
  • Previous manufacturing experience.
  • Previous food-manufacturing or quality-control experience.
  • Experience performing package, container, or seam inspections.
  • Experience using precision measurement or quality-testing equipment.
  • Experience entering quality inspection data into computerized systems.
  • Equivalent combinations of education, training, and relevant manufacturing experience that provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities will be considered.

***Please note: This position does not qualify for relocation expenses.***


Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh and fresh cut fruits and vegetables. Our diverse product portfolio also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts—available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Brighton, Michigan.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Brighton area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Brighton requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

Selected professionals will assess written and spoken Cantonese, review AI-generated language outputs, complete structured annotation and labelling tasks, and provide detailed feedback on linguistic accuracy, fluency, contextual appropriateness, and overall quality. The work requires native-level Cantonese proficiency and consistent application of language evaluation standards. No prior experience in AI is required.

Key Responsibilities

Cantonese Language Evaluation

  • Assess Cantonese text and speech data for linguistic accuracy, fluency, and contextual appropriateness
  • Review written and spoken language samples using structured evaluation criteria
  • Identify grammatical, lexical, contextual, or stylistic issues within Cantonese content
  • Apply native-level linguistic judgement across varied language samples
  • Maintain consistent quality standards across repeated evaluation tasks

AI Output Review & Quality Assessment

  • Evaluate AI-generated Cantonese outputs for accuracy, naturalness, and relevance
  • Identify errors, ambiguities, inconsistencies, and opportunities for improvement
  • Determine whether generated responses appropriately reflect the intended meaning and context
  • Provide detailed feedback explaining linguistic weaknesses or quality concerns
  • Escalate complex or uncertain language cases when additional review is required

Annotation, Labelling & Data Review

  • Participate in structured data annotation, labelling, and categorisation assignments
  • Apply project-specific guidelines consistently across language datasets
  • Review text and speech samples carefully before submitting evaluations
  • Maintain high attention to detail throughout repetitive assessment workflows
  • Ensure completed work is accurate, complete, and suitable for language-model development

Documentation & Project Collaboration

  • Document linguistic insights, recurring issues, and recommendations clearly
  • Collaborate with project leads to clarify task requirements and evaluation criteria
  • Support ad hoc linguistic quality reviews as project priorities evolve
  • Adapt quickly to new tools, guidelines, and language-evaluation workflows
  • Manage assignments independently while maintaining agreed quality and delivery standards

Ideal Profile

  • Native proficiency in Cantonese with strong command of written and spoken forms
  • Experience in language evaluation, translation, linguistic annotation, or related language-focused work
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong attention to linguistic detail, nuance, and contextual meaning
  • Ability to apply objective and consistent evaluation criteria across diverse language samples
  • Familiarity with content moderation, transcription, or quality-assessment workflows is advantageous
  • Comfortable using online platforms and digital evaluation tools
  • Strong analytical skills when assessing ambiguous or context-dependent language
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple assignments, and meet project deliverables
  • No prior experience in AI research or model training is required

Engagement Details

This role requires independent work in accordance with marine, NAVSEA, and OSHA Maritime electrical standards.

Per diem may be available depending on contract requirements and travel distance.

Responsibilities

  • Install, repair, and maintain shipboard electrical systems including lighting, power distribution, motors, panels, controllers, and auxiliary equipment
  • Pull, route, hang, and secure electrical and communication cabling through passageways, overheads, bulkheads, and machinery spaces
  • Terminate power and communication cables using approved lugs, connectors, and shipboard standards
  • Install, pack, and seal multi-cable transits (MCTs) and cable penetrations
  • Support installation and testing of power, lighting, alarm, and interior communication systems including 1MC and sound-powered phone circuits
  • Perform continuity, polarity, insulation resistance, and operational testing
  • Read and interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, and technical manuals

Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of marine or ship repair electrical experience
  • Strong ability to read and interpret wiring diagrams, schematics, and shipboard documentation
  • Proficiency in cable pulling, termination, splicing, MCT packing, and equipment installation
  • Working knowledge of AC/DC systems, ship service power distribution, grounding, and bonding
  • Experience using electrical testing equipment such as multimeters and insulation resistance testers
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required base access credentials, including DBIDS
  • Ability to pass background screening and drug testing per customer requirements

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working aboard Navy vessels or to NAVSEA electrical standards
  • Familiarity with shipboard power distribution, alarm, and interior communication systems
  • OSHA 10 Maritime certification
  • Experience supporting availability-level ship repair or modernization projects

Additional Information

Work is performed aboard vessels, in dry docks, and in industrial shipyard environments supporting Navy and commercial ship repair operations. Duties require working in confined and elevated spaces including machinery spaces, overhead areas, and cableways. Exposure to industrial noise, energized systems, heat, and mechanical hazards is expected. PPE is required in accordance with site safety policies, and respiratory protection may be required based on task or location. Work schedules may include overtime, nights, weekends, and variable shifts depending on production requirements.

Venture Dynamics is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable law.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Home, New York.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Home area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Home requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Vehicle Safety Director (Passive Safety & Crashworthiness)
description:
Role Summary

VinFast’s senior technical authority for Passive Safety and Crashworthiness, accountable for crash performance, occupant protection, restraints, pedestrian/VRU protection, EV post-crash integrity, CAE correlation and global crash/NCAP readiness. The role is hands-on: identify crash/injury mechanisms, challenge CAE and test evidence, and drive executable structural, restraint, packaging, material and calibration countermeasures. Functional Safety, ADAS/SOTIF and homologation are supporting interfaces; Passive Safety is the core mandate.

Key Responsibilities

• Own passive-safety strategy and technical sign-off from concept to SOP, including crash architecture, load paths, structural deformation, occupant survival space, crash pulse and compatibility.

• Lead occupant protection and restraint development across airbags, belts, pretensioners, load limiters, seats/head restraints, child occupants and sensing/deployment interfaces.

• Own crash CAE-to-physical correlation across component, sled, subsystem and full-vehicle testing; challenge model quality, dummy injury metrics, intrusion, pulse and deformation behavior.

• Drive root-cause and design convergence for frontal, offset, side, pole, rear, rollover/roof, far-side, whiplash, pedestrian/VRU and EV post-crash cases, converting failures into clear engineering countermeasures.

• Set VinFast crash/NCAP targets and readiness for Euro NCAP, Bharat NCAP, ASEAN NCAP, FMVSS/US NCAP, UNECE and other markets; optimize solutions for safety, mass, BOM cost, package and manufacturability through early front-loading.

• Build and lead the Passive Safety organization, establish design rules, DVPs, CAE/test correlation standards and lessons learned, and act as the primary passive-safety escalation point for senior management.

Cross-Functional Interfaces

Partner with BIW/Body, Restraints, Seats, Battery, Chassis, CAE, Physical Validation, Styling, Manufacturing, Quality and Program teams. Coordinate with Functional Safety, ADAS/SOTIF and homologation where crash sensing, restraint deployment, VRU interaction, rescue/post-crash functions or compliance overlap. Represent Passive Safety at architecture, design and program gates with quantified performance, root cause, countermeasure, cost/mass impact and residual risk.


Requirements

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Automotive or Structural Engineering; Master’s/PhD in crashworthiness, structural mechanics or biomechanics preferred.

• 12+ years automotive engineering experience with deep hands-on Passive Safety/Crashworthiness responsibility and at least 5 years in technical leadership.

• Expert knowledge of crash load paths, structural energy management, occupant kinematics, restraint interaction, injury mechanisms and physical crash-test root-cause analysis.

• Advanced experience with crash/occupant CAE tools such as LS-DYNA, Abaqus and Madymo or equivalent, including model review and physical-test correlation; strong restraint tuning and crash-test experience.

• Proven delivery of vehicle programs from concept to SOP with strong regulatory/NCAP crash performance, including resolution of major crash-test failures; EV crash/battery post-impact experience strongly preferred.

Key Competencies

• Deep passive-safety authority: moves from failed test/CAE evidence to mechanism, root cause and executable countermeasure.

• Solution and ownership mindset with strong judgment on safety vs. mass, cost, timing and package trade-offs.

• Strong executive communication and ability to defend technical decisions with evidence.

• Builder mindset: develops people, processes and a high-performing Passive Safety organization in a fast-moving OEM environment

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Product Owner I
description:
Bamboo Health is the leader in Real-Time Care Intelligence™ solutions aimed at improving lives for everyone experiencing physical and behavioral health challenges. From coast to coast, Bamboo Health partners with all major retail pharmacy chains, 52 states and territories, 100% of the top 10 best hospitals and more than half of the country’s largest health plans to improve more than 1 billion patient encounters annually. Summary:

We are seeking a highly analytical, data-focused Product Owner to join our Controlled Substances Reporting team. As a Product Owner, you will gather requirements, refine work, monitor dependencies, and manage backlog priorities. You will work collaboratively across product, engineering, and account management teams to support on-time delivery of customer-facing reporting products. We’re looking for a high potential product contributor who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and is comfortable using AI tools to work faster and smarter.

What You’ll Do:

  • Learn from senior team members and gain experience in all aspects of product ownership, contributing to the team's success by providing insights and assistance as needed.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define reporting requirements and deliver high-quality products on time and within budget.
  • Refine work into stories with clear acceptance criteria, plan sprints, prioritize tickets, and groom the backlog.
  • Ensure stories, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and requirements are clearly defined and ready for development.
  • Communicate product status, progress, and upcoming releases to stakeholders, executives, and customers.
  • Create and maintain product documentation, including user guides and data dictionaries.
  • Monitor key product metrics and analytics to identify areas of improvement and make data-driven decisions.
  • Explore opportunities to enhance workflows through AI or automation tools (e.g., document summarization, task routing, or data parsing).

What Success Looks Like…

In 3 months…

  • You are beginning to master Bamboo Health’s product development processes and tools, while building skill in triaging work and making tradeoffs during daily standups to balance competing needs.
  • You are actively participating in backlog refinement, sprint planning, and prioritization discussions.
  • You are incorporating AI-supported tools into your day-to-day work—whether through analysis, documentation, or task management.

In 6 months…

  • You are working closely with your product manager and team to create a metrics and instrumentation framework to identify opportunities to unblock growth.
  • You manage end to end report development from requirements definition through customer launch.
  • You own and maintain the internal short-term roadmap and are beginning to plan and provide direction on the internal medium to long-term roadmap for your area of ownership.

In 12 months…

  • You are a trusted resource on reporting products, able to explain current functionality, ongoing work, and upcoming enhancements.
  • You proactively flag risks to the current quarter’s plan and help keep next quarter’s planning on track – surfacing dependencies, gaps, or blockers before they become problems.
  • You contribute meaningful insights and recommendations that help inform future product and reporting enhancements.

What You Need:

  • 2+ years of experience working as a product owner with data-related technologies or in a data engineering organization.
  • You have a strong desire and willingness to learn product management and product development concepts, methodologies, and best practices.
  • You are familiar with data visualization and reporting tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar.
  • You are familiar with SQL, Python, or similar programming languages.
  • You understand data ingestion, storage, and analytics concepts and technologies.
  • You have experience supporting or driving projects involving multiple stakeholders and cross-functional teams.
  • You possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and dependencies simultaneously.
  • Comfort using or learning AI-supported tools (e.g., ChatGPT, CoPilot, or role-specific tools) to improve daily workflows.
  • A forward-thinking, curious mindset with an openness to experimenting with new technologies.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with sound judgment and creativity in designing solutions.
  • Proven ability to thrive in fast-paced, high-growth, and rapidly evolving environments.
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote-first environment, ensuring high-quality virtual interactions with minimal distractions.
  • The ability to travel periodically for work.

What You Get:

  • Join one of the most innovative healthcare technology companies in the country.
  • Have the autonomy to build something with an enthusiastically supportive team.
  • Learn from working at the highest levels and on the most strategic priorities of the company, including from world class investors and advisors.
  • Receive competitive compensation, including health, dental, vision and other benefits.

Belonging at Bamboo

We Care. #BambooHealthValuesCare

Every human being has the right to the best possible healthcare. Our Real-Time Care Intelligence™ solutions enable healthcare professionals to see and treat every individual as a whole person by providing the right information, at the right time – regardless of physical, behavioral or social barriers.

We’re a great place to work because we care. We continually seek to learn about our differences and ensure the unique perspectives and contributions of all employees are welcome, valued and celebrated.

Our commitment to making a positive impact starts by recognizing and leveraging our differences, building inclusive teams and cultivating a sense of belonging.

Dewberry is a leading, market-facing professional services firm with more than 60 locations and 2,500 professionals nationwide. What sets us apart from our competitors is our people.   • Self-motivated with highly developed verbal, written and interpersonal skills
  • Experience in staff management/department management
  • Experience in the design of various structural systems
  • Experience with Design/Build projects is a plus.

The projected range for this position is ($158,000.00 - 204,000.00) annually. Depending upon other factors, i.e., skills, experience, location, market conditions, the range may vary slightly.

The Precision Companies include Precision Fabricating & Cleaning Co., Inc. (PFC), Precision Mechanical Inc. (PMI) and Precision Enterprises, Inc. (PEI) - separate, but complementary, business units.

PMI has been offering mechanical services to a wide array of government, industrial, commercial, and institutional customers since 1986. PMI installs process piping and equipment, plumbing and HVAC systems in hospitals, schools, airports/air bases, semiconductor manufacturing facilities and launch complexes.

With strong financials, more than 200 employees, and 60,000 square feet of facilities located on 21 acres, the Precision Companies are ready to serve you.

High School Diploma or GED

Working with and around chemicals.

Hand tools, cleaning tanks, hand truck, pallet jack, personal protective equipment, sample collection hardware.

of knowledge and skills required of this job. You should not consider it an all-inclusive listing of

work requirements. You may be asked to perform other duties as assigned, including work in

If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

title: ALL OUTSIDE MACHINISTS
description:
Venture Dynamics is seeking skilled and experienced Outside Machinists to perform advanced mechanical installation, repair, alignment, and maintenance of shipboard machinery and equipment aboard Navy and commercial vessels. Outside Machinists will disassemble, troubleshoot, align, and reinstall pumps, valves, rotating equipment, propulsion components, and associated mechanical systems. This position requires strong mechanical aptitude, precision measurement skills, and the ability to work safely in confined spaces, elevated areas, and industrial shipyard environments.

Per diem may be available on select projects depending on contract requirements and travel distance.

Responsibilities

  • Install, remove, repair, and align shipboard machinery and mechanical systems

  • Disassemble and rebuild pumps, valves, gearboxes, motors, and rotating equipment

  • Perform shaft, pump, and equipment alignments using dial indicators, feeler gauges, micrometers, calipers, and other precision tools

  • Install bearings, seals, couplings, rotating components, and machinery foundations

  • Troubleshoot mechanical issues and support corrective actions

  • Read and interpret blueprints, schematics, mechanical drawings, and technical manuals

  • Use hand tools, power tools, and precision instruments for fit-up, measurement, and mechanical adjustments

  • Assist with staging, rigging, lifting, and material movement as required

  • Work in machinery spaces, tanks, voids, overheads, and other shipboard compartments

  • Follow NAVSEA mechanical safety requirements, OSHA Maritime standards, and all shipyard regulations

  • Maintain housekeeping standards, tool control, and safe work practices

Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of shipyard or marine mechanical experience as an Outside Machinist

  • Strong understanding of pumps, valves, rotating machinery, propulsion equipment, and mechanical systems

  • Proficiency using precision measurement tools (dial indicators, calipers, micrometers, feeler gauges, etc.)

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, schematics, manuals, and technical instructions

  • Must supply and maintain a personal tool set appropriate for mechanical repair (specialty tools provided when needed)

  • Ability to climb ladders, work in confined spaces, work at heights, and stand for extended periods

  • Ability to lift 40–60 lbs and perform physically demanding mechanical tasks

  • Must pass background check and drug screening per customer requirements

  • Reliable transportation and consistent attendance

  • Ability to obtain DBIDS/base access when required

  • Ability to work overtime, nights, weekends, and variable shifts as needed

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience performing precision alignments on propulsion equipment, pumps, and rotating machinery

  • Experience with pump and valve teardown, rebuilds, flushing, and reinstallation

  • Experience working aboard Navy vessels or to NAVSEA mechanical standards

  • Familiarity with WAF/Tagout procedures

  • Experience with laser alignment systems

  • OSHA-10 Maritime

  • Ability to wear a respirator when required for confined-space support, hot-work environments, or mechanical operations involving dust or fumes

  • Experience supporting marine repair, heavy industrial mechanical work, or shipyard operations

Additional Information

  • Work occurs aboard ships, in dry docks, machinery spaces, tanks, and industrial environments

  • PPE provided according to project and customer requirements

title: Route Supervisor
description:
Position Summary

The Route Supervisor is responsible for directing the daily activities of drivers and helpers in order to provide safe, effective ad courteous waste collection services to customers. The incumbent will ride with a driver during his/her scheduled route to identify opportunities for enhanced operating efficiencies, accurate billing, opportunities for increases in service and potential safety hazards.

Key Responsibilities

  • Rides with assigned driver on a designated commercial and/or residential route to gather data such as travel times, disposal volumes, service and collection times, and accuracy of the route sheet in an effort to increase efficiency, reduce cost, improve revenue and reduce safety hazards.
  • Ensures the proper usage of the OBC and OBC back office to help achieve the divisions efficiency, safety, and customer service goals.
  • Provides recommendations for improvement in route scheduling, service capabilities or other changes based on findings during on-route observations.
  • Coordinates and provides cross training to drivers to ensure proper coverage when employees are out due to vacation or sickness.
  • Collaborates with customer service and sales to achieve service quality and responsiveness to highly demanding customers.
  • Supervises and coaches drivers on pre and post trip inspections, and training/re-training of new and existing drivers when necessary.
  • Manages and provides leadership to team members by effectively communicating, establishing clear goals and objectives, coaching team members on achieving goals, and ensuring access to training and development opportunities that assist employees in attaining the necessary skills to achieve team and corporate results.
  • Participates in training and other learning opportunities to expand knowledge of the company, products, sales, and services and performs any other duties needed to help drive our vision, fulfill our mission, and/or abide by our core values.

The successful candidate will have a High School diploma or equivalent, a valid class A or B CDL driver’s license, 2-4 years of commercial driving experience, and a clean driving record. The incumbent must have a demonstrated ability to work as part of a team in a collaborative environment and experience in a customer-facing position.

Strong commitment to workplace safety and DOT regulations, outstanding relationship management skills, and an ability to measure and review productivity standards are required. Excellent listening, communication, and problem-solving skills and a working knowledge of Microsoft products are necessary.

Positive and supportive individual who is, attentive, observant, and results-oriented with the ability to see the larger picture while focusing on detailed information. title: Project Scheduler
description:
About Us

At ENFRA, we blend a rich history with a forward-looking vision. With over 100 years of experience, we are a pillar of stability in the energy infrastructure industry and a leader in innovative energy solutions. Our commitment to leveraging emerging technologies ensures that we remain at the forefront of the Energy-as-a-Service sector.

We believe in growth—not just for our business, but for our people. Our team members have the opportunity to advance their careers in a supportive environment that values continuous learning and development. We embrace innovation and encourage creative problem solving to tackle the energy infrastructure and energy challenges of tomorrow.

Inclusion is at the heart of our culture. We strive to create a workplace where every voice is heard and valued, fostering a collaborative environment where diverse perspectives drive our success.

Join us to be part of a legacy of excellence and a future of groundbreaking advancements. At ENFRA, stability, innovation, and growth are more than just values—they are the pillars of our continued success.

Overview

The Project Scheduler is an experienced individual contributor responsible for the development, maintenance, analysis, and integrity of the Project Schedule throughout all phases of assigned projects. Working under the direction of the Project Controls Director, the role independently leads scheduling execution on assigned small-to-medium projects or defined scopes within larger, more complex projects and may also assist with the preparation of proposal and bid schedules.

The Project Scheduler develops project schedules from Level 1 milestone schedules through Level 4 detailed working schedules based on the project execution strategy and the integration of relevant information from internal stakeholders, subcontractors, and other project participants. The position serves as the primary scheduling resource for assigned projects, owns the scheduling process, identifies emerging issues, evaluates schedule performance, develops recommendations, and drives follow-through on mitigation, corrective, and recovery actions.

The Project Scheduler is considered the technical expert in planning and scheduling for assigned projects and must understand and communicate the relationships among estimating, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, progress measurement, cost control, forecasting, risk management, change management, energy performance, and reporting. The role is expected to demonstrate ownership, technical expertise, commercial awareness, sound judgment, and the ability to influence project outcomes while consistently applying enterprise Project Controls standards and methodologies.

Responsibilities

Specific responsibilities include:

Project Leadership, Team Integration, and Project Setup

  • Serves as the primary scheduling resource and an active member of assigned project teams, providing timely, objective schedule information that supports execution decisions.
  • Works with Project Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Pre-Construction, Finance, subcontractors, and Project Controls personnel to translate scope and execution strategy into an integrated project schedule.
  • Leads scheduling setup and mobilization, including schedule architecture, work breakdown structures, calendars, coding, responsibility assignments, update cadence, and contractual scheduling requirements.
  • Reviews relevant proposal and contract requirements and incorporates schedule obligations, milestones, constraints, and deliverables into the planning approach.
  • Independently identifies emerging schedule issues, evaluates root causes, develops mitigation or recovery recommendations, and escalates material risks or decisions to project leadership and the Project Controls Director.

Schedule Management

  • Develops, baselines, maintains, updates, and analyzes network-logic-driven project schedules from proposal and milestone-level plans through detailed execution schedules.
  • Serves as the primary Primavera P6 subject matter expert for assigned projects, responsible for the configuration, administration, maintenance, quality assurance, and integrity of project schedules and related schedule data.
  • Develops integrated Level III schedules and, where required, detailed Level IV working schedules incorporating engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, commissioning, subcontractor, and client activities.
  • Leads schedule status collection and validation and updates actual progress, remaining durations, logic, constraints, milestones, resources, quantities, and forecast completion dates within Primavera P6.

Risk Management

Change Management

Energy Management

Planning & Project Setup

  • Develops schedule work breakdown structures, coding, calendars, logic standards, update procedures, progress rules, and reporting requirements.
  • Supports constructability planning, feasibility studies, project execution planning, and close-out reporting.

Interface with Operational Finance

Reporting & Performance Analytics

  • Develops, analyzes, and presents accurate schedule reports, dashboards, KPIs, progress curves, resource histograms, milestone reports, critical path analyses, and management narratives.
  • Performs schedule quality and health reviews and identifies logic, constraint, float, progress, and data-quality issues requiring correction.
  • Prepares schedule information for weekly, monthly, quarterly, client, and internal project reviews.

Team Leadership, Culture and Talent Development

Standards, Tools, and Continuous Improvement

  • Applies and champions enterprise planning and scheduling standards, procedures, tools, systems, and methodologies on assigned projects.
  • Serves as the Primavera P6 subject matter expert for assigned projects, responsible for schedule structure, coding, calendars, configurations, governance, data integrity, and adherence to enterprise scheduling standards.

title: Revenue Operation Analyst
description:
Job Details

The Role

We are seeking a Revenue Operations Analyst to own both sides of Salesforce: the integrity of the data going in and the reporting coming out. You will build the reports and dashboards that Sales, Business Development, Finance, and leadership run on, and keep the underlying data accurate so those numbers are trusted. This is a hands-on analyst role — we expect you to answer the question behind the request, not just deliver the number. The position reports to the Senior Manager of Revenue Operations and works daily with Marketing, Business Development, Sales, and Finance.


The Work -

Reporting & Analytics

· Builds and maintains Salesforce reports, custom reports, and dashboards for frontline reps, managers, and executives

· Owns recurring funnel reporting — Lead to MQL to SAL to SQL conversion, speed-to-lead, stage progression, and pipeline creation — with documented, consistent metric definitions

· Analyzes Business Development activity (outreach, response times, meeting conversion) and marketing-sourced lead quality — surface trends, outliers, and recommended actions

· Builds analysis beyond native Salesforce reporting using Excel models, SQL queries, and BI dashboards

· Reconciles data across Salesforce, HubSpot, and the sales engagement stack to ensure one source of truth

· Turns ad hoc questions from Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership into repeatable reporting with documented methodology

· Calculates monthly commissions and commission statements from Salesforce data

· Performs cohort and trend analysis (retention/expansion by segment, YoY, seasonality) and detect anomalies using statistical methods

· Evaluates data quality before analysis — identify root causes vs. symptoms and drive ambiguous metric definitions to precise, documented terms

· Builds decision frameworks with trade-offs, run scenario/what-if modeling, and redirect stakeholders when the wrong analysis is requested (core skills, ask right questions)

· Breaks down complex problems into the right data sources and metrics; apply statistical fundamentals (mean, median, percentiles, standard deviation, correlation) with documented methodology

Salesforce Data & Automation

· Maintain accurate, consistent records across accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities — including data cleansing, deduplication, and field standardization

· Monitor and enforce data quality standards; build reporting that makes data quality gaps visible

· Own lead import, routing, and assignment for marketing-sourced and third-party contacts to business development reps and sellers

· Design and maintain Salesforce Flows and declarative automation for lead management, data quality, and reporting

· Integrate data across sales technologies (HubSpot, Groove, Koncert, Seismic) for a holistic view of engagement and pipeline effectiveness

· Understand object relationships, data model architecture, and the security model (profiles, permission sets, roles, sharing rules) and how they affect report visibility

· Implement validation rules and duplicate management to prevent bad data at entry; use enrichment tools to fill data gaps

· Manage change (sandbox deployments, change sets) and use audit fields for change tracking and troubleshooting

Go-to-Market Support

· Build targeted audience lists for outbound campaigns and event follow-up, aligned to account segmentation, buying personas, and intent data

· Document report definitions, data logic, and recurring processes so the work is repeatable and not person-dependent

QUALIFICATIONS

· 4 - 5+ years in relevant revenue operations, sales operations, or business/data analysis supporting a commercial team

· Hands-on Salesforce expertise — reports, custom report types, dashboards, data imports, list views, and Flow Builder or comparable declarative automation

· Demonstrated analytical ability — able to structure a question, choose the right data, and explain what the result means, not just produce the output

· Experience using AI-assisted tools for data analysis (SOQL/SQL generation, Python scripts, Excel formulas) and data exploration (summarize datasets, identify patterns, generate hypotheses)

· Write effective AI prompts with context and constraints; verify generated output and recognize AI limitations and hallucinations

· Advanced Excel or Google Sheets — Power Query, Power Pivot, advanced lookups, string manipulation, and data modeling

· Working SQL skills — able to query a database or warehouse

· Experience building and maintaining dashboards in a BI tool (Power BI, Tableau, or similar)

· Clear written and verbal English and strong asynchronous communication habits — this role works with a US-based team and is expected to document its own work

· Salesforce Administrator certification is a plus

· Experience with HubSpot, Groove, Koncert, or Seismic is a plus

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Northville, Michigan.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Northville area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Northville requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

Position Summary

The Senior Quality Technician ensures calibration activities, Device History Record (DHR) reviews, and manufacturing documentation comply with FDA Quality System Regulations, ISO 13485 requirements, and internal quality procedures. This role serves as the subject matter expert for calibration activities and supports manufacturing, engineering, facilities, and quality teams in maintaining equipment traceability, audit readiness, and compliant product release documentation.

The Senior Quality Technician owns and maintains the site-wide calibration program, coordinates calibration vendors and maintenance activities, supports impact assessments, and performs detailed DHR reviews to ensure products meet all quality and regulatory requirements prior to release.

Responsibilities

Quality / Compliance

Supports quality system compliance activities related to calibration control, manufacturing documentation review, traceability, audit readiness, product release, and regulated quality operations within a medical device manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities include:

  • Own and maintain the company's calibration master list and calibration system.
  • Schedule, track, and coordinate calibration activities for all required equipment.
  • Review calibration certificates for accuracy, tolerance requirements, and compliance standards.
  • Ensure proper equipment labeling and calibration status identification.
  • Maintain calibration records and supporting documentation within the eQMS.
  • Monitor calibration metrics and support management review activities.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Hillsborough, New Jersey.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Hillsborough area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Hillsborough requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

description:

You will build and test model and software improvements for the American Community Survey (ACS), develop pilots for additional surveys and fields, and work with data scientists and MLOps engineers to integrate approved changes into production.

Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain Python components for text preprocessing, model invocation, prompt management, structured output validation, and coding workflows.

• Implement approved changes to prompts, model configuration, dictionaries, rules, and supporting code in small, version-controlled increments.

• Build pilots using LLMs, fuzzy matching, direct-match dictionaries, or hybrid approaches; adapt implementations to survey-specific taxonomies and requirements.

• Write unit, integration, regression, negative, and edge-case tests, and work with the evaluation team to compare candidate results with approved baselines.

• Reproduce production problems, isolate causes across code, data, prompts, and model behavior, and implement verified corrections.

• Partner with the MLOps Engineer on packaging, deployment, rollback, and post-release verification within Government-approved AWS environments.

• Participate in code reviews and SME working sessions; maintain technical documentation, user guidance, and reproducible examples for Government handoff.

Requirements

Required qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, data science, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

• 8+ years in software or ML engineering, including 3+ years building NLP or ML applications and hands-on experience integrating LLMs into working systems.

• Strong Python development skills and experience with data processing, APIs, automated testing, Git, and maintainable software design.

• Experience with text classification, prompt design, structured model outputs, and measuring the effects of implementation changes on model performance.

• Experience deploying or supporting applications in AWS, troubleshooting production issues, and collaborating effectively with data scientists and operational teams.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with fuzzy matching, dictionary-based coding, survey text, or industry and occupation classification.

• Experience with ML frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or Hugging Face, and handling sensitive data in controlled federal environments.

Conditions of employment. Position contingent on contract award. Must be able to obtain and maintain applicable Census Special Sworn Status and Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials, follow confidentiality requirements, and support Census core business hours and coordinated critical processing runs.

Benefits

  • Flexible spending account
  • Health insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Professional development assistance

title: Psychiatrist
description:
Overview

NaphCare is hiring a Psychiatrist to join our team of medical professionals in the Arizona Department of Corrections in Phoenix, Arizona.

Pay rates range from $165.00 to $174.00 per hour based on shift, site needs, hire status, and experience.

Full Time and Part Time positions may be available!

As a Correctional Psychiatrist, you will oversee clinical responsibility for the mental health programs within the facility, while working alongside correctional officers and other medical professionals. This is a unique position where you can make a difference to this diverse population of patients with complex mental health needs.

Responsibilities

The Psychiatrist is responsible for providing comprehensive psychiatric evaluations and diagnosing mental health conditions to facility residents that protects the rights, dignity, and health of our unique patient population. Additional responsibilities may include and not be limited to:

  • Providing medication management, therapy, and other evidence-based treatment plans to address mental health needs
  • Oversee the completion of mental health screenings and evaluations performed by others
  • Responding to acute mental health crises within the facility
  • Supporting the rehabilitation of patients and facilitating their successful transition back into the community
  • Coordinate, lead and participate in educational training activities related to mental health care
  • Ensuring compliance with State and Federal mandates and regulations, including court mandates and standards
  • Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, including correctional staff, psychologists, social workers and other medical professionals to develop and implement treatment plans and ensuring staff are responsive to patients’ needs

Qualifications

Education / Licenses / Certifications

  • Must hold a current unrestricted license as a Psychiatrist in the state
  • A current DEA registration in the state
  • Be able to obtain BLS CPR Certification (AHA preferred)
  • Be certified in a Board recognized by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN)
  • Must possess strong written communication and verbal skills and have strong computer skills.
  • Experience with underserved and marginalized populations, including those with mental health and substance use disorders
  • Strong communication skills and ability to communicate with diverse individuals, including other medical professionals, correctional staff and judges
  • Ability to interpret and analyze data to create treatment plans
  • Knowledge of applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards
  • Able to maintain confidentiality of all proprietary and/or confidential information
  • Display integrity, professionalism and be able to adhere to a Code of Conduct and comply with all facility(s) correctional healthcare policies, procedures, and legal requirements
  • Must pass the facility’s criminal background check and drug screening

Why Join NaphCare?

NaphCare is one of the largest providers of healthcare services to correctional facilities throughout the US and we are growing. If you have never considered a career in correctional healthcare, now may be the time. In addition to competitive salaries and generous employee benefits, we strongly support career advancement within the company.

NaphCare Benefits for Full-Time Employees Include:

  • Health, dental & vision insurance that starts day one!
  • Prescriptions free of charge through our health plan, beginning day one!
  • Lowest Cost Benefits!
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services
  • 401K and Roth with company contribution that starts day one!
  • Tuition Assistance
  • Referral bonuses
  • Term life insurance at no cost to the employee
  • Generous paid time off & paid holidays
  • Free continuing education and CMEs

NaphCare has a partnership with NetCE that provides CEU/CME for our staff. NetCE uses a rigorous peer review process to ensure that all activities and content are up-to-date. This service streamlines continuing education for all NaphCare Employees to meet state specific requirements for maintaining licensing.

Scope of Work:

title: Family Response Team
description:
FLSA: Non-exempt

DEPARTMENT: Housing Services


JOB OVERVIEW:

The Family Response Team Member (FRT) acts as the first point of contact within the Family Solutions Center (FSC) and provides screening, triage, crisis intervention, access to crisis housing, and transportation services to homeless families in SPA 7. The FRT quickly screens all homeless families referred, diverts families from the shelter system, connects homeless families to crisis housing and addresses families’ immediate needs. The FRT is responsible for assisting families navigate the homeless system from receipt of referral to acceptance into appropriate permanent housing programs.

The purpose of the FRT is to assist families in achieving transitional housing and access medical, educational, social, prevocational, rehabilitative, or other needed community services for eligible clients and families who have become homeless. Targeted population includes children (Birth to age 18) and their families who are at risk of becoming homeless or are currently homeless utilizing a Community Based Scattered Site Model. The Community Based Scattered Site Model is designed to maximize family independence, minimize family disruption, and result in stronger, more viable housing permanency outcomes.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITY:

The FRT provide an array of services in support of the Family Solution Center/Family Housing Programs. FRT gathers pertinent information from the family and complete pre-screening/triage tool which is designed to assist service providers target families towards the most appropriate housing intervention. The FRT will implement, based on information gathered, the crisis housing portion of the family’s coordinated assistance plan to address the family’s immediate housing and other crisis needs.

The FRT promotes a strengths based approach to service that empowers families, supports a community based philosophy of service, and ensures that all services are aligned with the agency’s mission, vision, and core values.

BENEFITS:

  • Full benefits package to all positions after 30 days of employment.
  • Employer-paid standard HMO Health, Dental, and Vision plans offered to employees.
  • 401k plan with 4% employer match.
  • 40 hours of paid sick time annually
  • Paid vacation time that accrues to 80 hours annually.
  • 14 Paid Holidays annually.
  • Opportunity for growth. We love to promote from within.
  • Bilingual Stipend if applicable.
  • $23.00 an hour starting pay.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Conducts standardized screening and triages families imminently at-risk and homeless
  • Works in coordination with the FSC Case Management team and HFSS crisis housing providers to ensure seamless and integrated care for homeless families
  • Diverts families to other sources of assistance when possible
  • Screens and immediately addresses safety concerns; Conducts child safety screenings
  • Develops and implements crisis housing plans
  • Connects families to immediate supportive services as needed such as mental health, health, substance abuse, child care, employment, etc.
  • Data entry to HMIS
  • Coordination with the DPSS Homeless Case Manager for initial eligibility assessment of CalWorks benefits
  • Follow-up activities to ensure completion of the crisis housing plan
  • Provides individual and group rehabilitation services under HUD, DMH, DPSS and city contracts.
  • Completes and submits progress notes in a 24 hour timeframe utilizing the agency’s electronic health record system (HMIS).
  • Assists family with identifying internal and external resources to assist with multiple stressors as it relates to homelessness, domestic violence, substance abuse issues, etc.
  • Provides interagency and intra-agency consultation, communication, coordination and referrals.
  • Attends community meetings as requested by Housing Manager to present on housing services, referral process and eligibility criteria.
  • Represents the agency at community resource fairs.
  • Follows up with families to ensure successful placement and housing permanency.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Preferred:
  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, or other mental health related discipline is preferred, but not required.
  • Minimum of 1-4 years of work experience related to providing case management or rehabilitative services in a mental health setting.
  • Fluent in Spanish

Required:

  • High School Diploma

The Whole Child is an equal employment opportunity employer and no candidate for employment will be rejected on account of race, color, religion, national origin, age, marital status, or sex. Candidates with physical impairments will be considered so long as it can be reasonably demonstrated that the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed without hazard to the individual, fellow employees, or clientele.
