title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Groton, Massachusetts.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Groton area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Groton requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Executive Communications Specialist
description:

title: Program Lead
description:

title: Logistics Analyst I

From managing supply chain tasks to maintaining accountability for equipment in both stateside and deployed environments, your work will directly contribute to mission readiness and operational excellence.

This role is ideal for individuals with a specialist mindset-those who thrive in structured environments, excel at detail-driven processes, and bring dependability and discipline to every aspect of their work. Qualifications & Required Experience

Preferred Experience

Equal Employment Opportunity

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Santee, California.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Santee area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Santee requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Building Science Technologist- Roofing
description:
At Rimkus, our Built Environment Solutions team operates on a global scale with the advantage of local expertise. Our licensed engineers, architects, and technical specialists bring deep knowledge of regional requirements and industry best practices, enabling us to deliver customized, high-quality solutions that maximize the success of our clients’ investments. With a comprehensive portfolio that spans nearly every engineering and architectural discipline, we help organizations plan, build, and manage assets with confidence.

What sets us apart is our forward-thinking approach. We integrate carbon footprint reduction, resiliency, maintainability, and long-term sustainability into everything we do helping clients not just meet today’s needs but prepare for tomorrow’s challenges. From design and pre-construction through construction, closeout, and ongoing operations, we provide tailored support at every stage. By identifying potential issues before they arise, we mitigate risks, extend asset life, and reduce costly unplanned repairs. Whether an asset is newly constructed, leased, or purchased, our innovative solutions empower clients to operate more efficiently and sustainably. Joining Rimkus means being part of a team that’s shaping the future of the built environment—one smart, resilient solution at a time.

Requirements

Job Posting

We are seeking a detail-oriented Roofing Technician / Building Science Technologist to join our team and help solve complex challenges involving existing buildings and facility improvements. In this role, you will apply your technical knowledge to evaluate commercial and residential properties, primarily involving roofing and overall building condition assessments, and support practical design solutions for rehabilitation, repair, and adaptive reuse projects. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys field investigation, technical problem-solving, and managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Perform roof condition assessments for commercial, institutional and residential facilities, and prepare reports for review by senior leadership team.
  • Perform pre-start meetings as well as on-site quality observations for ongoing roof replacement projects, complete with reports.
  • Perform building condition assessments for commercial, institutional and residential facilities, and prepare reports for review by senior leadership team.
  • Perform pre-start meetings as well as on-site quality observations for ongoing building envelope and related projects, complete with reports.
  • Assist with leak investigations involving roofs, walls, windows, foundations, and other building envelope components.
  • Assist in the preparation of reserve fund studies, sketches, details and technical documentation.

title: Regional Assistant Chief Engineer - North America
description:
Regional Assistant Chief Engineer – North America

Millennium Hotels & Resorts – Corporate
Reports To: Regional Director of Engineering – North America
Location: Chicago or Denver | Regional Travel Required
Employment Type: Full-time
Salary Range: $120,000 - $130,000

Join the Team at Millennium Hotels & Resorts

At Millennium Hotels & Resorts, we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and delivering exceptional hospitality experiences across a global portfolio. Our corporate teams play a critical role in supporting our properties, driving strategy, and enabling operational success.

About Corporate Operations

Our corporate office serves as the strategic and operational hub for Millennium Hotels & Resorts, supporting the hotels across multiple regions and brands. From finance and human resources to operations, marketing, and development, our teams work collaboratively to drive performance, enhance guest experiences, and support our employees across the portfolio.

This environment is fast-paced, collaborative, and focused on delivering results while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism and service.

As part of Millennium Hotels & Resorts, a global hospitality leader with over 145 hotels across key destinations worldwide, our hotels are backed by a legacy of quality, consistency, and service excellence.

At Millennium, we are guided by our core values:

  • Passion for Hospitality – Delivering meaningful and memorable guest experiences
  • Entrepreneurial Spirit – Taking ownership and acting with agility
  • Innovation – Continuously improving how we operate and serve
  • Progressive & Solutions-Oriented – Staying adaptable and focused on results

About the Role: Regional Assistant Chief Engineer – North America

As the Regional Assistant Chief Engineer – North America, you will support the Regional Director of Engineering in providing technical leadership and operational oversight across Millennium Hotels & Resorts' North American portfolio.

This role serves as a key resource to hotel Chief Engineers, General Managers, and regional leadership, helping ensure that our hotels maintain safe, efficient, reliable, and well-maintained facilities while meeting Millennium standards and applicable regulatory requirements.

You will contribute to regional engineering strategy, asset management, preventive maintenance, capital planning, energy management, sustainability initiatives, and technical problem-solving. This is an influential role requiring strong technical expertise, business acumen, communication skills, and the ability to drive results across multiple hotels and teams.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineering leader who combines strong technical knowledge with a strategic mindset and a passion for developing people, protecting hotel assets, improving operational performance, and delivering sustainable results.

Your Impact

You will help strengthen engineering performance across the region by providing technical guidance, developing engineering talent, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting consistent standards across the portfolio.

You will serve as a trusted technical resource and escalation point for complex engineering, facilities, life-safety, compliance, and building systems matters while partnering closely with hotel and corporate leadership.

Your leadership will help ensure our hotels are safe, efficient, operationally sound, and positioned for long-term success.

What You’ll Be Doing

Regional Engineering Leadership

  • Support the Regional Director of Engineering in providing technical leadership and oversight to Chief Engineers and engineering teams across the North American portfolio.
  • Serve as a technical resource, advisor, and escalation point for complex engineering and facilities issues.
  • Promote consistency in engineering practices, preventive maintenance, asset management, and operational standards across hotels.
  • Support regional engineering initiatives and contribute to the development and implementation of best practices.
  • Provide coverage and leadership support for the Regional Director of Engineering as needed.

Asset Management & Engineering Operations

  • Monitor the condition, reliability, and performance of hotel buildings, equipment, and critical infrastructure.
  • Conduct and participate in property visits, engineering audits, technical assessments, and facility condition reviews.
  • Identify operational risks, deferred maintenance, and opportunities to improve asset performance.
  • Review property engineering performance and develop recommendations and corrective action plans.
  • Support hotel engineering leaders in establishing effective preventive and predictive maintenance programs.
  • Promote consistent use of CMMS, work-order management, maintenance tracking, and reporting systems.

Capital Projects & Financial Management

  • Assist with the development, review, prioritization, and execution of annual capital expenditure plans.
  • Support major renovations, equipment replacements, building-system upgrades, and other capital projects.
  • Partner with Operations, Design & Construction, Procurement, and hotel leadership to support effective project planning and execution.
  • Review project scopes, technical specifications, budgets, and timelines.
  • Help ensure capital investments are aligned with operational priorities, asset needs, guest experience, and long-term value.
  • Support engineering leaders in managing departmental budgets and controlling maintenance and utility costs.

Energy, Sustainability & Continuous Improvement

  • Champion energy management, sustainability, and utility-cost reduction initiatives across the portfolio.
  • Analyze energy and utility consumption and identify opportunities for improved efficiency.
  • Support implementation of sustainability programs and engineering best practices aligned with Millennium's corporate goals.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage technology, automation, and innovative engineering solutions to improve efficiency and reduce operating costs.
  • Promote a culture of continuous improvement and solutions-oriented problem solving.

Safety, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Monitor compliance with company standards, applicable building codes, fire and life-safety requirements, environmental regulations, and other applicable laws and regulations.
  • Support hotel engineering teams in maintaining safe operating environments for guests and employees.
  • Assist with technical reviews related to fire/life-safety systems, emergency systems, building infrastructure, and critical equipment.
  • Identify potential operational and safety risks and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety, accountability, documentation, and regulatory compliance.

People Leadership & Development

  • Support the recruitment, onboarding, training, coaching, and development of Chief Engineers and key engineering personnel.
  • Partner with hotel leadership to strengthen engineering talent and succession planning.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to engineering leaders.
  • Share knowledge, best practices, and innovative solutions across the regional engineering community.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and professional growth.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Management

Build strong working relationships with General Managers, hotel leadership, ownership representatives, corporate departments, vendors, contractors, and service providers.

Partner with regional Operations, Design & Construction, Procurement, Finance, and other corporate functions on engineering-related initiatives.

Communicate technical information and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Represent the Engineering function with professionalism and a solutions-oriented approach.

Requirements

Qualifications & Experience

  • Extensive progressive experience in hotel engineering, facilities management, building operations, or a related field.
  • Significant experience supporting multiple hotels, a regional portfolio, or a corporate engineering function preferred.
  • Strong technical knowledge of hotel building systems, including:
    • HVAC and mechanical systems
    • Electrical systems
    • Plumbing
    • Fire and life-safety systems
    • Building automation and controls
    • Vertical transportation systems
    • Building infrastructure and related hotel systems
  • Demonstrated experience with capital projects, maintenance programs, budgets, and asset management.
  • Working knowledge of applicable North American building, safety, fire, environmental, and energy codes and regulations.
  • Experience with CMMS/work-order systems and energy-management platforms.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and lead without direct authority.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and/or Google Workspace.
  • Ability and willingness to travel extensively across the North American portfolio, typically 40–60%.
  • Hospitality or Millennium Hotels & Resorts experience is a plus.
  • Professional certifications such as CEM, LEED AP, CFM, or equivalent are preferred but not required.

Core Competencies

  • Technical Expertise & Problem-Solving
  • Regional Leadership & Influence
  • Asset & Facilities Management
  • Capital Project & Financial Acumen
  • Safety & Regulatory Compliance
  • Energy Management & Sustainability
  • People Development
  • Collaboration & Communication
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Results Orientation & Operational Excellence

Working Conditions

  • This is a regional leadership position requiring significant travel throughout the North American portfolio. The role includes a combination of corporate/office-based strategic work and on-site technical engagement at hotels.
  • The position may require occasional evening, weekend, or after-hours availability to support emergencies, critical engineering issues, major projects, or operational needs.

Benefits

At Millennium Hotels & Resorts, we support our employees with a competitive benefits package designed to promote wellbeing and long-term success:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • Company-paid Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Coverage
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Company Match (where applicable)
  • Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays
  • Hotel Room Discounts across our global portfolio
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to plan terms and company policy.

Why Join Us

At Millennium Hotels & Resorts, you’re not just taking a job—you’re joining a team passionate about hospitality, growth, and creating memorable experiences.

Whether you’re behind the scenes or on the front line, your work makes an impact. If you’re ready to learn, grow, and be part of something meaningful, we’d love to meet you.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Butler, Pennsylvania.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Butler area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Butler requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

  • Mandatory Language: Fluent/Advanced English is a MUST HAVE (you will have daily interactions with global teams, stakeholders, and headquarters).

  • Experience: Solid background in Strategic Planning, BizOps, Performance Management, or Operations within startups, tech companies, or on-demand logistics.

  • Analytical Mastery: Advanced SQL for handling large datasets and proven experience with data visualization tools.

  • Problem-Solving: Structured thinking to break down complex business problems and turn them into actionable execution plans.

  • Influence & Ownership: Strong ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and influence decision-makers in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Nice to Have

  • Previous experience dealing with supply dynamics (couriers/drivers) in two-sided or three-sided marketplaces.

  • Practical knowledge of Python or R for predictive analysis and automation.

Role Qualifications

The grit, relentless drive, and high-ownership mindset needed to scale results in a fast-paced marketplace.

  • We believe in Diversity and Inclusion – Diversity is one of our biggest strengths. Our differences are what makes us distinct. We respect each other and believe in equal opportunities for all.

We are committed to building inclusive and diverse teams.

At DiDi, we believe that our differences are our biggest source of strength. That‘s why we are committed to promoting equal opportunities to all candidates and employees as an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: State Program Officer - Type 1 Diabetes
description:
Overview

WJCF is an Indian non-profit organisation committed to saving lives by reducing the burden of disease and strengthening government-owned, high-quality health systems. Since 2007, WJCF has combined data-driven approaches and deep public health expertise with strong government partnerships to design, implement, and scale solutions across India’s national and state health programmes. We work for and at the service of governments — supporting the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and State Departments of Health to build systems that are strong, sustainable, and led by Indian institutions.

As an Indian organisation, WJCF brings an unmatched depth of contextual understanding of India’s health system architecture, policy landscape, and implementation realities across diverse geographies and population groups. This local institutional credibility, combined with global technical rigour, is central to WJCF’s effectiveness as a partner to governments and donors.

Our work is built around four complementary roles: as a Trusted Government Partner, co-designing programmes and strengthening health system architecture; as an Operational Partner, translating strategies into effective on-the-ground delivery; as a Market Shaper, improving the availability and affordability of health commodities; and as an Ecosystem Catalyst, convening governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector to drive solutions at scale.

WJCF’s programme portfolio spans thematic areas like hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases), syphilis, cervical cancer, diabetes, maternal and childhood anaemia, immunisation, under-5 diarrhoea and pneumonia, sexual and reproductive health, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri – Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), hypoxemia and oxygen, safe drinking water, sickle cell disease, presbyopia, lead poisoning, and cross cutting thematic areas like AI and Health, integrated disease surveillance, and climate and health.

We currently support programmes across 19 states and union territories, with teams working at national, state, district, and sub-district levels.

Our people are our greatest asset. WJCF brings together a talented, diverse team of professionals from public health, analytics, consulting, healthcare, the development sector, and academia, all united by a shared commitment to improving health outcomes for the people of India. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and deeply grounded in the communities and systems we work in. Our field teams collectively bring hundreds of years of experience managing public health programmes across the country.

WJCF collaborates with a range of international and domestic partners and donors to advance its mission, including an affiliation with the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), a global health organisation with which WJCF shares a common mission and values.

Program Overview

Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is an auto-immune condition characterized by reduced ability to produce insulin in the body, leading to a lifetime dependence on insulin for survival. The condition is associated with a significant strain and poor quality of life and leading to a high financial burden for people living with Type 1 Diabetes (PLT1D) and their families. However, with access to timely diagnostic, initiation on treatment and proper management of the condition, people living with T1D can lead healthy and productive lives, while achieving life expectancy comparable to the general population.

There are an estimated 9.4 million PLT1D globally, with India having the second highest share accounting for 8%-10% of the global prevalence. However, nearly 18% of children and adolescents with T1D (~0.3 million) live in India, the highest in the world. The incidence of T1D in the 0-19 age group is increasing more than any other age group. The estimated global incidence of T1D in the 0-19 age group was 8.15 per 100,000 in 2024 and is estimated to increase to 13.95 per 100,000 by 2040.

While the burden of T1D has continued to rise over the years, survival has remained poor. Survival rates for children and adolescents with T1D in India is worse compared to countries with similar socio-economic development. On average, in India, PLT1D is estimated to lose approximately 42 healthy years of life due to the combined effects of premature mortality, illness, and disability associated with the condition.

There is an urgent need to strengthen access to services and care for T1D. WJCF’s T1D program aims at strengthening and improving access to quality T1D care in India, with the overall goal of achieving longer, healthier, and more productive lives for PLT1D. The program aims to address critical barriers to access and delivery of quality T1D care in India by building awareness, improving access to detection, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up services and care, enabling treatment adherence and self-management, and strengthening governance and policy framework for delivery of T1D care.

Position Summary

WJCF is looking for a driven, detail-focused professional with strong coordination skills and a proven track record in operations and stakeholder management to take up the role of State Program Officer, T1D (MP). The SPO will provide catalytic support to the program coordination function of WJCF's Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program in Madhya Pradesh, contributing to the initiative to operationalise approximately 35 new T1D clinics. The position exists to speed up progress on core programmatic work — routine follow-up with PLT1D, tracking how Mission Madhuhari is progressing on the ground, maintaining and managing T1D operational trackers, and making sure implementation issues are escalated and resolved without delay.

The person we are looking for brings excellent interpersonal skills, works well independently, stays flexible, is at ease coordinating operations across cross-functional teams, and holds a high bar for their own work. This is a high-impact opportunity for young professionals who want to shift public health outcomes for the better, offering substantial stakeholder engagement alongside real operational leadership.

Responsibilities

1. Program Implementation and Operational Coordination

  • Offer day-to-day operational supervision and hands-on support to District Program Coordinators, including joint workplan development aligned with prevailing state-level priorities
  • Convene and lead weekly or bi-weekly reviews to track implementation progress, surface bottlenecks, propose corrective measures, and follow through on agreed action points
  • Drive the set-up and ongoing functioning of T1D clinics in line with approved phased scale-up plans, keeping trackers current on readiness, implementation status, milestones achieved, key gaps, and outstanding actions
  • Follow up regularly with schools and colleges on the establishment and functioning of T1D/Madhuhari Corners, and help ensure planned activities happen on time
  • Routinely flag under-performing geographies, districts, or clinics and travel to those locations to help DPCs get to the root of the problem. To strengthen this support, the SPO may cultivate working relationships with government officials at state, district, and health facility levels.
  • Monitor availability of insulin, syringes, glucometers, test strips, HbA1c consumables, and cold chain integrity at clinics; coordinate with state and district supply chain officials to pre-empt and resolve stock-outs
  • Oversee PLT1D enrolment and follow-up processes — keep the PLT1D registry current, track scheduled follow-up visits, and drive tracing and re-engagement of PLT1Ds lost to follow-up
  • Coordinate training and refresher sessions for clinic teams (physicians, nurses, counsellors, and FLWs), and provide on-site mentoring during field visits
  • Support awareness and demand-generation activities across schools, communities, and health facilities in coordination with the state team

2. Monitoring, Reporting, and Quality Assurance

  • Contribute to performance management, capacity-building, and quality improvement through regular feedback, coordination, quality assessments, and field validation visits, in consultation with the state-level WJCF team
  • Prepare progress dashboards, review decks, and briefing notes for state and divisional review meetings, and represent WJCF in these forums alongside the State Lead

3. Coordination, Risk Management, and Administrative Support

  • Establish and sustain strong working relationships with relevant state, divisional, and field stakeholders so that implementation runs smoothly and activities are delivered on schedule
  • Spot operational and systemic challenges, help put mitigation measures in place, and escalate high-priority risks or issues so they are resolved in time
  • Support planning and execution of activity budgets, procurement, travel, and logistics for trainings, field visits, and state-level events, including follow-through on approvals and expense documentation
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, and performance appraisal of District Program Coordinators, and mentor them on the ground
  • Document SOPs, case studies, and best practices emerging from Madhya Pradesh for replication across other states
  • Keep activities aligned with approved implementation plans and take on additional or ad hoc workstreams assigned by the program leads, including coordination, follow-up, and documentation support for emerging priorities during scale-up

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in public health, social work, healthcare management, social sciences, or a comparable discipline. A Master's in public health (MPH) or in Hospital/Healthcare Administration is preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience across public health programs, healthcare operations, field implementation, and program coordination, including supervising district or program coordinators and health facility staff, allocating tasks, following up, and monitoring performance.
  • Direct experience working with NHM and state health department structures, government reporting systems, and public health portals.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple program priorities under tight timelines across varied geographies — identifying roadblocks, planning and deploying course corrections down to the health facility level, and escalating issues through the right channels without delay.
  • Experience tracking key indicators, maintaining reports, and circulating operational updates promptly.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills for working with government officials at state, district, and health facility levels, as well as with partner agencies.
  • Hands-on experience with programmatic M&E and joint activity planning with field teams. Experience managing large field teams is an added advantage.
  • Working proficiency in MS Office, data management, and documentation.
  • A demonstrated sense of accountability, adaptability, and a collaborative way of working.
  • Fluency in Hindi and English, written and spoken.
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively across program geographies (approx. 50-60% of time), in discussion with the program lead.

Manufacturo powers operations for companies building satellites, fusion reactors, next-generation aircraft, and hypersonic vehicles. The Role

As a Backend Developer at Manufacturo, you will work on a complex product used to manage manufacturing operations. Your main focus will be our core platform, with production at its center and close connections to planning, inventory, quality, and shopfloor workflows.

This is a backend-first, hands-on engineering role with real ownership. You will build product features, design APIs, model business logic and data structures, and contribute to the technical quality, maintainability, and reliability of the platform.

description:
Overview

Manufacturing Company with Career Development Opportunities!

Comprehensive Benefits Package!

Full Time| 1st Shift| Monday - Friday| 5:00am-1:30pm

Must be able to read exact measurements on a tape measure without assistance!

About Us

Daifuku is the nation’s leading independent, U.S.‐based provider of intelligent material handling systems. With hundreds of engineers in‐house, the company designs, manufactures, integrates, and installs the full spectrum of intra-logistics solutions. Responsibilities

Position Summary

The Fabricator operates fabricating machines to create structural steel products used in industrial automation.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Operating fabrication shop and machine shop machinery and equipment, such as cutoff saws, shears, rolls, brakes, presses, forming machines, spinning machines, and punches, to cut, shape, and bend metal plates, sheets, tubes, and structures
  • Reading job specifications and blueprints to determine machine adjustments and material requirements
  • Setting stops or guides to specified length as indicated by scale, rule, or template
  • Positioning workpiece against stops or aligns layout marks with die or blade
  • Measures workpiece dimensions to determine accuracy of machine operation
  • Detects workpiece defects and machine malfunctions
  • Removes burrs, sharp edges, rust, and scale from workpiece
  • Performs minor machine maintenance such as oiling machines, die, or workpieces
  • Employees are responsible for complying with all requirements of Daifuku’s QMS policies and procedures.
  • Employees are to ensure sustainable process outputs that drive continuous improvement to provide leading industry performance and exceptional customer satisfaction.

Qualifications

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent preferred
  • Minimum 1 year of related experience preferred

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Requirements:

  • Ability to read blueprints
  • Knowledge of standard and metric measurements
  • Knowledge of quality assurance and self-inspection techniques
  • Self-motivated and detail-oriented
  • Team orientation
  • LOTO certification required
  • Crane operation certification required
  • Forklift operation experience preferred but not required
  • Availability to work on Saturdays as needed
  • Ability to read, write, speak, and understand the English language

ADA Requirements:

  • Medium work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Standing: Remaining upright on the feet, particularly for sustained periods of time.
  • Walking: Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
  • Pushing: Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward or outward.
  • Pulling: Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, drag, haul or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Lifting: Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to-position. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires the substantial use of the upper extremities and back muscles.
  • Grasping: Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Hearing: Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction, and having the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and making fine discriminations in sound.
  • Visual: The worker is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; extensive reading; visual inspection involving small defects, small parts, and/or operation of machines (including inspection); using measurement devices; and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.

title: Project Manager (Medicaid/Provider Management)
description:
Info-Matrix is seeking a proactive, execution-driven Project Manager to join our team in Harrisburg, PA!

In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end planning, coordination, execution, and monitoring of all interface and integration workstreams related to a Medicaid/MMIS Provider Management Module. You will serve as the pivotal operational bridge connecting client stakeholders, the PMM solution vendor, downstream module vendors, integration broker/API gateway teams, and PMO leadership.

The ideal candidate blends proven project management disciplines with a solid understanding of system integration lifecycles (APIs, batch exchanges, EDI, web services) within large-scale public sector health information systems.

Interface Lifecycle & Workstream Management

· End-to-End Coordination: Direct and monitor the planning, definition, development, end-to-end testing, and deployment of all inbound and outbound PMM interfaces (e.g., trading partner data exchanges, verification agencies, internal module integrations, and federal clearinghouses).

· Scope & Schedule Control: Build, maintain, and baseline detailed interface delivery schedules and work breakdown structures (WBS) aligned with the MMIS Integrated Master Schedule (IMS).

· Dependency & Critical Path Tracking: Proactively map cross-module interface dependencies, tracking technical prerequisite tasks between the PMM contractor, integration broker teams, and legacy/external data exchange partners.

· Milestone Delivery: Drive interface milestones from conceptual interface control documentation (ICD) through development, connectivity setup, system integration testing (SIT), user acceptance testing (UAT), and operational readiness review (ORR).

Stakeholder Liaison & Vendor Integration

· Vendor & Department Liaison: Serve as the primary project management point of contact for PMM interface matters, interfacing daily between Department leads, MMIS PMO leadership, and module vendor project teams.

· Facilitate Technical Working Groups: Organize, facilitate, and steer recurring Joint Interface Working Groups, technical walkthroughs, and Joint Application Development (JAD) sessions.

· CMS Certification Support: Coordinate documentation and testing evidence required for Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Outcomes-Based Certification (OBC) / Medicaid Enterprise Certification Toolkit (MECT) milestones tied to provider data exchange.

Governance, Risk & Issue Management

· Roadblock Identification & Resolution: Act as a proactive problem solver, identifying technical blockers, schedule slippages, and scope friction early; formulate and execute risk mitigation strategies and corrective action plans.

· Action Item & Change Control: Track and resolve all interface action items, defects, and change requests through formal Change Management Board (CMB) governance processes.

· Status Reporting & Executive Visibility: Deliver clear, data-driven status reporting, weekly dashboard metrics, burndown charts, and executive escalation briefs regarding interface health, milestones, and testing velocity.



Requirements

· Minimum Experience: At least four (4) years of structured IT project management experience leading multi-stakeholder system implementation, integration, or modernization projects.

· Required Certification: Active Project Management Professional (PMP®) certification in good standing (Project Management Institute).

· Healthcare / MMIS / State Government Domain: Demonstrable experience working on Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS), state Department of Human Services / Health agency projects, or comparable large-scale health information IT programs.

· Interface & Integration Familiarity: Direct experience coordinating system interfaces, APIs (REST/SOAP), EDI transactions, batch file transfers (SFTP), and enterprise data integration pipelines across disparate vendor platforms.

· SDLC Process Knowledge: Comprehensive understanding of the Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC), Agile/Scrum and Waterfall delivery models, and testing phases (Unit, SIT, UAT, Regression, Interface Mock Runs).

· Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science, Health Informatics, or a related discipline from an accredited college or university.

· Location & Presence: Preferred to be located in or willing to commute to Harrisburg, PA, with the ability to participate in scheduled on-site team meetings and client sessions. Will consider exceptional remote candidates.

Preferred Skills & Competencies

· Provider Module Expertise: Prior hands-on familiarity with Medicaid Provider Management / Provider Enrollment & Screening modules, Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) integrations, or National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) interfaces.

· Healthcare Interoperability Standards: Exposure to healthcare communication standards and frameworks (e.g., HIPAA EDI 274/837/835, HL7/FHIR, MITA 3.0 framework).

· Results-Driven Leadership: Demonstrated self-starter mindset with the ability to drive consensus across competing priorities among independent vendor organizations and state clients.

· Superior Communication: Outstanding oral and written presentation skills, with proven success conveying complex interface architecture timelines to non-technical executive stakeholders.

Tools & Technology

· Work Tracking & Backlog: Azure DevOps (ADO) / TFS for user story management, defect tracking, work item boards, and backlog grooming.

· Scheduling: Microsoft Project

· Productivity & Reporting: Microsoft Office Suite (Teams, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint) and business intelligence reporting (Power BI or Tableau dashboards).

Key Deliverables

· Detailed PMM Interface Master Work Plan and milestone schedule updates.

· Interface Traceability & Readiness Tracker (tracking ICD sign-offs, development completion, connectivity test logs, and end-to-end testing sign-offs).

· Weekly Interface Status Dashboards, risk registers, and critical path dependency analyses.

· Joint Interface Working Group agendas, detailed technical minutes, and closed-loop action item registers.

· Inputs to CMS Certification operational evidence artifacts for provider module data exchanges.

title: Developer – AI-Enabled Delivery
description:
At Mindbox we connect top IT talents with technology projects for leading enterprises across Europe.

Are you a Java Developer passionate about building secure, scalable microservices and eager to work in an innovative AI-enabled SDLC environment? This role combines hands-on engineering, cutting-edge GenAI practices, and strong controls to ensure quality, security, and compliance in an enterprise environment.

Sounds like your kind of challenge?

What you get in return
  • Flexible cooperation model

  • 4–8 years’ experience in software engineering with strong background in:

Desirable
